These measurements directly capture the sequential collapse of the layered MOF framework and the associated morphological evolution under controlled heating, decoupled from beam-induced effects during electron microscopy. Complementary ex-situ pyrolysis (700–1100 °C), together with high-resolution TEM, synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (X-PDF) analysis, and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), reveals the diffusion of Zn-containing species, ligand decomposition, and progressive graphitization within the amorphous matrix. We identify temperature-dependent stages involving ligand breakdown, migration of Zn–Nx species, followed by Zn loss, and ultimately forming porous N-doped carbon at 1000 °C that exhibits the strongest electrochemical response within this series. These findings establish temperature-dependent structure–property relationships that enable the thermal engineering of MOF-derived ORR catalysts.
n900c122acae3: Acute lung injury (ALI) is characterized by an uncontrolled cycle of inflammation and oxidative stress. However, conventional therapeutics are limited by physiological pulmonary barriers and poor targeted bioavailability. In this study, an inhalable multifunctional liposomal system (designated as R&I/Lip@PEG-M) was elaborately engineered to codeliver Resveratrol and IMD-0354 to disrupt the inflammation-oxidative stress cycle for ALI therapy. Upon nebulized inhalation, the negatively charged R&I/Lip@PEG-M liposomes would efficiently penetrate the mucus barrier, extensively accumulate in the pulmonary alveoli, and be specifically taken up by alveolar macrophages via mannose-mediated targeting recognition. Particularly, the internalized liposomes could exert combined therapeutic effects by scavenging intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and blocking the NF-κB signaling pathway to inhibit inflammation. In the LPS-induced ALI mouse model, the designed R&I/Lip@PEG-M significantly reduced the population of inflammatory macrophages, reprogrammed the redox microenvironment, and successfully mitigated lung damage and pulmonary edema.
n18e48ff0f97f: Two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offer tunable interlayer spacing and accessible surfaces that can overcome key limitations of conventional sodium-ion battery (SIBs) anodes. Here, we investigate Na+ storage mechanisms in three-layer 2D heterostructures composed of horizontally stacked graphene (G), nitrogen-doped graphene (NG), and MoS2 (M) by combining cyclic voltammetry with operando spectroelectrochemical Raman spectroscopy. Restricting the active thickness to three atomic layers enables direct spectroscopic access to interfacial charge transfer and strain during cycling. Electrochemical analysis reveals that Na+ storage is governed by two coupled factors: the permeability of the electrolyte-facing outer layer, and the electronic–mechanical interactions within the interlayer space. NG outer layers facilitate ion access and deliver up to 40-fold higher capacities than pristine graphene stacks, whereas MoS2 top layers suppress ion infiltration. Operando Raman correlates faradaic features with reversible structural changes, allowing separation of charge-doping and strain effects during cycling. The results demonstrate that Na+ storage proceeds predominantly via reversible accumulation in confined interlayer and blister-like reservoirs formed during solvent cointercalation. Incorporating MoS2 as a middle layer redistributes charge and buffers mechanical strain, enhancing cycling stability. These findings provide insights into charge storage mechanisms in 2D materials.
n344f6e871368: Optogenetics enables highly specific regulation of neuronal activity with exceptional spatiotemporal precision, providing powerful tools for neural circuit interrogation and the treatment of neurological disorders. However, the limited tissue penetration of visible light restricts its application to deep neural tissues. Near-infrared (NIR) neuromodulation has emerged as a promising alternative by leveraging the superior tissue penetration and minimal invasiveness of NIR light. Recent advances in NIR-responsive nanomaterials, optical engineering, and neurotechnology have rapidly transformed the field from nonspecific photobiomodulation to cell-specific nanotransducer-mediated neuromodulation and integrated neuromodulation systems. In this review, we summarize the optical principles governing NIR propagation in biological tissues and the mechanisms underlying NIR-mediated neural stimulation. We then discuss recent advances in representative NIR nanotransducers, including photothermal, optoelectric, photoacoustic, and NIR-to-visible upconversion platforms together with integrated neuromodulation systems that combine NIR stimulation with multimodal neural recording and closed-loop feedback. We further highlight emerging applications in the central nervous system, optic nerve, and peripheral nerve disorders. Finally, we discuss the key challenges toward clinical translation, including improving tissue penetration, cell specificity, biosafety, and translation, developing intelligent multidisciplinary neuromodulation platforms, and integrating artificial intelligence with closed-loop neural interfaces to achieve adaptive, precise, and personalized neuromodulation.
n81f9458e755a: Lanthanide-doped luminescent nanocrystals (NCs) hold significant promise for bioimaging, theranostics, catalysis, sensing, lighting, and displays, motivating an in-depth understanding of their optical properties. This work reveals the profound, yet widely disregarded, impact of surface structure changes on the luminescence of growing NCs through a model study of Eu3+ surface-exchanged Sr2YF7 NCs. Contrary to expectation, a stark drop in luminescence intensity exceeding several orders of magnitude was observed as the particle size increased. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy imaging shows that the NCs evolve from spheroidal to cuboidal morphologies during growth, with a shift in preferentially exposed crystal facets from {111} to {200} that renders lattice distortion less favorable. High-resolution optical spectroscopy probing surface Eu3+, together with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and reaction kinetics study, reveals a high extent of Eu3+ exchange in the small spheroidal NCs with lattice distortion extending far from the surface into the interior. This starkly contrasts the situation in the large cuboidal NCs, where the extent of Eu3+ residing in the surface region is severely limited, thereby causing the dramatic drop in luminescence. These findings demonstrate surface structure control as a powerful strategy for tailoring the luminescence properties of Ln3+-doped NCs and other nanomaterials for advanced applications.
nfbc81d758378: Intertwined electronic orders in low-dimensional quantum materials often evolve in a strongly thickness-dependent manner, yet direct spectroscopic access to their mutual evolution remains a key challenge. NbSe2 is a prototypical layered superconductor in which charge-density-wave order coexists with superconductivity, but spectroscopic signatures of the charge-density-wave state are frequently obscured, limiting direct comparison with superconducting order. Here, we demonstrate all-van der Waals planar tunnel junctions as a spectroscopic platform for simultaneously probing charge-density-wave and superconducting states in NbSe2 from the bulk to the bilayer limit. Temperature-dependent tunneling spectra reveal distinct anomalies associated with charge-density-wave formation and superconducting gap opening, allowing both quantum phase transitions to be tracked within the same device architecture. We find that the charge-density-wave transition temperature increases from ∼34 to ∼56 K as the NbSe2 thickness is reduced from 11L to the bilayer, while the superconducting transition temperature decreases from ∼7.2 to ∼5.4 K. These results reveal a clear anticorrelation between the two ordered states as dimensionality is reduced. Moreover, our spectroscopic studies reveal that the emergence of charge-density-wave order modifies the electronic states of NbSe2 over a broad energy window extending up to ±300 meV, a widely anticipated but previously experimentally inaccessible characteristic. Our results provide comprehensive spectroscopic evidence for the thickness-dependent competition between charge-density-wave order and superconductivity in ultrathin NbSe2 and position planar van der Waals tunnel junctions as a powerful platform for investigating emergent quantum phases in layered materials.
n035457817aae: Staphylococcus epidermidis is the leading cause of medical-implant-related infections. This pathogen attaches to medical implants coated in host fibrinogen via adhesin proteins. To resist high shear forces, adhesin-ligand rupture forces can exceed 2000 pN, a force that is much higher than streptavidin–biotin (150–300 pN). Yet, these adhesin-ligand complexes have a quite moderate KD (∼380 nM). This nanomechanics is explained, in part, by catch-bond behavior where adhesin-ligand lifetimes increase with force. Notably, prior reports of adhesin catch-bond mechanics at both low (3–30 pN) and high (1100–1400 pN) forces have lifetimes that are difficult to reconcile. Here, we combined constant-velocity and constant-force assays and thereby showed slip-bond behavior over six decades of lifetimes first for SdrG:Fgβ (1000–2400 pN) and then for SdrE:CFH (800–2200 pN) from Staphylococcus aureus. Individual lifetimes for SdrE:CFH exceeded 15 min at 800 pN. To investigate the thermodynamics of SdrG:Fgβ stability, we measured its lifetime using the constant-force assay as a function of both force (1000–1800 pN) and temperature (10–37 °C). Analysis yielded the enthalpic-dissociation barrier (ΔH‡ = 40 ± 4 kBT) and, assuming an enthalpy-dominated barrier, the dissociation attempt frequency (∼6 × 1010 s–1). Our results unambiguously demonstrate high-force slip-bond behavior for two different adhesin-ligand pairs and provide biophysical parameters governing the stability of key virulence factors.
ne01172f5198e: MRSA mastitis is clinically refractory and characterized by progressive inflammation driven by intracellular bacteria that form persistent niches in mammary epithelial cells and macrophages to evade antimicrobial clearance. Conventional antibiotics, particularly β-lactams, are widely used but suffer from poor intracellular accumulation, failing to reach these reservoirs. Even nanocarrier-based strategies struggle to achieve efficient endosomal escape and precise intracellular targeting. Herein, we report a fibronectin-functionalized, fluorinated PLGA nanoparticle encapsulating amoxicillin and sulbactam (Fn-F-PLGA@A/S) engineered with a 2.5% (w/w) fluorinated core for efficient endosomal escape. The fibronectin decoration enables sequential targeting of both host integrins and bacterial fibronectin-binding proteins (FnBPs). Fn-F-PLGA@A/S achieved efficient intracellular delivery, clearing 90% of intracellular MRSA in macrophages and epithelial cells within 4 h in vitro. To prolong mammary retention, Fn-F-PLGA@A/S was loaded into a thermosensitive hydrogel. In a murine MRSA mastitis model, a single intramammary dose of the gel formulation achieved >90% bacterial reduction, attenuated TNF-α and IL-6, and preserved alveolar architecture and tight junctions. Proteomic analysis revealed upregulation of AMPK-mediated autophagy, suggesting that beyond direct antibiotic action, the potent intracellular clearance achieved by Fn-F-PLGA may involve the engagement of host autophagic machinery, potentially facilitating the sequestration of MRSA within degradative compartments. Collectively, by integrating sequential targeting, sustained local retention, and autophagic engagement, this platform provides a robust strategy to address the key limitations of conventional antibiotics against intracellular pathogens in refractory infections.
ne1702d896a41: Lithium‐carbon dioxide (Li–CO2) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high‐energy storage with CO2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two‐electron conversion toward Li2C2O4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual‐atom Fe–N–Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N‐doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe1‐Mo1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe1‐Mo1/ICPs) to promote a reversible two‐electron Li2C2O4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N‐doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter‐site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe–N–Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor‐acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li2C2O4. Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li2C2O4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual‐atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.
n3855271dde3e: For wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskites, quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) surface reconstruction using bulky-cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium-based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low-dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic-spacer charge-state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs0.2FA0.8PbI1.8Br1.2 wide-bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N-methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge-neutralized ammonium–sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden–Popper-like quasi-2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap-mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide-ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO-treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO-treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS-L-1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge-neutralized organic spacer for quasi-2D surface reconstruction in wide-bandgap mixed-halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.
n8bc1da4da222: Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self‐assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene‐block‐poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time‐resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport‐mechanical‐morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self‐assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.
n672f68b9ba76: Biodegradable piezoelectric implants are optimal platforms for transient biosensing and therapeutics. However, limited piezoelectric properties and toughness impede the deployment of biodegradable piezoelectric implants in dynamic tissues and organs. In this study, we have developed silk fibroin (SF) fibers with high piezoelectricity and toughness via a microfluidic spinning method and post-treatment via dynamic salting-out (DSO). The optimized SF-DSO fibers exhibited remarkable mechanical properties (fracture strain: 45.58%, toughness: 115.03 MJ/m3) and enhanced piezoelectric performance (d 33, eff = 26.51 pC/N). Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and two-dimensional wide-angle X-ray scattering (2D-WAXS) analyses revealed increased β-sheet content and molecular alignment, correlating with improved properties. The fibers also showed excellent cytocompatibility and biodegradability, confirmed by in vitro and in vivo evaluations. Piezoelectric films based on SF-DSO fibers provided stable electrical outputs and were successfully used for in vivo applications, including respiratory monitoring, muscle motion detection, and ultrasound-driven energy harvesting in rats. The regenerated SF-DSO fibers prepared in this study offer a promising option for next-generation biodegradable piezoelectric implants.
n6222d0a4e8c7: Postoperative abdominal adhesion, characterized by its high prevalence, therapeutic intractability, and severe secondary complications, remains an intricate pathological condition following surgery. Here, using a peritoneal adhesion model integrated with multi‐omics analyses, we identify ROS‐driven activation of the cGAS–STING pathway as a central mechanism underlying macrophage activation and adhesion formation. To address this, black phosphorus nanosheets functionalized with Cu2+ and NH2–PEG–polyinosinic acid (BPNS@Cu@PI) are engineered as a peritoneal macrophage‐specific nanozyme to scavenge ROS. Furthermore, a silk fibroin‐based Janus hydrogel with an MMP‐responsive porous layer and a dense barrier layer (MMP‐JSF) is constructed to mitigate copper‐associated impairment of tissue repair. In vitro, this nano‐hydrogel system enables targeted delivery, redox regulation, mitochondrial homeostasis restoration, cGAS‐STING pathway inhibition, inflammation suppression, and wound healing promotion. In a 7‐day rat model, the BPNS@Cu@PI demonstrated significant efficacy in inhibiting adhesions, with the accompanying MMP‐JSF further enhancing therapeutic outcomes for tissue healing. Mechanistically, in a 3‐day model, the platform not only inhibited adhesions but also exhibited robust therapeutic effects in suppressing the ROS‐STING pathway and restoring mitochondrial function, as evidenced by both pathological and transcriptome analysis. Collectively, this work establishes a pathway‐specific nano–hydrogel strategy for adhesion‐free healing with translational potential.
n205580412cf2: Efficient solar‐driven interfacial evaporation requires precise coordination of heat and mass transport, yet achieving such synergy within conventional molecular systems remains challenging. Here, we address this limitation using an atomically precise polyoxoniobate (PONb)‐based molecular heterojunction, [Te5Cu0.2Nb15O57H5.6][(CuL)7(OH)]·21H2O (PONb‐CuL, L = 2,2′‐bipyridine), in which hydrophilic PONb clusters are covalently integrated with photothermal organocopper CuL units. This Janus molecular architecture couples broadband solar absorption with interfacial water‐cluster regulation within a single framework. Under one‐sun irradiation, a two‐dimensional PONb‐CuL evaporator delivers an evaporation rate of 2.87 kg m−2 h−1. Incorporation into a three‐dimensional aerogel architecture further boosts the evaporation rate to 5.34 kg m−2 h−1, affording a freshwater yield of 29.25 L m−2 under outdoor operation. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the PONb domain promotes hydrogen‐bonded water‐cluster formation, whereas the organocopper domain reduces the energy barrier for interfacial water transport and vapor escape. This work introduces polyoxometalate‐based molecular heterojunction engineering as a strategy for orchestrating coupled heat and mass transport, offering critical insights into the rational design of efficient solar‐to‐vapor conversion systems.
nfb5d1875ce7e: Here, we develop a redox‐responsive nano‐immune coupling strategy for synergistic control of tomato bacterial wilt. The CuO@MON nanocomposite consists of copper oxide nanoparticles embedded within glutathione‐responsive mesoporous organosilica (MON), enabling selective disassembly in the thiol‐rich bacterial microenvironment. Under in vitro conditions, Ralstonia solanacearum was treated with CuO@MON at concentrations ranging from 0 to 500 mg/L for 24 h, with CuO, MON, and zhongshengmycin as controls. CuO@MON exhibited concentration‐dependent antibacterial activity and higher efficacy than CuO alone, with an EC50 value of 96.96 mg/L. Mechanistic analyses showed that CuO@MON enhanced intracellular ROS generation (2.054 ± 0.098‐fold increase), promoted glutathione depletion, and induced membrane damage and genomic DNA degradation in R. solanacearum. In tomato plants, CuO@MON treatment (250 mg/L) reduced stem colonization by R. solanacearum by 84.0% after 4 days of inoculation compared with infected controls, while zhongshengmycin achieved a 94.9% reduction as a conventional positive control. Moreover, CuO@MON enhanced defense‐related responses, increasing PR‐1 expression from 400 ± 96‐fold to 533 ± 140‐fold and PR‐5 expression from 340 ± 50‐fold to 807 ± 121‐fold relative to healthy controls. Collectively, CuO@MON integrates pathogen suppression with host defense activation, providing a nano‐immune coupling strategy for sustainable bacterial disease management.
nbb6bdeb9fd43: Aqueous Zn batteries are promising for safe and low‐cost large‐scale energy storage, yet their practical deployment is hindered by severe Zn anode instability arising from coupled hydrogen evolution, corrosion, and dendritic electrodeposition, particularly under temperature extremes. Here we report a solvation–interphase coupled strategy enabled by a hydrated eutectic electrolyte formulated from zinc trifluoromethanesulfonate (Zn(OTf)2), ethylene glycol (EG), and an SnF2 additive (optimized as ZOTF‐16/SF30), which delivers stable Zn electrochemistry over an exceptionally wide temperature window from −40°C to 60°C. Spectroscopic and physicochemical analyses reveal that EG confines H2O within a reinforced hydrogen‐bond network and reconstructs the Zn2+ coordination environment, thereby suppressing active‐water reactivity and mitigating hydrogen evolution and corrosion. Concurrently, SnF2 programs interfacial chemistry to generate an in situ zincophobic/zincophilic bilayer interphase, wherein the zincophobic component blocks water penetration and parasitic reactions while the zincophilic component homogenizes Zn2+ flux and nucleation, enforcing uniform Zn deposition and dendrite‐free growth. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells exhibit ultrastable cycling for over 2400 h at 1 mA cm−2. Moreover, Zn||I2 full cells deliver remarkable long‐term durability over 120 000 cycles, sustaining extended lifetimes at 60°C and −40°C. This work establishes a practical electrolyte‐interphase co‐design blueprint for climate‐resilient aqueous Zn batteries, highlighting hydrated eutectic chemistry as a versatile platform for stabilizing reactive metal anodes.
n25b946637e70: The nervous system is emerging as a central regulator of tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic response. However, the dynamic mechanisms linking neural activity to malignant, immune, and barrier states remain difficult to dissect in vivo. Animal models capture key aspects of cancer neuroscience, but poorly control human‐specific multicellular interfaces, neural activity, secreted signals, and real‐time readouts. AI‐enabled organoid chip platforms offer a complementary route to reconstruct and interrogate the nerve‐tumor interface by integrating human‐derived organoids, microfluidic control, sensing, and computational modeling. Here we review advances in nerve‐tumor organoids and integrate relevant progress in microfluidics, in situ functional sensing, and AI‐driven modeling. These systems can enable controlled studies of perineural invasion, nerve‐mediated immune regulation, trans‐barrier drug responses, and longitudinal functional states. Key challenges include model standardization, long‐term stability, multimodal data interpretation, and clinical translation. AI‐enabled organoid chip platforms could help shift cancer neuroscience from descriptive observation towards perturbable, human‐relevant and data‐rich systems for mechanism discovery and precision therapy assessment.
nb033f0a65dfd: Ru has been investigated as a promissing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalyst in anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). However, its excessive oxophilicity blocks active sites and over-structures interfacial water, limiting alkaline HER kinetics. In this work, we report a Ru-RuO2−δ heterostructure that overcomes these kinetic bottlenecks via an engineered interface-to-surface proton transfer relay. This architecture promotes a more flexible interfacial water network that facilitates Grotthuss-type proton transport, coupled with facilitated hydrogen spillover from high-affinity Ru clusters to low-affinity RuO2−δ surfaces. By decoupling proton delivery from surface binding, the Ru-RuO2−δ achieves an intrinsic activity 26-fold higher than pristine Ru, requiring ultra-low overpotentials of only 15 ± 4 and 165 ± 6 mV at 10 and 1000 mA cm−2, respectively. Notably, the catalyst demonstrates long-term durability under high-current-density operation (> 470 h at 1 A cm−2) with a degradation rate 2,000-fold lower than commercial Pt/C. In a practical AEMWE, it delivers 1 A cm−2 at a cell voltage of 1.67 ± 0.02 V (45.1 ± 0.5 kWh kgH2 −1), meeting the U.S. DOE energy-consumption target. Beyond providing a high-performance alternative to platinum, this work introduces a design principle for accelerating electrocatalytic kinetics through the engineering of interface-to-surface transport relays.
nc79a5c8ccf40: With the rapid evolution of flexible electronics and biomedical systems, stimuli‐responsive smart fibers have emerged as important functional materials. Electrospinning serves as a versatile fabrication route for micro/nanofibers, enabling tunable fiber morphologies, high porosity, and large specific surface areas to regulate the structure–property relationships of stimuli‐responsive smart fibers. This review systematically summarizes the fundamentals, structural design strategies, fabrication technologies, and applications of electrospun stimuli‐responsive smart fibers. The response mechanisms underlying seven typical stimuli, including temperature, light, pH, humidity, force, magnetism, and electricity, are first discussed. Subsequently, material selection, electrospinning strategies, and structural design approaches are discussed, highlighting how architecture and interfacial regulation govern response speed, sensitivity, and cycling stability. Furthermore, recent advances in five core application domains, including optical responses, wettability switching, shape‐morphing actuation, energy harvesting/storage, and signal transduction, are summarized. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are discussed, with emphasis on multi‐stimulus coupling, artificial intelligence (AI)‐assisted fabrication, and green scalable production. Overall, this review provides comprehensive theoretical guidance for the development and industrial translation of high‐performance intelligent fiber materials.
nc2cfe1c35a7d: Ionic thermogalvanic hydrogels with high ionic thermopower are promising for wearable power supply. However, due to the presence of solid network, their ionic conductivities are still low, limiting their power densities. Herein, a facile and effective enhancement strategy on ionic conductivities and thus ionic thermoelectric properties of PVA(poly(vinyl alcohol))/CMC(carboxymethyl cellulose) hydrogels is proposed through antisolvent engineering. An antisolvent (ethanol) of PVA is introduced into PVA/CMC precursor solution prior to the hydrogel formation, which can change the conformation of PVA and CMC molecular chains as well as hydrogen bond network of prepared hydrogel. It can decrease PVA crystalline domains, and present higher water content and more sub-micron porous structure through freeze-thaw cycles to form stretchable and transparent hydrogel with faster ionic transport. This PVA/CMC hydrogel with antisolvent engineering presents the high ionic conductivity of 57.9 mS cm−1 and elongation at beak of 256%, which are 3.75 and 1.8 times higher than pristine hydrogel, respectively. This boosts its Pmax /∆T2 to a high value of 0.67 mW m−2 K−2, higher than that of most PVA hydrogels. During this configuration with 27 hydrogels, it can output a high voltage of 718.1 mV under 10 K temperature difference, which is potential for wearable power supply.
n6125e6bc27d7: Vertically aligned nanocomposites (VANs) are self‐assembled thin‐film architectures in which phase distribution, interfacial density, and strain fields are defined concurrently during growth. Nanoscale vertical alignment and coherent interfaces generate anisotropic confinement and directional connectivity, thereby modifying ionic, electronic, optical, and magnetic responses across oxide, oxide‐metal, oxide‐nitride, and oxide‐alloy systems. This review examines how growth kinetics, elastic mismatch, and interfacial energetics control pillar morphology, defect distribution, and transport anisotropy in VAN platforms. Studies spanning electrochemical electrodes, dielectric materials, and magneto‐optical systems demonstrate enhanced oxygen exchange kinetics, anisotropic permittivity, strain‐stabilized phases, and coupled magnetic–optical behavior arising from architectural control. By correlating structural parameters with functional outputs, the literature establishes VANs as a versatile strategy for engineering coupled phenomena in complex oxides. Emerging design guidelines and open challenges are discussed to outline future directions for energy conversion and nanoelectronic applications.
n5adaedef4129: Molten silicates can be immobilized by protective reaction products or continue to penetrate oxide ceramics, but the structural features that distinguish these pathways remain unclear. Here we examine CMAS reactions with RETa3O9 and connect crystallographic cation partitioning in corrosion products with passivation across rare‐earth chemistry, melt composition, and multicomponent design. EuTa3O9 forms a durable bilayer comprising a dense AX2O6 barrier and a cation‐sequestering B2Y2O7 layer; a related consumption–barrier architecture persists in Fe‐rich lunar‐ and Martian‐regolith analogue melts. Across 11 RETa3O9 compositions, rare‐earth size acts as a structural descriptor for access to AX2O6‐, B2Y2O7‐, and CZO4‐containing reaction pathways. Using this relationship as a design constraint, Eu‐centred high‐entropy RETa3O9 compositions retain resistance to bulk penetration while reducing thermal conductivity. HEC‐2 forms an 84.4 µm reaction layer after 100 h at 1300°C and exhibits an 8.3% lower calculated effective thermal conductivity than EuTa3O9 at 1200°C. These results link reaction‐product chemistry to mechanism‐constrained composition design for high‐temperature protective ceramics.
ne7360b5761db: The directional anchoring of heteroatoms into a high‐entropy oxides (HEOs) platform offers substantial scientific and technological promise, yet achieving atomic‐level control over such doping remains challenging and rarely demonstrated. Here, we precisely anchor B atoms into an HEO framework (BS‐HEO), possessing a distinct O‐Mn‐B coordination unit in which Mn acts as an electronic hub that triggers an electron‐siphoning effect, thereby redistributing the interfacial electron configuration. Theory and experiments confirm that the electron‐reconstructed surface enables the optimization of the balance between intrinsic activity and adsorption toward 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (5‐HMF) within the potential window (1.40–1.45 V vs. RHE), consequently enhancing interfacial mass transport efficiency. As a result, when the carbon balance is taken into consideration, the BS‐HEO catalyst delivers impressive HMFOR performance at 1.42 V versus RHE, achieving 96.0% selectivity for 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and 99.1% faradaic efficiency (F.E.), which surpasses most previously reported benchmarks. This work not only demonstrates precise B anchoring into a HEO but also introduces a new strategy for tailoring and identifying active sites in high‐entropy materials for high‐performance electrosynthesis.
na95787a82ebf: Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic platforms, yet their nonvolatile operation is fundamentally limited by rapid ion back‐diffusion governed by interfacial ion relaxation at the electrolyte–semiconductor boundary. Channel‐level optimization alone cannot prevent post‐bias ion relaxation driven by concentration gradients in the electrolyte. In this context, polymer additives offer an effective route to regulate interfacial ion transport without modifying the semiconductor channel. Here, bio‐derived sodium alginate is incorporated into a Na–TFSI electrolyte to reconstruct the electrolyte/channel interface and modulate ion redistribution. The resulting interfacial ion‐trapping barrier suppresses back‐diffusion and prolongs relaxation times of doped ions. This electrolyte‐level control markedly enhances synaptic retention and improves linearity and dynamic range in long‐term potentiation/depression (LTP/D) characteristics. These findings establish interfacial ion regulation at the electrolyte level as a decisive design principle for organic neuromorphic systems and highlight naturally derived polyelectrolytes as promising additives for stable synaptic operation.
n95af98ecf334: Neuromorphic Computing In the Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77301), Eunho Lee and co‐workers present a bio‐derived interfacial network strategy for organic electrochemical synaptic transistors. The bio‐ polymer network effectively suppresses TFSI− anion back‐diffusion from the channel into the electrolyte after bias removal, stabilizing the electrochemically doped state. This prolonged interfacial ion retention enables highly persistent nonvolatile synaptic memory, establishing bio‐based polymer networks as a powerful design tool for advanced neuromorphic electronics.
nc31643c5e0dc: Spatially resolved electroluminescent (EL) textiles are highly desirable for flexible hazard detection, yet conventional systems limit real‐time localization of dynamic stimuli. Inspired by insect olfaction, where spatial information emerges from distributed sensing and spatiotemporal signal differences, we report a cellulose‐based EL sensing textile for real‐time gas leak localization via material‐architecture‐governed spatial encoding. Plant‐derived cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) serve as fundamental building blocks, organizing functional components through blending or surface modification and being assembled via wet‐spinning into continuous fibers with hierarchical porosity, flexibility, and volumetric stimulus accessibility essential for rapid gas sensing. Conductive fibers are fabricated through in situ polymerization of polyaniline (PANI) on CNF surfaces, enabling reversible, gas‐responsive electrical modulation with detection limits of 1 ppm for HCl and 3.6 ppm for NH3. Coaxial electroluminescent fibers comprising a PANI@CNF conductive core and ZnS‐embedded CNF shell provide stable light emission over 100 h of continuous operation. Intersections between these fibers form self‐defined units that translate localized gas exposure into spatiotemporally resolved EL patterns, mapping propagation pathways with a naked‐eye detection threshold of 100 ppm, while maintaining stable emission after washing and bending. This work establishes a bio‐inspired, architecture‐driven strategy for smart textiles, highlighting cellulose‐based nanocomposites as key components for next‐generation smart technologies.
n854e99aa4b8e: Dielectric capacitors with excellent energy-storage performance are highly desirable for next-generation advanced high/pulsed power capacitors that require miniaturization and integration. However, the low energy-storage density arising from insufficient breakdown strength (BDS), inadequate maximum polarization (P max), and large remanent polarization (P r), remains a critical challenge for the practical application of dielectric capacitors. Herein, we propose a strategy to synergistically incorporate the M2-M3 two-phase coexistence and low-atomic-displacement (LAD) region into the AgNbO3 system, thereby achieving high BDS, large P max and extremely low P r simultaneously. Ultrahigh U rec ∼ 17.1 J·cm−3, excellent η ∼ 89% are achieved in the (Ag1-3 x Eu x )(Nb0.7Ta0.3)O3 (Eu x ANT) multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) at x = 0.03, representing a breakthrough in the overall energy-storage performance of lead-free antiferroelectric (AFE) capacitors. This study not only develops a promising high-performance lead-free energy-storage dielectric, but also offers a novel microstructural design strategy for the synergistic optimization of multiple energy-storage parameters to improve the energy storage performance of AFE system.
n9bd0973f3338: Uncontrolled dendrite growth during zinc plating/stripping hinders the practical application of aqueous zinc metal batteries in energy storage systems. In this study, the classical diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) theory was employed to understand the mechanisms of zinc dendritic growth fundamentally and then to guide the design of interfacial structure-directing engineering. [EMIm]EtSO4 ionic liquid as a structure-directing agent was developed to successfully overcome the disordered Zn dendrite growth following the rules of “random motion” and “contact-stick”. Comprehensive characterizations suggest that EMIm+ cations guide the interfacial ordering process by building a buffer layer and a hydrophobic barrier on the Zn anode, while EtSO4 − anions orchestrate the reconstruction of the Zn2+ solvation structure. This synergistic regulation transforms zinc deposition morphology from stochastic fractal growth to highly ordered epitaxial growth. As a result, the zinc anode achieves 99.3% Coulombic efficiency at 1 mA cm−2 and stable cycling over 2000 h. It further endows the Zn||NVO battery with significantly improved stability and anti freezing performance (−40°C). This work demonstrates an interfacial engineering strategy that effectively suppresses DLA-type dendritic growth, providing a new perspective for high-performance aqueous zinc batteries.
n780ce3f51a50: Electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction (ECO2R) into value‐added chemicals is challenging due to the high overpotential of reaction intermediates, the instability of adsorbed species in the absence of mobile cations, and requiring acidic aqueous electrolyte feed to prevent salt precipitation. A gas‐fed, zero‐gap proton exchange membrane (PEM) ECO2R setup utilizing hydrogen (H2) as anodic feed and nitrogen‐doped carbon‐supported cobalt nanoparticles (Co/N‐C) as catalyst may be a solution to these problems but is observed to be ineffective at suppressing the H2 evolution reaction (HER). Immobilizing poly‐diallyldimethyl ammonium (PDDA+) cations with finely milled Co/N‐C results in a change of selectivity from HER toward coordinating CO2 intermediates on active sites. Optimizing Co loading at 1.20 wt.% for Co/N‐C delivers a peak faradaic efficiency toward carbon monoxide production (FECO) of 65% and sustains 5 h electrolysis with FECO above 50% under a constant current density of 100 mA cm−2. The effects of acid‐wash, cobalt content, mass loading, and PDDA+ on the gas‐diffusion electrode and secondary particle size in catalyst ink are optimized to improve FECO against a prohibitively low pH environment. These results highlight the intrinsic properties of PDDA+ on Co/N‐C electrocatalyst for a modular, humidified gas‐fed, zero‐gap PEM CO2 electrolyzer technology.
n3fe4eaeba590: A major challenge in auricular reconstruction is the endochondral ossification of engineered cartilage after subcutaneous implantation. To overcome this, we developed a functionally tailored, hybrid hydrogel scaffold that integrates anti‐angiogenic therapy with biomimetic architecture to stabilize the chondrogenic phenotype. The core consists of a DLP‐printed, bevacizumab‐eluting pNAGA‐GT hydrogel framework with 200‐µm resolution, exhibiting a compressive modulus of 5.35 MPa and a tensile modulus of 0.34 MPa, providing robust mechanical support. Sustained bevacizumab release suppresses local angiogenic activity and is accompanied by increased TIMP3 and reduced MMP9/MMP13 expression, thereby contributing to cartilage matrix preservation and reduced ossification. Encapsulating this core, a visible‐light–crosslinked GelMA‐Tyr hydrogel creates a soft (∼15 kPa), degradable (60‐day) microenvironment that spatially organizes chondrocytes and perichondrium‐derived stem/progenitor cells (PSPCs) into a cartilage‐mimetic construct, thereby preserving cell viability and chondrogenic function. This dual‐phase design enables the generation of stable, multilayered ectopic cartilage, offering a clinically translatable strategy for microtia reconstruction.
nc20e23edc3ad: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers decentralised freshwater production with concurrent electricity generation, yet capillary-driven water supply imposes a kinetic ceiling in high-flux or high-salinity conditions, where boundary-layer buildup drives salt accumulation and performance decay. Here we establish a dual-driving transport regime that couples capillary flow with chemically induced Marangoni convection in low-tortuosity, vertically aligned channels. A longitudinal gradient of oxygen-containing functional groups, introduced into a graphene-oxide aerogel by thermal-gradient reduction, generates a persistent surface-tension disparity that sustains Marangoni microcirculation, continuously refreshing the evaporation interface by displacing concentrated boundary layers into the bulk. A miniaturised evaporator achieves 540 kg m− 3 h− 1 (2.7 kg m− 2 h− 1) in 20 wt% NaCl under 1-sun illumination, sustaining stable operation for 12 h without observable salt accumulation, while simultaneously delivering a short-circuit current of 25 µA and an open-circuit voltage of 0.7 V. Series-integrated devices directly power an LED. These results demonstrate that chemical-gradient programming can recruit Marangoni convection as a robust co-driver to surpass capillary-limited transport, offering a generalizable strategy for high-flux brine desalination with concurrent energy harvesting.
n733d6dfd46c2: Aqueous lithium‐ion batteries (ALIBs) stand out as promising grid‐scale energy storage candidates, leveraging aqueous electrolytes to address the safety hazards and environmental concerns of traditional nonaqueous batteries. Their development, however, has long been constrained by the narrow electrochemical stability window of water, which limits cell voltage and promotes parasitic reactions. This review summarizes recent progress in ALIBs from the synergistic perspectives of electrolyte regulation, interfacial reaction mechanisms, and cell‐level engineering considerations in relation to practical metrics, including energy density and long‐term cycling durability. Particular emphasis is placed on the control of Li+ solvation environments and the formation of functional interphases, which collectively suppress water‐induced side reactions and expand the accessible operating window. By integrating these tightly linked aspects, this review delineates the mechanistic foundations and design principles that redefine the effective stability boundary of aqueous batteries and support the continued evolution of ALIBs toward scalable, high‐energy, and durable technologies.
n7e08cfd56c1d: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) combines imaging and spectroscopy for diverse applications in agriculture, industry, and medicine. However, current broadband and visible light based HSI systems suffer from limited spectral range, poor environment‐resistant capabilities and severe emission overlap. Here, we propose a innovative HSI approach based on narrow‐band near‐infrared (NIR, 900–1700 nm) rare‐earth luminescent materials. First, through concentration triggered multi‐site synergistic sensitization strategy, we developed high‐efficiency narrow‐band NIR emitters, LaZnGa11O19:Cr,RE$\text{Cr,RE}$ (RE = Yb, Er, Nd, Tm and Ho), achieving FWHM of 28 nm and 50% external quantum efficiency. Subsequently, we integrated as‐developed emitters with HSI technology to construct a novel narrow‐band NIR‐enhanced HSI system. Compared to wide‐band emitters, its theoretical signal isolation in dual‐channel mode significantly improved from 1.84 dB and 0.14 dB to 14.62 dB and 9.08 dB, effectively extending the spectral range of imaging systems while avoiding signal crosstalk between multiple wavelength signals. Furthermore, when applied to real‐world image information scenarios, the as‐constructed system achieves isolation of 11.8 dB (channel to background) and 10.2 dB (channel‐to‐channel) close to theoretical values, demonstrating the feasibility of narrow‐band NIR‐enhanced HSI approach. These results provide unique ideas and inspirations for the design of high‐performance NIR luminescent materials as well as advanced imaging applications.
n7bbd52f76994: Precise and crosstalk‐free discrimination of pressure and temperature remains a fundamental challenge in artificial sensory systems due to the intrinsic coupling of mechanical and thermal transduction. Herein, we present a flexible, high‐fidelity dual‐modal sensor based on an ultralight hierarchically porous conductive sponge. The engineered porous architecture synergistically integrates piezoresistive and thermoelectric effects within a single carbon nanomaterial, achieving physical decoupling between resistance‐type pressure signals and voltage‐type temperature outputs, effectively suppressing dual‐modal interference. Owing to its compressibility, conductive network, and thermal insulation, the sensor delivers a pressure sensitivity of 4.43 kPa−1, a detection limit of 25 Pa, a response time of 91 ms, and durability over 20 000 cycles, alongside a Seebeck coefficient of 9.96 µV K−1 and a temperature resolution of 0.5 K. As a proof of concept, it enables real‐time Morse code communication and physiological monitoring. Moreover, a 3 × 3 sensor array integrated with machine learning demonstrates robust tactile‐thermal fusion perception, highlighting its potential as a multifunctional sensing platform. This work presents a material‐driven strategy to overcome multimodal signal interference, significantly promoting sensory perception in complex environments.
n6cc3081da8a9: Fast‐charging lithium (Li)‐ion batteries (LIBs) require electrolytes enabling rapid ion transport and desolvation. Conventional solvents strongly coordinate with lithium ions (Li+), leading to high desolvation energy barriers and organic‐rich interphases limiting rate capability. Here, we propose a descriptor‐guided strategy for designing decoupling electrolytes to overcome sluggish Li+ desolvation and poor interphase transport kinetics, enabling fast‐charging LIBs. A solvent screening descriptor (decoupling coefficient (Dc)) is introduced based on the ratio of molecular volume to Li+ affinity, which captures solvent electronic and steric effects. Among evaluated solvents, propyl acetate (PA), possessing a high Dc, is identified as a suitable solvent to formulate decoupling electrolytes, which lowers the desolvation energy barrier, promotes anion participation, and fosters an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Consequently, the PA‐based decoupling electrolytes enable exceptional fast‐charging LIBs. Li||graphite (Gr) cells deliver a capacity of 190.1 mA h g−1 at 6 C with 80% capacity retention after 2000 cycles. Furthermore, industrial‐scale 5‐Ah Gr||LiFePO4 pouch cells, with a high cathode mass loading of 34 mg cm−2, achieve an initial capacity of 4.29 Ah and retain 70% capacity over 600 cycles at 2 C. Even at 4 C, an impressive capacity of 4 Ah (138.9 Wh kg−1) can also be achieved.
n70dcee1006b5: Successful integration of silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) towards highly selective electrochemical CO2 reduction to carbon monoxide (CO) is often hindered by size‐dependent selectivity trade‐offs in Ag NPs and by inefficient full‐cell operation. Here, we systematically investigate ligand‐mediated colloidal synthesis of (quasi) monodisperse Ag NPs (6–15 nm) and evaluate them in a gas‐diffusion‐electrode‐based flow‐cell architecture, revealing a pronounced size‐dependent activity volcano. By incorporating a non‐catalytic carbon support, we demonstrate that an optimized Ag‐to‐carbon (Ag/C) loading, specifically 20% with 10 nm Ag NPs, achieves nearly 100% Faradaic Efficiency (FE) for CO at −100 mA·cm−2, significantly outperforming other particle sizes and a commercial Ag catalyst at similar loadings. In situ Raman spectroscopy reveals a substantial role of Ag/C interactions in enhancing the affinity toward the *COOH intermediates, thereby promoting high CO2‐to‐CO selectivity. Post‐electrolysis, X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) further indicates the electronic and chemical structural stability of the optimized Ag/C, which retains the metallic Ag0 state. Finally, we demonstrate the bifunctional nature of Ag/C electrodes by pairing CO2 and formaldehyde electrolysis, enabling simultaneous CO generation at the cathode and formate (HCOO−) with hydrogen (H2) at the anode at reduced cell potentials. This work highlights an energy‐efficient paired electrosynthesis strategy supporting the progress toward a circular carbon economy.
n44dccd727d1c: Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation technology offers a groundbreaking approach to water treatment. However, the relentless pursuit of high energy efficiency has encountered a bottleneck in vapor generation, necessitating consideration of vapor diffusion. To tackle these limitations, this work establishes a comprehensive liquid‐liquid‐vapor transport kinetics framework, which couples water transport, vapor generation, vapor diffusion, and thermal management. This system optimizes water transport while minimizing thermal losses by tailoring the pore architecture. More importantly, we design dedicated convection windows for activating internal self‐generation convection to accelerate vapor dissipation. This system delivered a superior evaporation rate of 4.93 kg m−2 h−1, exceeding the conventional designs (2.9 kg m−2 h−1) while achieving energy efficiency of 89.6% (considering both environmental heat gain and convective heat gain). This enhancement stems from the efficient vapor generation and release process, driven by the synergistic interplay of water transport, thermal management, and convection control. Outdoor experiments demonstrate that the optimized array system achieves a water production rate of approximately 1.95 kg m−2 h−1 without any detectable contamination. This illustrates that this strategy can be used for maximizing the performance of 3D evaporators.
n852d9822e345: Electronic skins (e‐skins) generally transduce contact mechanics but cannot interrogate materials concealed by packaging, limiting robotic perception to accessible surfaces. A multimodal cross‐medium e‐skin is developed by co‐designing a five‐channel piezoresistive network and a conformal surface‐plasmon (CSP) waveguide within a shared flexible interdigitated‐electrode architecture. The piezoresistive channel maps grasp pressure over 0–140 kPa with response and recovery times below 50 ms, whereas the CSP channel confines microwaves to a subwavelength near field for phase‐based pre‐touch sensing and frequency‐resolved electromagnetic fingerprinting. Strong field localization preserves transmission fingerprints under bending and twisting up to 80° and enables interrogation through glass, plastic, and paper containers. Coupled with a support vector machine, these fingerprints discriminate 16 sample classes with 99.4% test accuracy and 99.7% leave‐one‐out cross‐validation accuracy. When integrated with a dexterous robotic hand, the platform unifies grasp‐pressure mapping, proximity perception, and nondestructive recognition of hidden contents. This shared‐architecture strategy transforms conformal plasmonic waveguides into deformation‐tolerant functional sensing interfaces and extends e‐skin beyond contact‐limited tactile sensing toward cross‐medium robotic perception.
nc8cb108749db: Molecular memristors have shown great potential for digital memory and analog computing applications. However, developing molecular active layers with controllable structures and stable electrical properties remains challenging. Here, we employ a triphenylamine centered three armed terpyridine ligand (TPA‐(TPy)3) to construct a two‐dimensional (2D) iron based metal–organic network (Fe‐MON) film through interfacial coordination assembly. The three‐armed molecular topology promotes lateral network growth, enabling the formation of continuous and robust Fe‐MON films. In contrast, the structurally analogous two‐armed ligand (TPA‐(TPy)2) fails to generate continuous networks, resulting in inferior device stability. The resulting Al/Fe‐MON/ITO memristors exhibit reliable digital resistive switching characteristics with narrow ON/OFF voltage distributions, good retention, and endurance. Moreover, the synergistic redox activity of triphenylamine and Fe2+/Fe3+ centers enables continuous conductance modulation under pulse stimulation, achieving 64 distinguishable multilevel conductance states. By integrating these conductance states into a convolutional neural network (CNN), the system achieves 96.57% accuracy in flower image recognition. This work demonstrates the capability of 2D metal–organic network films for digital‐analog dual‐mode memristors.
n86c41dfa6c5d: Efficient and selective CO2 conversion under mild conditions remains challenging because rapid interfacial charge recombination and poorly controlled carbon‐conversion pathways often limit both catalytic activity and product selectivity. Here, we report a Pt/Cu2O@BaTiO3 (Pt/Cu2O@BTO) dual‐site heterostructure in which Pt and Cu2O are spatially separated on piezoelectric BaTiO3 nanorods to establish differentiated interfaces for CO2 reduction and H2O oxidation. Under coupled mechanical stimulation and light irradiation, stress‐induced piezoelectric polarization synergistically enhances interfacial charge separation while promoting CO2 adsorption and activation at Pt‐related reduction sites. Benefiting from the piezo‐photocatalytic coupling, Pt/Cu2O@BTO achieved a CO production rate of 146.7 µmol g−1 h−1 and a CO selectivity of 95.8%. In situ FTIR spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that the dynamic piezoelectric polarization not only accelerates charge transport and CO2 activation, but also redirects the subsequent evolution of key *CO intermediates by making CO desorption more competitive than further hydrogenation. This work demonstrates that dynamic interfacial polarization can simultaneously regulate charge‐transfer behavior and reaction pathways in CO2 reduction, providing a strategy for selective carbon conversion in multi‐field catalytic systems.
n8445dfb3f489: Interfacial instability remains the major barrier for practical aqueous zinc batteries. Conventional electrolyte design mainly focuses on reducing water coordination number in the Zn2+ solvation shell. However, this static criterion often neglects ligand‐exchange kinetics and can still leave highly reactive water at the interface. Herein, we propose a dynamic solvation perturbation (DSP) strategy to regulate Zn2+ solvation through transient solvent coordination. Descriptor‐guided screening identifies methyl acetate (MA) as an optimal modulator with balanced Zn2+ coordination and water regulation. MA forms a fast‐exchange mixed solvation sheath, shortens water residence time, and passivates residual water via dynamic solvation‐shell rearrangement. Additionally, MA exhibits facet‐selective adsorption on Zn anode, which suppresses direct water attack and promotes uniform Zn nucleation. As a result, the DSP‐regulated electrolyte enables the Zn anode to achieve long‑term cycling life over 8000 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2. Remarkably, stable cycling is maintained for more than 2000 h at 32% DOD and more than 1000 h at 80% DOD. In addition, the Zn||V2O5 pouch‐cell with the MA‐containing electrolyte exhibits approximately 80% capacity retention over 300 cycles at 0.1 A g−1, highlighting its potential for practical applications.
nb773bbebe043: Electrochemical direct lithium extraction emerges as a promising route toward sustainable lithium supply, yet pervasive interference from Na+ and Mg2+ incurs formidable kinetic barriers. Herein, we construct field‐responsive H1.6Mn1.6O4@poly (3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene)‐polystyrenesulfonate (HMO@PEDOT:PSS) sulfonate interfaces and establish a dynamic ion sieving mechanism for selective lithium recovery. Synergistically integrated conductive PEDOT framework and sulfonate functional moieties endow the heterointerfaces with instantaneous electric field‐triggered responsiveness. The field‐sensitive‐sulfonate sites dynamically regulate interfacial cation affinity, enabling prominent selective separation of Li+ against Na+ and Mg2+ in harsh brine media. Profiting from real‐time interfacial modulation, the as‐fabricated electrode achieves superior lithium extraction performance and drastically enhanced magnesium rejection, having an exceptional separation factor αMgLi$\alpha _{Mg}^{Li}$ of 458.9 while preserving a high αNaLi$\alpha _{Na}^{Li}$ of 1069.4. Alternating electric field actuates reversible conformational evolution of sulfonate groups, alleviating impurity ion entrapment and reviving blocked Li+ migration pathways. Theoretical calculations unveil field‐induced thermodynamic inversion, converting strong Mg2+ adsorption into electrostatic repulsion to facilitate impurity expulsion. In situ spectroscopic characterizations further corroborate dynamically tunable sulfonate‐cation coordination behavior. This work sheds light on triggered sulfonate‐cation interfacial engineering to boost high‐performance electrochemical lithium extraction via dynamic ion sieving.
nd6fb64d7e47c: Excessive UV exposure is a major cause of skin damage, yet practical wearable UV monitoring systems require not only mechanical compliance but also long‐term biological and environmental compatibility. Here, we report an elementally biocompatible flexible optoelectronic transistor (EBOT) platform in which all functional components are constructed from physiologically relevant elements. Zn‐Mg‐based oxides serve as the semiconductor and dielectric layers, Mg acts the electrode, and biodegradable poly(3‐hydroxybutyrate‐co‐4‐hydroxybutyrate) (P34HB) provides a flexible substrate and encapsulation layer. A low‐temperature, all‐hard‐mask fabrication strategy enables device and circuit patterning without photolithography, preserving the compatibility of the constituent materials. Post‐fabrication supercritical‐fluid treatment further optimizes the device characteristics, improving the on/off ratio, responsivity and detectivity by 48.1%, 7.5% and 16.8%, respectively. Rather than eliminating persistent photoconductivity, we harness defect‐mediated carrier trapping and relaxation as an intrinsic temporal integration mechanism, allowing a single device to simultaneously encode UV dose and exposure history without additional memory components. The EBOT platform exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and mechanical durability over 1,000 bending cycles. Furthermore, vertically integrated sensing‐computing architectures are demonstrated by stacking photodetection and logic functionalities, providing a pathway toward highly integrated transient bioelectronic systems. This work establishes an elementally compatible strategy for developing flexible and environmentally transient optoelectronic platforms.
nc0fbf8edfe25: Direct ink writing (DIW) using frontal ring‐opening metathesis polymerization (FROMP) enables rapid, energy‐efficient fabrication of thermoset and elastomeric architectures through a self‐propagating exothermic curing reaction. However, FP‐DIW is constrained by stringent rheological requirements, feature‐size limits from front quenching, and the need for the reaction front to track the nozzle. Here, we overcome these constraints by leveraging embedded 3D printing to implement FP‐DIW with delayed solidification, thereby decoupling shape retention and solidification from ink chemistry and rheology. A yield‐stress support medium stabilizes low‐viscosity inks, suppresses gravitational and capillary instabilities, mitigates quenching at small diameters, and enables complex overlapping and mechanically interlinked features to fuse after deposition. Two thermal initiation strategies are introduced: volumetric dielectric heating via microwaves and surface heating at the support‐bath boundary. Dicyclopentadiene (DCPD), cyclooctadiene (COD), and mixed formulations provide tunable mechanical properties with glass transition temperatures from –50°C to 160°C. The approach enables lattices, springs, mechanically interlocked structures, and multimaterial architectures, substantially expanding the accessible material, feature‐size, and geometric design space compared with FP‐DIW in air.
n3885555f637f: 2D layered semiconductors show great promise as channel materials for post‐Si electronic devices, and the interfaces they form are critical determining factors in device performance. In particular, the interface between 2D layered materials and metal contacts is highly problematic because of the Fermi‐level pinning (FLP) phenomenon. FLP results in a high Schottky barrier height (SBH), which hinders carrier transport and polarity modulation in devices. Here, we present a simple, scalable, solution‐processable contact‐engineering approach for the 2D layered material WSe2 that involves inserting a van der Waals (vdW) interlayer of networked single‐walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs). The networked CNTs act as a pseudo‐2D layer that effectively separates the metal contacts from WSe2. Additionally, the bundled CNTs serve as an efficient electrical interlayer. In the Pd‐contacted case, the SBH with WSe2 decreases from 357 meV to 46 meV upon insertion of the CNT interlayer, which enables efficient tunneling‐based carrier injection into the WSe2 channel, resulting in an improvement in the pinning factor from S = −0.021 to S = −0.42. This work demonstrates that a 2D vdW interlayer can be prepared through a solution process to mitigate FLP, thereby facilitating the large‐scale fabrication of device arrays and circuits based on 2D layered materials.
n6957a674617c: Carbon Nanotube van der Waals Contacts A pseudo‐two‐dimensional network interlayer formed from single‐walled carbon nanotubes separates the metal electrode from WSe2, creating a van der Waals interface that mitigates Fermi‐level pinning. The resulting reduction in Schottky barrier height in field‐effect transistors enables efficient tunneling carrier injection and polarity modulation, offering a simple, scalable route toward high‐performance electronics based on two‐dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides. More details can be found in the Research Article by Daisuke Kiriya and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77339).
n4c423ecb46a4: Electrostatic complexation of oppositely charged biomacromolecules produces a spectrum of condensed phases, from liquid coacervates to ordered solids. Yet the underlying amino acid sequence‐level rules remain poorly understood. Here, we utilize computationally designed coiled‐coil peptide “bundlemers” as a programmable platform to systematically investigate these principles. This study demonstrates that precise control over the material phase formed through electrostatic complexation is achieved through subtle amino acid sequence modifications. By tuning coiled coil terminal motifs and surface charge distribution, bundlemer‐polypeptide complexation can span liquid coacervates, soft solids, or solid precipitates. Specifically, bundlemer coiled coil nanoparticles with +24 charge were complexed with different lengths of polyanionic polypeptide. Nanoparticles with a mixed charge character containing both acidic and basic amino acids produced coacervate phases. When the bundlemers displayed only basic amino acids making a single charge‐type +24 nanoparticle, solid precipitates with specific hexagonal lattice symmetry were formed. When the charge character was flipped with negatively charged bundlemers and positively charged polypeptide, similar hexagonally packed complexes were formed. This work establishes a robust framework for programming the self‐assembly of polyelectrolyte‐based soft matter, offering a sequence‐guided pathway from disordered liquid condensates to precisely defined, ordered nanomaterials.
n79e735a227b5: Conjugated polymers are at the heart of numerous current and emerging technologies. Doping, a process by which charge carriers are introduced, is crucial to their functionality and performance. Despite a significant historical context, doping processes based on ground‐state charge‐transfer (CT) complex formation, mediated by the supramolecular hybridization between the frontier molecular orbitals of distinct molecular species, remain rare and are consequently poorly understood. In this context, there are no clear demonstrations of this alternative doping phenomenon in contemporary donor–acceptor conjugated polymers. Here, we use diketopyrrolopyrrole‐based donor–acceptor semiconducting polymers and a π‐conjugated penta‐t‐butylpentacyanopentabenzo[25]annulene “cyanostar” macrocycle to demonstrate the first examples of features that control ground‐state CT complex formation in these contemporary conjugated polymer frameworks. Using complementary experimental techniques, we articulate how subtle molecular, electronic, and solid‐state features impact the supramolecular hybridization of the frontier molecular orbitals and impact the resultant (opto)electronic, magnetic, and transport properties. These studies demonstrate that the admixture between distinct π‐conjugated materials can have dramatic outcomes on solid‐state electronic properties and performance through modification of the density of states. These results and associated mechanistic insight will enable completely new co‐design rules for organic semiconductors and emerging molecular dopants that offer new functionality and precise property control.
n144739bf0027: Metal halide scintillators have attracted continuously increasing interest for low‐dose and high‐resolution X‐ray imaging, yet typical luminescent silver halides suffer from severe hygroscopicity and exciton quenching caused by Ag–Ag cluster aggregation. To address these challenges, we design and report mononuclear five‐coordinate silver(I) halide complexes (dppb)2AgX·DMSO (X = I, Br, Cl) with 1,2‐Bis(diphenylphosphino)benzene (dppb) ligand. Halogen substitution enables tunable broadband emission, while the chloride analogue achieves efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and a high PLQY of 76%. The chloride analogue possesses more rigid AgClP4 coordination environment compared with its bromide and iodide counterparts, enabling restricts excited‐state relaxation, suppresses non‐radiative decay, and preserves favorable singlet‐triplet energetics and spin‐orbit coupling. Meanwhile, the chloride analogue shows superior scintillation with a high light yield of 26631 photons/MeV, and a detection limit of 304.67 nGyair s−1. Furthermore, a high spatial resolution of 20.2 lp mm−1 for X‐ray imaging is achieved based on the transparent Ag‐Cl composite gel scintillator screen. This work not only provides a promising design principle for achieving high scintillation in TADF‐type Ag(I) halide complexes by halogen regulation, but also provide a new platform for Ag(I) halide complexes in X‐ray imaging.
n7ba7cf28bb3f: Conjugated polymer‐based phototheranostics have attracted considerable attention for cancer treatment owing to their excellent photothermal properties and biocompatibility. However, integrating efficient photodynamic activity into conjugated polymer systems without compromising their intrinsic photothermal performance remains a major challenge. Here, we report structurally engineered selenophene‐doped polypyrrole nanoplatforms (Ppy‐PSe NPs) for imaging‐guided synergistic phototherapy. Incorporation of selenium‐containing heterocycles into the conjugated polypyrrole framework introduces a pronounced heavy‐atom effect, which promotes intersystem crossing and substantially enhances reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation while preserving broadband near‐infrared (NIR) absorption and efficient photothermal conversion. Upon NIR laser irradiation, Ppy‐PSe induces severe oxidative stress, lysosomal disruption, cytoskeletal collapse, and apoptotic cell death. Mechanistically, ROS‐mediated suppression of HSP90 disrupts the oncogenic JAK2/STAT3 signaling axis, thereby reprogramming tumor thermotolerance and sensitizing malignant cells to photothermal injury. In vivo, Ppy‐PSe exhibits favorable biosafety, efficient tumor accumulation, and robust photoacoustic imaging capability for real‐time therapeutic guidance. Notably, NIR‐triggered treatment achieves complete tumor eradication in a lymphoma xenograft model, particularly under NIR‐II irradiation. This work establishes a multifunctional conjugated polymer nanoplatform that integrates ROS amplification, thermo‐sensitization reprogramming, and imaging‐guided synergistic phototherapy for precision cancer treatment.
nb12d9b3d2a75: The cycling stability of silicon-based anodes is severely compromised by the large volume changes of active particles during (de)lithiation, which disrupt the electrode structure due to insufficient interfacial bonding. Here, by leveraging the initiated chemical vapor deposition (iCVD) technique, we construct a poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (PGMA) anchoring interlayer on SiO x particles. This interfacial design replaces weak physical interactions with robust covalent bindings: the epoxy groups in PGMA undergo ring-opening reactions with the poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) binder. This covalent linkage maintains direct contact between SiO x particles and the binding network during volume expansion, while enabling the conductive matrix to recover upon contraction, thereby effectively preventing particle isolation and pore formation. Consequently, the PGMA-modified electrode exhibits significantly enhanced interfacial adhesion and structural robustness, spatially confining solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth and mitigating continuous electrolyte depletion. As a result, the proposed strategy delivers improved cycling stability, retaining 95.0% of its capacity after 300 cycles with alleviated polarization. This study offers new perspectives for designing high-performance silicon-based anodes by overcoming a key limitation in electrode structural stability, namely the weak interaction between silicon particles and the binder.
n275775639136: High‐entropy phosphides (HEP), derived from high‐entropy alloys (HEA), combine multimetallic active sites with phosphorus‐induced structural and electronic modulation, yet remain difficult to construct at the atomic‐layer scale. Here, a two‐step phosphorization and epitaxial‐growth strategy is developed to synthesize Pd@PdP@HEP nanocrystals with surface‐confined PdPtIrRhRuP HEP atomic layers. This design is further supported by density functional theory (DFT) formation‐energy calculations, which indicate that P preferentially occupies surface and near‐surface sites. Controlled phosphorization of Pd cubic seeds enables systematic regulation of P incorporation, lattice expansion, and structural disorder, while subsequent multimetallic growth produces compositionally complex surface layers. Electron microscopy and synchrotron‐based X‐ray absorption spectroscopy confirm the formation of P‐enriched HEP atomic layers and reveal strong electronic coupling between P and neighboring metal atoms. The optimized Pd@PdP@HEP catalyst exhibits higher alkaline hydrogen‐evolution activity than commercial Pt/C and the unphosphorized Pd@HEA counterpart, while maintaining excellent durability. DFT calculations show that P‐induced surface reconstruction and charge redistribution downshift the d‐band center, bring the hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔGH*) closer to thermoneutrality, and shift the hydroxyl adsorption free energy (ΔGOH*) toward more positive values. These effects create a balanced adsorption environment, contribute to enhanced alkaline hydrogen‐evolution kinetics, and provide an effective strategy for engineering nonmetal‐modified high‐entropy catalysts.
nd93f4ac1dcb9: Aerosol chemical vapor deposition (CVD), a variant of floating catalyst CVD, enables one‐step, solvent‐free, and scalable production of high‐quality single‐walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) films for next‐generation electronics, photonics, and optoelectronics. However, simultaneously achieving high production yield and superior film conductivity remains an unsolved challenge, as conventional approaches to boost yield inevitably promote nanotube bundling and degrade performance. Here, the mechanistic origin of this yield‐performance trade‐off is investigated through precise control of nanotube structural parameters during synthesis. Systematic investigation identifies nanotube diameter as the most influential structural parameter for balancing production yield and film conductivity within the broad parameter space explored: large‐diameter SWCNTs not only form lower‐resistance junctions but also tend to suppress bundling during aerosol‐state growth, thereby indirectly enhancing film conductivity while simultaneously facilitating higher yield. Bundle length and crystallinity also contribute positively, although their influence is less pronounced. Consequently, SWCNT‐predominant films (>55%) comprising large‐diameter nanotubes (∼2.4 nm) are synthesized, achieving an unprecedented yield‐to‐sheet‐resistance ratio at 90% transparency of 4.7 mm2 L−1 (Ω □−1)−1 after doping—an order of magnitude higher than previously reported values for SWCNT films. This work establishes fundamental structure‐property‐yield relationships and provides a rational design strategy for scalable production of high‐performance SWCNT films.
nc524eaeab918: Liquid crystal networks (LCNs), characterized by their unique dynamic mechanical properties derived from LC mesogens, have emerged as one of the most promising materials for ubiquitous vibration and impact protection. Additive manufacturing further expands their potential by enabling the fabrication of lightweight and customizable architectures with tailored energy-dissipation properties. However, the requirements of photocurable groups inherently constrains network topology, hindering synergistic enhancement in energy dissipation and mechanical robustness, a fundamental challenge for energy-dissipative polymers. Here, we propose a topology-engineering strategy to access hybrid-topology liquid crystal network (HT-LCN) that integrates LC mesogens, linear polymer chains, dangling chains, and crystalline domains within a single printable network, enabling multiple energy-dissipation mechanisms while preserving structural robustness. As a result, HT-LCNs exhibit an ultrawide effective damping temperature range (∼200°C), exceptional toughness (68 MJ m− 3), and the highest impact absorption reported for 3D-printable polymeric matrix materials (179 MJ m− 3@4000 s− 1). Furthermore, HT-LCN-based architectures show more than 200% higher specific energy dissipation than conventional printed systems, paving the way for designing and engineering robust 3D printable energy-dissipation devices.
ncab54c4ff8f3: Diabetic wounds remain a critical clinical challenge due to their hostile microenvironment featured by high infection risk, persistent inflammation, etc. Herein, we innovatively constructed an exogenous‑payload‑free hydrogel via in situ photopolymerization for electrochemical therapy (ECT) of diabetic burn wounds, which utilized (3‐acrylamidopropyl)trimethylammonium chloride as monomer and hydroxypropyltrimethyl ammonium chloride chitosan as biomass scaffold. Cationic quaternary ammonium groups on the hydrogel backbone first captured bacteria through electrostatic attraction. The platinum electrodes embedded within hydrogel generated therapeutic agents under a mild 2.0 V: counter Cl− within the hydrogel matrix was oxidized at the anode into reactive chlorine species for sterilization, while water in the hydrogel was electrolyzed to produce H2 at the cathode to downregulate pro‐inflammatory cytokines IL‐6 and IL‐1β. Meanwhile, the electric field accelerated fibroblast migration and angiogenesis by activating the PI3K/AKT and VEGF pathways. By harnessing the hydrogel's own structural components as the sole therapeutic resources, this work established an exogenous‑payload‑free strategy for multifunctional ECT toward diabetic wound healing.
naf18cb663db0: Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) from electrospinning offer robust mechanical frameworks but often require complex post‐treatments and suffer from low room‐temperature ionic conductivity and sluggish Li+ transport, hindering the development of solid‐state batteries. Here, we propose a surface‐grown protective fiber strategy: growing CoMn‐layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheets on polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers to anchor residual propylene carbonate (PC) molecules, forming a composite SPE (LDH@PAN SPE) with interfacial stabilization. Abundant LDH hydroxyl groups immobilize PC via hydrogen bonding, while metal sites electrostatically interact with the lithium salt anions (TFSI−), promoting Li salt dissociation and optimizing [Li(PC)x]+ solvation. Additionally, hydrogen bonding between PAN cyano‐groups and LDH creates continuous radial Li+ pathways. The LDH@PAN SPE achieves high ionic conductivity (1.36 mS cm−1), Li+ transference number (0.80 at 20°C), and a 4.9 V window. Li||Li symmetric cells cycle for 1600 h at 0.2 mA cm−2 with a critical current density of 1.8 mA cm−2. LiFePO4||Li full cells deliver excellent rate capability (110.2 mAh g−1 at 5 C) and long‐term cycling (81.3% retention after 1100 cycles at 1 C) at room temperature, alongside flexibility and flame retardancy.
