Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show that the oxidized [4Fe–4S]2+ cluster stabilizes substrate interactions and the conformation of the C-terminus, facilitating a catalytically productive orientation of C256. The activation barrier of 17.7 ± 1.7 kcal mol–1 from quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) umbrella sampling MD simulations at the B3LYP-D3(BJ)/6-31G(d) level is consistent with kinetics experiments performed on an ortholog enzyme. The redox state of the iron–sulfur cluster shows its role in modulating the conformation of conserved K144, which is important for transition state stabilization in the nucleophilic attack. These findings illuminate the mechanism of this P. aeruginosa target and provide broader insight into the roles of iron–sulfur clusters in controlling enzyme reactivity.
nf54c9c3a4e37: Sn–Pb perovskites are promising low-bandgap absorbers for photovoltaics, but their efficiency is limited by the low open-circuit voltage, VOC. The VOC deficit, WOC, is related to energetic disorder, characterized by the Urbach energy, EU, comprising static and dynamic contributions. For Cs0.25FA0.75SnxPb1–xI3, these contributions were determined using time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) and photoluminescence (PL) measurements between 180–350 K. For Pb-based films, both techniques provided similar EU values. However, for Sn-containing compositions (x = 0.2 and 0.5), TRMC-derived EU were twice higher than those found by PL. These differences arise from compositional heterogeneity: TRMC integrates absorption over the entire thickness while the PL-derived absorption originates from low-bandgap domains, likely from the Sn-rich top surface as revealed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The PL-derived EU trend corresponds to the bandgap-normalized WOC, which is smallest for x = 0.5 (∼9.2 meV), attributed to the low dynamic contribution originating from the lower mass of Sn.
n30b94de8dfc0: Catalyst layers are widely used to accelerate water dissociation in bipolar membranes (BPMs), yet their role in defining junction electrostatics and reversible reaction kinetics remains unclear. Here, we probe the electrochemical response of catalyst-containing BPM junctions using open-circuit voltage measurements, polarization analysis, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We show that catalyst nanoparticles influence both the recovery of the membrane potential and the voltage losses associated with water dissociation and formation at the catalyst layer. These changes reflect coupled effects of catalyst surface chemistry, junction electrostatics, and proton-transfer kinetics. Notably, catalysts that recover the membrane potential do not necessarily reduce overvoltage under applied bias, highlighting that membrane-potential recovery alone is insufficient to predict BPM performance. By combining improvements in membrane-potential recovery and reaction kinetics, catalyst–ionomer interface engineering reduces water-formation losses by up to 65% and increases peak power density for energy storage by more than an order of magnitude.
ncaa528f19de4: Organic electrodes for secondary batteries are hindered by molecular dissolution and low operating voltages. Herein, we report a coordination-driven strategy to construct insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules (BTD-M, M = Cu, Ni, or Zn) featuring high-voltage p-type triphenylamine-derived ligands (N4′,N4′-diphenyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-3,4,4′-triamine, BTD). By precisely tuning metal–ligand coordination, we thermodynamically lock discrete molecules against electrolyte dissolution while preserving unhindered access to active sites. The optimal BTD-Cu exhibits a narrow bandgap of 0.7 eV, enabling extensive electron delocalization for electronic conductivity. This electrode delivers a near-theoretical capacity of 134 mAh g–1 at 1C and still delivers 83 mAh g–1 at 10C. Leveraging bipolar redox chemistry of p-type ligands and metal centers, the symmetric all-organic dual-ion battery achieves an average voltage of 2.4 V and a cycle life exceeding 1000 cycles. This work establishes insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules as an accessible platform for organic battery design.
n7239f24e26b8: Sustainable Na-ion batteries (NIBs) have attracted widespread attention in transportation vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems due to abundant sodium sources, high safety records, and favorable all-climate performance. However, their overall performance and cost are largely governed by cathode materials, which determine practical application and commercial market prospects. Iron- and/or manganese-based polyanionic cathodes not only reduce cost but also provide high working voltage and desirable cycling stability, benefiting from strong inductive effects and robust structural covalency of polyanionic groups, making them attractive for sustainable batteries. This review summarizes material design concepts, research progress, technological bottlenecks, and development directions for various types of phosphate, pyrophosphate, and sulfate cathodes. Besides, we focus on clarifying the structure–function relationships by comprehensively comparing synthesis methods, crystal structures, electrochemical behavior, and reaction mechanisms of Fe/Mn-based polyanionic cathodes for NIBs. This review provides critical guidance for the future advancement of practical NIBs.
ncffc9d7d09d2: Hydroxide-induced degradation and swelling of organic anion exchange membranes (AEMs) fundamentally limit the advancement and industrialization of alkaline hydrogen production. Here, we present a free-standing inorganic AEM comprising 90 wt % layered double hydroxides within a three-dimensionally fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene scaffold. The membrane achieves zero swelling, suppressed hydrogen crossover, and a low area-specific resistance of 0.089 Ω cm2 while remaining stable for 1344 h in 1 M and 30 wt % KOH at 80 °C, under which commercial polymeric membranes fail rapidly. The confined hydrogen-bond network within layer double hydroxide galleries promotes Grotthuss-dominated OH– transport as supported by ab initio molecular dynamics. The membrane sustains 1 A cm–2 operation for 550 h in AEM water electrolyzers and 425 h in alkaline water electrolyzers, establishing a durable inorganic AEM platform for alkaline hydrogen production and related electrochemical energy technologies.
n385a1c2c168c: Secondary injury following spinal cord injury (SCI) is not a unidimensional pathological process; rather, it involves a spatiotemporally organized cascade that rapidly evolves from an acute inflammatory storm and tissue breakdown to stalled repair and impaired regeneration in the subacute phase. However, most current therapeutic strategies depend on single-dose administration or isolated targets and thus fail to keep pace with the dynamic progression of SCI. Here, we developed a core–shell microneedle platform that aligns drug delivery with SCI progression by temporally decoupling the release kinetics of distinct therapeutics. The shell enabled rapid methylprednisolone (MP) release to suppress inflammatory cascades and restrict the expansion of secondary injury during the acute phase, while the core achieved sustained release of miR124-enriched M2 macrophage-derived exosomes (M2-miR124-Exo), promoting neuroprotection and microenvironmental remodeling during the subacute phase. This “suppression-then-repair” strategy synchronized treatment timing with stage-specific pathological demands, overcoming the limitations of conventional single-window delivery systems. Mechanistically, the platform promoted neuronal survival and axonal regeneration partly through modulation of key signaling pathways, including MAPK. In vivo, the platform markedly improved locomotor recovery in SCI rats, reduced lesion size, and exhibited no detectable systemic toxicity. These findings establish a programmable, pathology-guided delivery paradigm that addresses the spatiotemporal mismatch in SCI therapy and offers a promising strategy for precision intervention in complex CNS injuries.
n4a6924edc7f8: Encapsulation of two-dimensional (2D) materials with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is widely used to fabricate ultraclean van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures for optoelectronic and quantum transport studies. These devices are often operated under strong out-of-plane displacement fields that tune the electronic properties of the active 2D material, while the surrounding hBN is typically assumed to remain electronically inert. This assumption, however, neglects defect states that are present even in high-quality hBN crystals. Here, we probe their response to the applied displacement field using monolayer graphene encapsulated between hBN crystals as a sensitive charge sensor. Increasing the displacement field induces notable charge transfer between graphene and hBN, producing additional electron doping of ≈10–20 × 109 cm–2 even at the moderate displacement field (∼0.5 V nm–1), while simultaneously increasing carrier-density inhomogeneity of the graphene layer. Both effects are consistent with ionization of defect states within the hBN bandgap, with the bulk density ∼1–7 × 10–5 nm–3 varying across different hBN crystals. Our results show that displacement-field-induced defect ionization in hBN can modify the electronic response of vdW heterostructures, with direct implications for device design and interpretation of experiments.
n2e7df69f5597: We demonstrate a flexible nanofibrous membrane featuring a valley-cell array (NMVA). Inspired by honeycombs and spider silk, the NMVA is rationally designed using poly(vinyl alcohol), carbon black, and MOF-303 as its main components. The synergistic effect of the flexible honeycomb network, abundant hydrophilic sites of MOF-decorated nanofibers, rapid photothermal response, and multidimensional structural stability favors highly efficient adsorption and desorption dynamics during water harvesting. The valleys of the honeycomb cell arrays enhance light capture for photothermal conversion and water release, while the abundant hydrophilic sites facilitate water molecule capture and uptake. As a result, NMVA achieves a high water uptake capacity of ∼0.41 g g–1 at 25 °C and 30% RH, and can release 92% of the absorbed water within 30 min under 1 sun irradiation. For an integrated NMVA in outdoor conditions under sunlight of ∼0.76 kW m–2 on average, water harvesting capacities reach 3.85–5.0 L kg–1 day–1 at 42–68% RH through continuous all-day water uptake–release over seven cycles. This study provides insights into the design of novel materials that can be extended into the realms of water engineering for energy systems and portable devices.
n26dc3652116f: Cardiomyocyte contraction drives the pumping action of the heart and is fundamental to cardiac mechanophysiology research. Conventional optical and force-based approaches for cardiomyocyte contraction detection are limited by phototoxicity or potential alterations in cell morphology and physiology. Electrical impedance sensing is a label-free approach for noninvasive contraction recording, but current sensor optimization still mainly relies on substantial adjustments to electrode size or pattern. Herein, we present a nanoedge-regulated impedance sensing (NERIS) approach. Electrode structures with different pit depths are designed to regulate the cell-electrode interface to precisely optimize impedance properties. Increasing pit depth shifts the peak impedance response to lower frequencies, potentially reducing detection system bandwidth demands. At the optimized frequencies, long-term recordings support quantitative analysis of cardiomyocyte mechanophysiology. Furthermore, functional cardiac drug assessment is performed by characterizing contractile responses to norepinephrine and isradipine. This NERIS approach is expected to be widely applied in cardiomyocyte mechanophysiology and cardiac drug assessment.
n6e362e6663b1: Following the successes of the messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines against COVID-19, mRNA-LNPs are being explored for varied multidose applications including cancer immunotherapies and protein replacement therapies. LNPs rely on poly(ethylene glycol)-lipid (PEG-lipid) coatings for stability, but increasing anti-PEG antibody prevalence threatens repeat-dose efficacy and increases pseudoallergic risk, creating an urgent need for alternatives. Here, we introduce poly(acrylamido) lipids (PAM-lipids), a family of polymer lipids that effectively replace PEG-lipids in mRNA-LNP formulations. Systematic variation of monomer chemistry, molar mass, and end group reveals critical structure–activity relationships determining LNP size, polydispersity, and transfection efficiency. Varying PAM monomer chemistry allows minimization of antipolymer antibody cross-reactivity, with multiple PAM-lipids demonstrating no anti-PEG antibody binding. Several PAM-LNPs exhibit superior mRNA transfection efficacy to PEGylated clinical benchmarks in vitro and in vivo across multiple cell types, organs, routes of administration, and mRNA cargos. In particular, lead PAM-LNPs enhance mRNA delivery to dendritic cells (up to 120-fold in vitro and 3-fold in vivo) and macrophages (4-fold in vivo), with 2.5-fold superior lymph node expression, driven in part by increased cellular association and lymphoid targeting. Crucially, PAM-LNPs evade circulating anti-PEG antibodies to rescue lost mRNA efficacy after repeated dosing, resulting in 300% mRNA expression relative to that of PEG-LNPs. These findings demonstrate PAM-lipids as a chemically varied, immunologically compatible family of PEG alternatives for mRNA-LNP therapeutics.
nfffa949cc975: Layered manganese-based oxides for potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) suffer from severe structural degradation, primarily due to irreversible phase transitions, Jahn–Teller distortion, and sluggish K+ diffusion kinetics. Here, we propose an alkali-metal site riveting strategy by selectively incorporating oversized Rb+ ions into the prismatic sites of P2-type K0.55Mn0.8Ni0.1T0.1O2. The introduced Rb+ acts as a rigid pillar, expanding the interlayer spacing and reinforcing adjacent transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) bonds. This synergistic modulation not only widens the two-dimensional diffusion channels for rapid K+ transport but also effectively suppresses the detrimental P2–P′2 phase transition and mitigates Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn3+. Consequently, the optimized K0.55Rb0.025Mn0.8Ni0.1Ti0.1O2 cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 105.3 mAh g–1 at a current density of 20 mA g–1, outstanding rate capability (56.1 mAh g–1 at 500 mA g–1), and long-term cycling stability with 82.1% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, a pouch cell paired with a soft carbon anode achieves 81.3% capacity retention over 300 cycles. This work demonstrates that anchoring oversized cations in alkali-metal layers provides a universal and effective strategy toward near-zero-strain layered oxide cathodes for advanced PIBs.
n10de749cbfa9: Photoresponsive drug delivery systems are often described as bioorthogonal. However, certain wavelengths and intensities of visible light are known to modulate cellular phenotypes. This apparent discrepancy highlights a gap in knowledge with direct implications for the design of photoresponsive drug delivery systems. In this report, we investigated the response of primary macrophages to visible light (405–630 nm) due to their broad tissue distribution, phenotypic plasticity, and central role in orchestrating immune responses across diverse pathologies. We found distinct wavelength-dependent changes in cytochrome c oxidase activity, metabolic function, cytokine secretion, and biomarker expression at clinically relevant intensities of light. Further investigation of red light (630 nm) demonstrated complex dose-dependent metabolic and phenotypic responses. To illustrate the clinical implications of these findings, we employed 470 nm-triggerable carbon monoxide-releasing micelles to deconvolute the individual and combined effects of light exposure and therapeutic payloads. Our findings suggest that macrophages respond in a wavelength and intensity-dependent manner, and incorporating photoresponsive carbon monoxide-releasing systems elicits distinct immunomodulatory responses compared to irradiation alone. This work establishes a basic design framework for leveraging light parameters such as wavelength and intensity to achieve desirable immunomodulatory responses with photoresponsive drug delivery systems for specific disease applications.
n320e2a7d7a19: Secretory proteins encode cellular states not only through their abundance but also through their intracellular transport before being released. However, visualizing protein secretion behavior with molecular specificity and a low background remains challenging. Here, we report VEGF-responsive electrochemiluminescence (ECL) nanoemitters that enable spatiotemporal mapping of intracellular protein distribution at different stages of the secretion process by integrating a metal–organic framework (MOF) confining Ru(bpy)32+ with DNA tetrahedral gates (DTGs) programmed with aptamers. The MOF core provides bright, stable, and electrically addressable ECL emission, whereas the discrete DTGs regulate coreactant accessibility and prevent premature emission until VEGF recognition triggers gate displacement and restores ECL activity, converting intracellular molecular recognition events to quantitative optical signals. This architecture enables rapid, concentration-dependent, and selective activation, allowing high contrast discrimination of VEGF-rich tumor cells from epithelial cells. Under DFO stimulation, single-cell ECL imaging revealed heterogeneous VEGF upregulation and mapped its progressive redistribution from the perinuclear region to the cell periphery during secretion. This gated ECL platform enables quantitative spatiotemporal visualization of protein secretion behavior beyond the static molecular localization.
n8bef34ebf68d: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS− readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li+, constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H2O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm−2)/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF6‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.
n89e5b5bca6e5: Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N4. To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.
nffe48c158979: Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g−1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mgIr cm−2, it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm−2. Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.
ncf71a8efe79d: High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li+ transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li+ transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide‐enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb‐O‐Cl framework on LiNi0.83Co0.07Mn0.10O2 cathodes (denoted as C‐NCM). Derived from a mixed‐anion LiNbOCl4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb‐O‐Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb‐containing near‐surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li+ transport. Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li+ migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C‐NCM exhibits reduced sulfide‐derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface design from passive oxide‐barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed‐anion interfacial chemistry.
ne30e3fb6ac4e: Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi0.65Co0.05Mn0.30O2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO2. Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.
n1be1486fcdc2: Two‐dimensional heterostructures combining sp–sp2$^2$ hybridization—blending graphene with graphyne‐based allotropes—offer substantial potential for enhancing the tunability of electronic and transport properties while providing significant structural flexibility, which are desirable characteristics for next‐generation nanoscale electronics. Despite such potential, their experimental realization remains elusive, as synthesized carbon heterostructures are limited to doped, graphene‐based systems exhibiting exclusively sp2$^2$ hybridization. Here, the on‐surface synthesis of covalently bonded sp–sp2$^2$ lateral heterostructures between graphene nanoribbons and graphdiyne networks on Au(111) is demonstrated. Atomic‐resolution scanning tunneling microscopy, combined with density functional theory, reveals the formation mechanism of the covalent interfacial bonds between nanoribbons and graphdiynes, also highlighting the key role of surface chemistry. Bromine atoms, deriving from the molecules dehalogenation and chemisorbed along the nanoribbon, inhibit junction formation, but bonding efficiency can be boosted up to 66% by controlled removal of these byproducts. Electronic structure and transport calculations show that the 2D heterostructure by itself is characterized by disentangled properties for the two subsystems, forming an atomically narrow junction, enabling voltage‐tunable spatial current separation in two dimensions. These results define a viable strategy for engineering graphene‐based sp–sp2$^2$ heterostructures, paving the way for the design and synthesis of all‐carbon nanoscale electronic architectures.
n42c97edef5de: Autonomous soft actuators are essential for untethered intelligent robotic systems. However, achieving energy‐efficient operation and long‐term shape retention in solid‐state platforms remains a significant challenge, as most conventional systems rely on continuous power input or complex fluidic architectures. Here, we report an environmentally adaptive ionic actuator inspired by the Venus flytrap, capable of self‐sensing and bidirectional deformation without sustained external energy. By incorporating azobenzene moieties into an ionogel network, we trigger a unique nanopore‐mediated Janus actuation. A single, low‐power UV pulse (35.3 mW cm−2) induces rapid photoisomerization and localized dehydration, forming surface nanopores that facilitate asymmetric moisture uptake. This structural reconfiguration drives directional bending that is passively maintained for over 10 min, which is an exceptionally long retention time compared to conventional soft actuators. Furthermore, electrification‐induced voltage signals enable zero‐bias proximity sensing. By integrating these synergistic characteristics, we demonstrate a biomimetic ionograsper that combines ion‐redistribution‐induced sensing with energy‐efficient light‐triggered actuation for sophisticated object manipulation. Overall, this work provides a robust strategy for developing multifunctional and power‐efficient soft robots capable of intelligent environmental interaction.
n2e53476b6aec: Bioinspired Ionic Soft Actuators In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74981), Hong Chul Moon, Yong Min Kim, and co‐workers propose a multifunctional ionic soft actuator that integrates ion‐redistribution‐based proximity sensing with structural‐reconfiguration‐driven bidirectional actuation. UV‐induced photoisomerization and dehydration generate a nanoporous surface that promotes asymmetric rehydration, enabling long‐lasting deformation after a single low‐power stimulus, while mobile‐ion redistribution provides self‐powered non‐contact sensing for energy‐efficient soft robotic manipulation.
n626fd9beb0a4: Mucosal inflammatory disorders such as dry eye disease (DED) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), driven by TNF‐α‐mediated immune‐epithelial crosstalk, remain therapeutically challenging. Conventional inhibitors often suffer from poor mucosal permeability and transient efficacy with 1:1 binding. Although extracellular protein degradation (eTPD) technologies can eliminate pathogenic proteins, most of them operate stoichiometrically, limiting dosage efficiency and durability. Here, we report a receptor‐mediated endolysosomal recycling chimera (RECYC) platform that enables catalytic, recyclable degradation of TNF‐α with multiple turnovers, achieving sustained suppression of mucosal inflammation. RECYC integrates a pH‐responsive peptide that binds TNF‐α at physiological pH and releases it in acidic endosomes, with a CI‐M6PR‐targeting aptamer that remains pH‐stable to drive continuous recycling. The anti‐TNF‐α RECYC achieved efficient uptake and recyclable clearance of extracellular TNF‐α across conjunctival and colonic epithelial cells and macrophages, achieving superstoichiometric TNF‐α clearance with up to 7.5 catalytic turnovers. The ∼30 kDa RECYC exhibited superior tissue penetration in murine cornea and colon compared to inhibitory antibodies. In murine DED and IBD models, RECYC restored ocular surface homeostasis and reduced colon inflammation with low‐dose, infrequent administration. Human corneal limbus organoids further confirmed prolonged anti‐inflammatory activity. Together, RECYC establishes a modular, recyclable eTPD platform for sustained treatment of TNF‐α‐driven mucosal inflammation.
nb7a3ca15d683: Simultaneously achieving high visible transparency, high refractive index (n), and a large Abbe number (υ D) in organic polymers remains a fundamental challenge. Here, a facile and efficient dual sulfur-mediated Michael addition strategy is reported to synthesize transparent high refractive index polymers (HRIPs) with large υ D. By combining main backbone de-conjugation to preserve visible transparency with rational side-chain engineering for n-tuning, the optimal polymer (H4) achieves an ultrahigh n of 1.86 at 589 nm alongside a large υ D of 34.93 and robust stability. Moreover, polymer H4 exhibits remarkable performance in nanoimprint lithography, replicating features down to 75 nm with aspect ratios up to 8.5 and a low volumetric shrinkage of only 3.23%. Notably, a nanoimprinted metalens prototype fabricated from H4 delivers a relative focusing efficiency of 49.8% at 550 nm (NA = 0.5), approaching the theoretical design value (52.94%). Therefore, the high refractive index polymer H4 bridges molecular design and manufacturable meta-optics, showing tremendous potential in scalable, flexible, next-generation photonic platforms by translating side-chain polarizability engineering into practical wavefront control.
n64a6df8ab309: In structural energy storage devices (SESDs) that simultaneously store electrochemical energy and bear mechanical loading, the external force will normally affect the electrochemical performance of SESDs. One example is that, under cyclic bending stress, voltage ripples emerge in charge‐discharge curves, which cause voltage instability. In this study, we demonstrate that these voltage ripples originate from spatially heterogeneous electric field distribution within the mechanically deformed region. By using polarized electric fields formed through hydrogen bonding networks in MXene additive electrolyte, we can effectively homogenize the distribution of the electric field, thereby attenuating voltage ripples and smoothing the voltage curves. Moreover, the uniform electric field distribution promotes uniform Zn deposition and extends the device lifespan. As a result, the fabricated Zn‐ion‐based structural hybrid supercapacitor (CSHS) with MXene additive electrolyte exhibits a capacity retention of 93.6% after 10 000 three‐point bending cycles at a strain of 0.5%, much higher than that of CSHS without the addition of MXene (80.4%). The investigation into the suppression of voltage ripples of SESDs paves a viable way to design high‐performance structural power sources capable of exhibiting stable voltage under mechanical loading.
n1594ca0dfe47: Aerogels have emerged as a unique class of ultralight porous materials that combine exceptional thermal insulation with low density, high porosity, and remarkable structural versatility, enabling broad opportunities across aerospace, energy, electronics, environmental remediation, and wearable technologies. However, their widespread adoption has been constrained by the high cost, limited scalability, and energy‐intensive nature of conventional manufacturing processes, particularly supercritical CO2 drying. This review highlights recent advances in scalable and cost‐effective aerogel fabrication, including ambient‐pressure drying, templating strategies, top‐down manufacturing, chemical vapor deposition, and solution spinning, which collectively enable enhanced performance while significantly reducing production complexity and cost. We further present a unified perspective on the thermal transport physics of porous materials by systematically discussing the mechanisms of solid conduction, gas conduction, convection, and thermal radiation, and comparing aerogels with other porous architectures such as cellular foams. These fundamental insights establish rational design principles for engineering next‐generation aerogels with tailored thermal functionalities. Finally, we showcase emerging applications that extend well beyond thermal insulation, including moisture‐ and water‐driven energy harvesting, oil–water separation, high‐temperature acoustic insulation, and thermoregulating smart textiles. By bridging scalable manufacturing, fundamental thermal science, and emerging multifunctional applications, this work provides a comprehensive framework for the rational design and commercialization of next‐generation aerogels, paving the way toward their widespread adoption in advanced materials and engineering systems.
nfacb45ed1c36: Efficient wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite top cells are essential for high‐performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs), yet their fabrication in humid ambient air remains difficult because moisture‐ and oxygen‐induced reactions deteriorate film quality and stability. Here, 4‐[[4,6‐bis(octylthio)‐1,3,5‐triazin‐2‐yl]amino]‐2,6‐bis(1,1‐dimethylethyl)‐phenol (BTDP) is introduced into the perovskite precursor to enable WBG perovskite formation under high‐humid ambient air conditions. BTDP scavenges superoxide radical anions, inhibits I− oxidation to I2, absorbs ultraviolet light, coordinates with Pb2+ to regulate crystallization and forms a hydrophobic barrier at surfaces and grain boundaries. With this strategy, blade‐coated WBG perovskite solar cells (PSCs) fabricated at 60% relative humidity deliver a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.45%, which represents the highest PCE reported for air‐processed WBG PSCs with bandgap ≥1.68 eV. Mini‐modules with an aperture area of 14.81 cm2 reach 20.12% efficiency. Moreover, the method enables ambient‐air fabrication of two‐terminal perovskite/tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) TSCs with a certified efficiency of 32.59%, among the highest PCEs reported for two‐terminal perovskite/TOPCon TSCs. This study provides a scalable route to efficient, stable single‐junction and tandem perovskite photovoltaics.
nb0b4a69f1d1d: AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next‐generation ferroelectric in‐memory computing architecture and radio‐frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high‐quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high‐electron‐mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system‐level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy‐efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).
n5b0d605e0c61: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a multifactorial degenerative joint disease characterized by irreversible cartilage deterioration associated with chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, tissue acidosis, and abnormal mechanical loading. During OA progression, inflammation‐associated metabolic reprogramming and hypoxia‐enhanced glycolysis promote lactate accumulation and local acidosis. OA‐associated acidosis may function as an exacerbating factor within this pathological microenvironment by engaging acid‐sensing pathways and contributing to chondrocyte senescence, apoptosis, and SASP‐associated inflammatory amplification, thereby exacerbating cartilage degeneration. Accordingly, therapeutic strategies that actively neutralize pathological acidity while concurrently modulating inflammatory and oxidative stress cascades may provide a more robust, disease‐modifying approach for OA intervention. Herein, we designed a nanoreactor termed OLDH‐DP@POM by integrating mildly alkaline layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheets with active acid‐neutralizing capability and anchoring polyoxometalates (POM) with antioxidant activity, thereby enabling coordinated regulation of pathological acidosis and oxidative stress. Meanwhile, lubrication‐enhancing zwitterionic poly(2‐methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine) (PMPC) polymer brushes were grafted, endowing the nanoreactor with superior joint lubrication and chondroprotective capability. Both in vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that OLDH‐DP@POM effectively neutralized local acidosis at osteoarthritic lesions, substantially ameliorated synovial inflammation, suppressed Piezo‐mediated mechanotransduction, delayed chondrocyte senescence, and ultimately attenuated cartilage degeneration. Overall, this work provides a promising nanotherapeutic platform for disease‐modifying treatment of OA.
ncdcb9062b087: Designing two-dimensional (2D) materials from atomically precise nanocluster building blocks is a challenging task, yet crucial for next-generation electronic devices. By tuning cluster nuclearity and ligand environment, well-defined assemblies can be designed, enabling control over optoelectronic properties at the atomic level. Herein, we report the bottom-up synthesis of two structurally distinct 2D nanocluster-assembled materials constructed from Ag12 (2D Ag12-CAM) and Ag11 (2D Ag11-CAM) nanocluster building blocks. The change in cluster nuclearity arises solely from ligand tuning; benzenethiol yields the Ag12-based framework, whereas 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzenethiol (BTFMBT) directs formation of the Ag11 analogue. Lateral memristive devices fabricated from these materials (D-1: 2D Ag12-CAM; D-2: 2D Ag11-CAM) exhibit coexistence of negative differential resistance (NDR) and robust resistive switching with endurance stable over 4000 switching cycles. Device D-2, based on 2D Ag11-CAM, shows a markedly enhanced on-off (I on/I off) ratio (∼ 642) compared to device D-1 (∼ 200), and more pronounced NDR. Furthermore, the 2D Ag11-CAM (D-2)-based device was evaluated for neuromorphic functionality, mimicking the adaptive behavior of biological synapses. It exhibits analogue potentiation and depression under pulse stimulation, while experimentally extracted synaptic weight updates enable an artificial neural network to achieve a test accuracy of 84.2%, approaching that of a machine learning (ML)-trained network (93.2%).
n4ccac956fd53: Bifunctional electrocatalysts that simultaneously drive CO2 reduction (CO2RR) and oxygen evolution (OER) in neutral electrolytes are essential for aqueous Zn‐CO2 batteries (AZCBs), but conventional designs prioritize CO2RR and are often incompatible with OER, resulting in low energy efficiency, poor reversibility, and rapid degradation of batteries. Here, we introduce a unified catalyst architecture integrating Cu and Ni single atoms with boron‐, nitrogen‐co‐doped carbon (CuNi@BNC‐T). Heteroatom co‐doping stabilizes high single‐atom loadings, enhances metal‐support interactions, and suppresses carbon corrosion, while N‐coordinated Cu+ and Ni3+ sites cooperatively boost CO2RR‐OER, enabling ethanol formation and low‐overpotential OER. This strategy achieves a 0.7 V voltage gap at 5 mA cm−2, 522 h cycling at 20 mA cm−2, and first ethanol production via AZCBs with energy efficiency of 88% (flow‐cell). By elucidating previously unresolved degradation pathways, this work also correlates catalyst dynamics with battery failure, establishing design principles for durable bifunctional catalysts in aqueous Zn‐CO2 systems.
nd6e55a3132e3: Emergency hemostasis during prehospital care significantly reduces trauma‐related mortality. Nanoclay exhibits potent procoagulant properties, but its detachment from the substrate leads to non‐negligible adverse reactions and diminished hemostatic efficiency, hindering its clinical application. Despite improved immobilization via polymer incorporation, irreversible surface encapsulation undermines the procoagulant efficacy of nanoclays. Here, inspired by the anchoring mechanism of fish scales to skin via collagen fibers, we introduce a nanofiber‐bridged design that enables robust immobilization of nanoclay and maximized loading density, while also achieving its full exposure for optimal hemostatic performance. The microfiber‐derived nanofiber network expands the interfacial contact area and anchors nanosheet inner surfaces via synergistic covalent and non‐covalent interactions, effectively redistributing stress to resist dynamic shear forces. The resulting kaolin‐cotton hemostatic dressing demonstrates superior physical stability (no detectable kaolin leakage) and enhanced hemostatic efficacy in rat (62%), rabbit (58%), and pig (35%–43%) hemorrhage models compared with conventional hemostatic agents. Importantly, no leakage‐induced chronic inflammation was observed. Moreover, laboratory‐scale preparation and processing of 5 kg products demonstrate the feasibility of industrial‐scale production, making them further processable into various cotton‐based materials. This bioinspired dressing offers improved efficacy and safety, along with affordability, underscoring its potential for clinical translation.
n0e6592222268: Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode-targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode-specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)-dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record-high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg− 1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode-free full cells based on Na4Fe3(PO4)2 (NFPP), Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP), and NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.
n26fb167361c7: Thermal conductivity is one of the fundamental manifestations of how the underlying atomic arrangement in materials facilitates heat flow. The critical role of thermal conductivity in influencing the performance of materials in the energy and quantum technologies arena makes engineering it to match functionality a crucial challenge to address. Here, we focus on intrinsically tuning thermal transport in inorganic crystalline solids through the strategic design of crystal structures. As structure is determined by the underlying chemical bonding, light is also shed on the influence of chemical bonding on thermal transport, including the concept of multicentered bonding and the role of antibonding states. In this review, we distill global research efforts into key design features rooted in chemical bonding and structural principles that enable an intrinsic property‐based descriptor‐framework for the purposeful manipulation of thermal conductivity in inorganic solids. We survey examples in which lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline solids has been pushed to extremes, specifically toward the diffusion limit or even rendered glassy. The broad and significant applicability of these principles across functional materials such as thermoelectrics, superionic conductors, ferroelectrics and halide perovskites is thus demonstrated. Finally, we explore emerging directions in the field, including topological phonons, thermotronics, and the phonon wave‐particle crossover, alongside the impact of artificial intelligence and machine learning on materials discovery.
n22b86b29462d: Artificial photosynthesis technology holds great promise for sustainable energy conversion and value‐added chemical synthesis, yet integrating efficient light absorption with high product selectivity remains a major challenge. This study constructs an Ni‐La2O3/La2NiO4 catalyst through in situ perovskite derivation that mechanistically and functionally mimics the chloroplast for artificial photosynthesis by coupling photo and photothermal catalysis with the integration of broad‐spectrum light harvesting, directional charge transfer, as well as CO2 adsorption and hydrogenation. Three functional interfaces are formed: La2O3‐La2NiO4 (Z‐scheme), Ni‐La2NiO4 (Schottky junction), and La2O3(adsorption)‐Ni(activation). The two heterojunctions facilitate electron transfer to metallic Ni nanoparticles, which activates H+ to form an NADPH‐like surface Ni‐H species by enabling the collection of photo and photothermal generated electrons. Meanwhile, the Lewis‐basic La2O3 captures CO2 and promotes its activation at the La2O3‐Ni interface. In CO2‐to‐CH4 conversion, Ni‐La2O3/La2NiO4 demonstrates an exceptional CH4 production rate of 9.96 µmol h−1 g−1 and a selectivity of 92.5% under natural conditions (i.e., AM 1.5 irradiation, ambient temperature, and atmospheric pressure) without external assistance, which outperforms pure La2NiO4 by 10.2 and 4.6 times, respectively. This work advances a new strategy for efficient solar‐to‐fuel conversion.
nc1105fddef5e: Conventional self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are conformationally rigid. They cannot buffer interfacial strain during rapid perovskite crystallization, limiting both film quality and device stability. We introduce a conformational engineering strategy using 2‐benzhydrylidene‐succinic acid (BSA), a rigid diphenylmethylene anchor with flexible succinic acid chains to create an elastic buried interface. Atomic simulations show BSA acts as a compressible buffer, delaying stress accumulation by ∼6 Å under displacement. This dynamic strain dissipation improves heterojunction contact and enhances hole extraction and transport. BSA‐modified p‐i‐n devices reach 26.89% (0.045 cm2, certified 26.52%). Large‐area modules (22.95 cm2) deliver 24.30% (certified 23.95%), which is among the highest certified values for this area. The devices retain 90% of initial efficiency after 316 h of diurnal cycling and 88% after 300 extreme transient thermal shock cycles from ‐20 °C to 100 °C. This conformational design integrates mechanical compliance with electronic functionality in scalable perovskite photovoltaics.
na2dbf3dff9bf: Particle packing in battery electrodes is pivotal to the fast‐charging performance of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, precise control of particle packing structure remains a major challenge in electrode fabrication, primarily owing to the absence of robust interfacial bonding between micron‐scale particles. Herein, we propose a novel layer‐by‐layer single‐layer particle assembly technique to fabricate electrodes with well‐defined particle packing structures. Using this approach, we prepared a 12‐meter‐long graphite (Gr)/hard carbon (HC) hybrid anode featuring a body‐centered cubic (BCC)‐like structure, which maximizes intimate Gr/HC contact interfaces and facilitates solid‐state Li+ transport. Coupled with LiFePO4 (LFP) cathodes, the as‐fabricated anode exhibits a high‐capacity retention of 80.7% after 1650 cycles at 4C. From an electrode design standpoint, this controllable particle‐packing strategy paves the way for a universal framework for developing sustainable, long‐cycling, and fast‐charging electrodes, potentially applicable to many types of battery anodes and cathodes.
na3742449c0ac: Transverse thermoelectrics (TEs), enabling interconversion between orthogonal heat and electric currents, offers unique advantages in device geometry and design flexibility. Yet, achieving large transverse TE signals at room temperature remains challenging. Here, we establish a cooperative framework in which the goniopolar effect and the anomalous Nernst effect jointly enhance the transverse TE response in kagome magnets. We demonstrate that kagome lattice‐derived electronic structures intrinsically yield axis‐dependent polar Seebeck coefficients arising from flat bands and van Hove singularities (VHSs), while broken time‐reversal symmetry induces topological band splitting that generates large net Berry curvature within the same energy window. Combining transport measurements, DFT calculations and real‐space thermal imaging, we demonstrate a room‐temperature record cooperative transverse TE signal of 15.6 µV/K in the kagome ferromagnet MgMn6Sn6 among metallic systems. Our findings establish a cooperative framework linking the anomalous Nernst and goniopolar effects and provide a widely applicable design strategy for achieving large transverse TE response in kagome magnets.
n6c26d2d4a9a2: Periprosthetic microbial bone infection (PMBI) is a serious pathological condition that may lead to terrible consequences without timely therapeutic intervention. However, the clinical management of PMBI is challenged by the difficulties in the efficient and accurate identification of microbial pathogens. For this purpose, we report a DNA‐based loop‐amplifier fluorescence signaling network (DLFSN) for the efficient and accurate detection of pathogenic microbes in the context of PMBI. The DLFSN system comprises an Amplifier Unit A and a Quantifier Unit B. Specifically, Amplifier Unit A transforms pathogenic microbial genetic materials into fluorescent DNA molecules through an entropy‐driven automated reaction loop, leading to efficient and precise amplification of pathogen‐specific genomic input signals. Subsequently, Quantifier Unit B converts the quenched fluorescent intermediate products into an activated state, thus allowing the precise identification of the genetic signature of pathogenic microorganisms in a quantitative manner. DLFSN demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy comparable to gold standard PMBI diagnostic technologies, including tissue section staining and qPCR, while the actual assay time was much lower at only around 30 min for real‐life patients. The DLFSN system provides a promising precision diagnostic tool for early PMBI diagnosis, holding promise to improve orthopedic outcomes in the clinic.
n35da88ac7f3e: Precise manipulation of the coordination environment in single‐atom catalysts is crucial yet challenging for boosting oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance. Here we present a sacrificial‐guided etching strategy to activate intrinsically passive d10 Zn centers in single‐atom catalysts, wherein Bi(NO3)3‐mediated protection preserves ZnN4 coordination by mitigating excessive etching, while NaCl‐driven Cl doping imparts a remote electron‐withdrawing effect, concertedly modulating the electronic structure of the Zn centers. This decoupling strategy, which assigns protection and doping to distinct species, unlocks asymmetric Zn single atoms with dual precision over coordination number and dopant configuration. The resulting catalyst achieves an exceptional ORR half‐wave potential of 0.916 V, surpassing commercial Pt/C, and delivers a record peak power density of 258 mW cm−2 with outstanding cycling stability exceeding 450 h in zinc‐air batteries. Integrated theoretical and in situ spectroscopic analyses reveal that Cl incorporation disrupts the symmetric ZnN4 electronic structure, optimizes the d‐band center, and alters unoccupied orbital hybridization, thereby accelerating O2 protonation and boosting the overall catalytic activity. This work establishes a well‐defined strategy for the precise construction of single‐atom metal centers, providing insights into the development of high‐performance non‐precious metal electrocatalysts.
nb6d1d0746714: Pyroelectric dynamic therapy is capable of triggering pro-inflammatory cell death and anti-tumor trained immunity. However, the high thermal conductivity, quick pyroelectric carrier recombination of traditional pyroelectric materials, and the limited immunogenicity of tumor cells greatly hinder the efficacy of trained immunotherapy. Herein, a nanoplatform integrating iron-doped defect-engineered misfit layered calcium cobalt oxide (Ca3Co4O9− x ) nanostructure, immune adjuvant polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid, and nanovesicles extracted from 4T1 cells is constructed to initiate pyroptosis and the anti-tumor trained immunotherapy. The low thermal conductivity of misfit layered Ca3Co4O9− x reduces the overall thermal conductivity. The oxygen vacancies created by defect engineering serve as electron traps, inhibiting charge carrier recombination. Therefore, Ca3Co4O9− x achieves multi-level energy conversion between thermal, electrical, and chemical fields, enriching various reactive oxygen species (ROS). Polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid synergizing with ROS activates caspase-1/Gasdermin D-mediated pyroptosis, and stimulates the secretion of more types of inflammatory cytokines through the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway, leveraging the limited immunogenicity of the tumor environment. Nanovesicles provide precisely homologous tumor-targeting ability by efficient biomimetic fusion. The nanoplatform demonstrates excellent pyroptosis-inducing efficiency and anti-tumor immunity training ability, indicating the feasibility of the multi-physical field energy conversion and defect engineering strategy for synergistic enhancement of pyroelectric dynamic therapy in anti-tumor trained immunotherapy.
n37fe3de8ffac: Cyclohexanol electrooxidation reaction (CHAOR) offers a sustainable route for producing adipic acid. However, achieving high ring-opening efficiency and stable long-term yield remains challenging due to limited understanding of active oxygen species and reaction pathway. In this study, Ru single atoms and oxygen vacancies are used to construct a synergistic interface for efficient CHAOR. Oxygen vacancies serve as structural promoters by creating Lewis acid sites that enhance organic species adsorption and mitigate the agglomeration of Ru atoms. Atomically dispersed Ru sites act as functional modulators by disrupting the interfacial hydrogen-bond network-as confirmed by in situ Raman-to lower the *OH formation barrier and facilitate the accessibility of organic molecules to the catalytic surface, as supported by quartz crystal microbalance experiments and density functional theory calculations. The tandem electrochemical-chemical mechanism is elucidated: *OH formation is the electrochemical step, while its reaction with organics is the chemical step. Benefiting from the synergy, Ru-NiO x achieves 100% conversion and 87% AA (adipic acid) yield at 1.45 VRHE. Furthermore, a photovoltaic-electrolysis system is developed to address solar intermittency and power fluctuations, in which Ru-NiO x exhibits excellent stability over 1000 h with a maximum productivity of 204.4 µmol cm−2 h−1. Scaling to eight electrolyzers demonstrates good scalability, indicating strong potential for practical application.
n6c0b3af00761: The rational design of solid‐state electrolytes (SSEs) with high ionic conductivity, interfacial robustness, and thermal stability remains a critical challenge for lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Herein, we established the crystal‐transformed hydrogen‐bonded organic framework/trinuclear Cu cluster organic framework heterostructures (HOFa/TrCuMOF8) as thermally stable SSEs for LMBs. The crystal‐transformed HOF/MOF heterostructure constructs continuous low‐energy Li+ transport pathways, while the pendant ‐CH3 with strong steric hindrance induces anion adsorption to effectively suppress TFSI− migration. Meanwhile, coordination‐confined TrCu synergizes with imine (C = N) groups to create a dynamically polarized local electronic environment through Li+‐induced charge redistribution, thereby promoting selective Li+ transport. Consequently, the HOFa/TrCuMOF8 SSEs deliver a high Li+ transference number (0.94) and ionic conductivity (2.7 mS cm−1 at 30°C). Compared with polypropylene (PP) separators, the flexible HOFa/TrCuMOF8 SSEs maintain structural integrity at high temperatures (180°C), effectively suppressing electrolyte shrinkage and thermal short‐circuit propagation. The assembled Li|HOFa/TrCuMOF8 SSEs|LiFePO4 LMBs achieve 97.8% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 2 C and maintain stable cycling even at 100°C. Remarkably, the Li|HOFa/TrCuMOF8 SSEs|NCM811 pouch cell exhibits an impressive energy density of 259.4 Wh kg−1 with enhanced thermal safety. This work provides a crystal‐transformation strategy for engineering HOF/MOF heterostructures toward thermally stable solid‐state lithium batteries.
n1a5095ae1b22: Rechargeable zinc–air batteries (RZABs) require durable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts. However, the long‐term stability of metal‐nitrogen‐carbon atomic‐site catalysts (M–N–Cs) remains challenged by electrochemical corrosion and reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐induced damage arising from multiple degradation pathways, which collectively demand comprehensive solutions due to the “buckets effect” of instabilities. Herein, we develop a robust FeNi–N–C dual‐atom catalyst (DAC) featuring a bridging µ2‐O electron modulator for long‐life RZAB catalysis, retaining 80% of its initial energy efficiency after 2800 h. Theoretical simulations and experimental evidence support multifaceted stabilization of the N/O‐coordinated vicinal Fe–Ni configuration. The µ2‐O bridge improves intrinsic structural stability, decreases electron density on adjacent metal and N atoms to mitigate N‐site protonation and intermediate‐induced metal stripping, and promotes an O─O cleavage pathway that suppresses H2O2/ROS accumulation. These findings provide a coordination‐engineering strategy for designing durable M–N–C catalysts for long‐life RZABs.
n3fdc1313d70b: Out-of-plane spin–orbit torque generation in mirror-symmetry-broken materials is a promising approach for current-induced field-free magnetization switching. However, the key challenge lies in identifying materials with high in-plane spin Hall conductivity that simultaneously generate large out-of-plane spin–orbit torque for low-power spintronic applications. Previously studied low-symmetry materials, in which mirror-symmetry breaking is confined to the surface and the spin Hall conductivity is low, have not resolved this challenge. Here, we demonstrate deterministic field-free magnetization switching enabled by the bulk-mirror-symmetry-broken topological material Bi1− x Sb x (012) with high in-plane spin Hall conductivity. The power consumption is two orders of magnitude lower than that of heavy-metal-based devices. Spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance measurements confirm the bulk origin of the out-of-plane spin–orbit torque in Bi1− x Sb x (012), yielding an out-of-plane spin Hall conductivity of ∼1.12×105ℏ2eΩ−1m−1$ \sim \!1.12 \ensuremath{\times{}}{10}^{5}\frac{\hslash}{2e}{\mathrm{\Omega}}^{-1}\ {\mathrm{m}}^{-1}$ (for x = 0.2), which is 5.6 times larger than that of TaIrTe4. Our results establish bulk mirror-symmetry engineering as an effective strategy for designing energy-efficient field-free spin–orbit torque devices.
ne5dda881f25f: Electromagnetic wave pollution has seriously affected human body health owing to rapid technological development, such as 5G/6G communication networks. The demand for wearable materials with high‐performance electromagnetic protection and excellent mechanical properties is urgent, but still lacks reasonable preparing strategies to realize multifunctional features. Here, we develop a dual‐network structural strategy to construct a high‐performance ionogel fiber by using a scalable dry‐spinning method. In this approach, semi‐crystalline hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) combined with poly thioctic acid (PTA) serves as a structural backbone by hydrogen bonding network; simultaneously, MXene nanosheets and IL [EMI][ES] build an interconnected 3D conductive network, imparting functional properties to the backbone matrix. The ionogel fiber exhibits excellent EMI shielding effectiveness (60.6 dB), high strength (9.5 MPa), superior elongation (>200%), good self‐healing, and recyclability. Notably, we found that the electromagnetic shielding performance of the fabric woven from the ionogel fibers increases by up to 7.5% within a strain range of ≤10.0%. This enhancement can be due to a stretch‐induced orientation of the MXene nanosheets, which optimizes the internal conductive network of the ionogel. This work offers a promising route toward next‐generation, wearable electromagnetic protection materials adaptable to both static and dynamic environments.
n19c76943ae4f: Acidic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) enhances carbon efficiency and electrolyzer stability. Although nickel single‐atom catalysts (Ni‐SACs) effectively convert CO2 into CO in neutral/alkaline conditions, their performance in acid is hindered by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here we show that tailoring the local strain of Ni‐SACs can enhance HER suppression across a broad potential range. Density functional theory calculations indicate that Ni‐SACs with steeper local curvature reduce *COOH adsorption by 0.23 eV while increasing *H adsorption by 0.55 eV. To validate our predictions, we leveraged carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with different diameters to impose controlled local strain on Ni‐SACs. In Ar‐saturated 0.05 M H2SO4, Ni‐SACs on 5‐nm CNTs (Ni‐CNT5) demonstrate the lowest hydronium and water reduction current density among all types of CNT support. In a flow cell with pH 1 catholyte, Ni‐CNT5 maintains >95% CO Faradaic efficiency (FE) from −1.0 to −2.4 V, in contrast to Ni‐CNT50 with ∼70% FE(H2) at −2.4 V. Owing to its effective HER inhibition, Ni‐CNT5 achieves 80% single‐pass CO2 conversion efficiency and operates stably in acidic electrolyte with negligible loss in current or selectivity. Our findings expand the toolbox for SACs engineering, highlighting the critical role of local stress for controlled activity.
n80a65955af06: Rational design of dual-site catalysts to decouple complex multi-electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO3 −) reduction reaction (NO3RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co7Fe3 heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO3RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4-electron step reduces NO3 − to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4-electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4-electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well-defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co7Fe3 with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO3RR through synergistic dual-spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near-unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH3 yield rate of 36.07 ± 0.52 mg h−1 cm−2 at −0.48 V versus RHE. Additionally, a rechargeable Zn-nitrate battery featuring this material as the cathode delivers a peak power density of 18.15 mW cm−2 with excellent cycling stability. This study provides a novel paradigm for designing efficient tandem electrocatalysts.
nf40d2ae319e3: Environmentally benign scintillators with broadband radioluminescence are highly desirable for low‐cost, high‐performance x‐ray imaging. Recently, copper iodide (Cu–I) clusters have emerged as promising candidates, owing to strong spin‐orbit coupling, favorable solution processability, excellent x‐ray absorption efficiency, and efficient exciton harvesting enabled by aggregation‐induced emission and thermally activated delayed fluorescence. However, the mechanism by which aggregation‐state variation enhances the light yield by modulating intermolecular interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a pair of isomeric Cu–I clusters with nearly identical x‐ray attenuation coefficients as a model platform to isolate and elucidate the role of intermolecular coupling. In this context, we uncover a breakthrough mechanistic picture in which engineered excited‐state coupling accelerates carrier relaxation and promotes efficient exciton harvesting and radiative recombination. Guided by this mechanism, water‐resistant cluster scintillator glasses with excellent processing flexibility are fabricated, delivering a high light yield of 32,456 photons MeV−1 and spatial resolution of 33.6 lp mm−1. Furthermore, tandem integration with a high‐Z scintillator enables selective density‐discriminating x‐ray imaging and micro‐computed tomography. This work provides mechanistic guidance for ligand engineering in the design of efficient cluster scintillators and facilitates the high‐throughput development of promising metal‐cluster complexes for advanced optoelectronic applications.
nb37c7d1eb252: Neuromodulation provides a means to perturb neural activity for investigating nervous system function and treating neurological disorders. Advances in stimulation strategies, molecular tools, functional materials and neural interfaces have progressively expanded the precision and versatility of such interventions. Yet neural activity can require regulation in opposing directions across different cellular, circuit and pathological states, motivating bidirectional neuromodulation that can both enhance and suppress neural activity. In this review, we examine the mechanisms and technologies that enable such bidirectional control across electrical, optical, thermal, mechanical, magnetic and chemical modalities. We compare these approaches in terms of spatiotemporal performance, penetration depth, specificity and safety, and examine the materials, transduction strategies and device architectures used to implement bidirectional neural control. We further discuss the applications of bidirectional neuromodulation in neuroscience research and the treatment of neurological disorders. Finally, we discuss the technical challenges and future directions toward more precise, independent and integrated bidirectional control, including its extension to closed‐loop adaptive regulation.
n339ae8d1c61a: Highly active and durable anode electrocatalysts are crucial for acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWE), yet IrO2-based catalysts often face a trade-off between activity and stability. In this study, a Cr-IrO2 catalyst is developed through partial substitution of Ir by Cr atoms in the IrO2 framework to overcome this limitation. Experimental and theoretical calculations reveal that the resulting Cr─O─Ir motifs amplify the orbital overlap the lone electron pair of O in H2O and the empty orbitals of Ir, thereby enhancing initial H2O adsorption. Meanwhile, Cr doping reduces the positive charge of H atoms in adsorbed H2O, thereby regulating the interfacial water structure and disrupting the hydrogen-bond network, which facilitates water dissociation and consequently increases the *O coverage for OER. Furthermore, the introduction of Cr atom into IrO2 weakens *OH adsorption at the second active site and shortens the dual-site distance, synergistically promoting the direct O−O radical coupling and enabling the oxide path mechanism (OPM). Consequently, Cr-IrO2 achieves 10 and 1000 mA cm− 2 at overpotentials as low as 233 and 348 mV, respectively, and demonstrates exceptional durability for over 2000 and 400 h in a practical PEMWE operating at 0.1 and 1 A cm−2, respectively.
n489b4337ec36: Flavin‐dependent monooxygenases (FMOs) catalyze redox reactions central to antibiotic degradation and metabolic detoxification, yet replicating their intricate cofactor‐dependent electron transfer in synthetic systems has remained elusive. Here, we report an electronic modulation strategy that enables cofactor‐free FMO‐like catalysis within a high‐entropy alloy nanozyme (HEAzyme‐Cu1.5). We induce localized electron cloud enrichment that shifts Cu 3d orbitals toward the Fermi level, establishing a self‐sustained redox channel without flavin cofactors. This atomic‐scale entropy‐driven alignment bridges the functional gap between natural cofactor‐dependent enzymes and artificial catalysts, demonstrating for the first time that complex redox cascades traditionally confined to biological systems can be reconstructed purely by materials design. This entropy‐driven electronic reconfiguration enables near‐zero barrier O2 activation and rapid hydroxylation with a kinetic constant. Integrating this multifunctional HEAzyme into a portable hydrogel sensor platform achieves real‐time antibiotic detection down to 11–25 nM and > 90% degradation within 20 min in complex water samples. This work establishes a universal design principle for programmable enzyme mimetics, where atomic‐scale entropy, electronic‐state alignment, and multimetal cooperation converge to emulate and transcend biological catalysis. Such entropy‐encoded redox systems offer a transformative route toward intelligent bioinspired materials for environmental remediation, green synthesis, and metabolic engineering.
ndd54768e2ce3: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) plays a critical role in maintaining central nervous system homeostasis by regulating molecular and cellular exchange between the brain and peripheral circulation. While most delivery strategies focus on crossing the BBB, targeting brain endothelial cells directly may offer a complementary and more controlled alternative for therapeutic intervention. This study presents a ligand‐free lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platform that enables efficient mRNA delivery to the brain endothelium via systemic administration. A modular synthesis strategy was used to generate a chemically diverse library of cholesterol‐based lipids. Screening of 486 LNPs identified an optimized four‐component formulation consisting of C6O2B2 (novel cholesterol‐based lipid), DODAP, DSPC, and DMG‐PEG, which achieves high transfection efficiency in brain endothelial cells without the incorporation of free cholesterol or disruption of BBB integrity and function, such as those utilized in focused ultrasound (FUS) techniques. This BBB‐targeting LNP platform avoids neuronal and glial transfection, thereby offering a noninvasive, and scalable approach for cerebrovascular gene delivery. The work establishes a new class of cholesterol‐based lipids and provides a foundation for next‐generation RNA therapeutics targeting BBB‐associated diseases.
n4b61bf1662e2: Magnetic materials, such as Ferumoxytol and Gd‐DTPA, have played an important role in biomedical areas. The relentless pursuit of novel magnetic materials that are clinically applicable is an eternal theme in biomedical engineering. Pyrite (FeS2) is a mineral drug in China that has been used for a long history. Besides the inherent biocompatibility proved in the human body as well as the donor of H2S, pyrite also belongs to the family of transition metal dichalcogenides, which endows it with flexible functional tunability of magnetism to be a promising candidate for novel magnetic nanodrug. However, the nano‐FeS2 synthesized by common coprecipitation often shows poor magnetic susceptibility, so its application has greatly been limited. Herein, we reported an innovative strategy to prepare nano‐FeS2 with high magnetic susceptibility (HS‐nano‐FeS2) via alternating magnetic field‐assisted coprecipitation. AMF treatment effectively regulated electronic reconstruction of Fe2+ in nano‐FeS2 without foreign‐element doping, and super‐exchange interaction is proposed as the dominant factor for the optimized magnetic susceptibility toward a favorable spin‐polarized configuration. The HS‐nano‐FeS2 is suitable for long‐term MR angiography imaging with excellent biosafety. We believe HS‐nano‐FeS2 provides a novel magnetic candidate for clinical translation and demonstrates an innovative strategy at the electronic level.
n2bb233d2b3c3: Osteomyelitis remains a major clinical challenge; however, current therapeutic strategies do not sufficiently address host immune defense, inflammatory microenvironment remodeling, or bone regeneration. Here, we show that excessive accumulation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in infected bone tissues contributes to osteomyelitis‐associated apoptosis and impaired osteogenesis. NETs disrupt PINK1/Parkin‐mediated mitochondrial quality control in osteoblast lineage cells, thereby promoting apoptosis, whereas inhibition of NET formation alleviates these pathological changes and improves bone repair in mice. Bone defects are aggravated in Prkn‐knockout mice upon the induction of osteomyelitis, supporting the functional role of PINK1/Parkin‐dependent mitophagy in the repair of infected bone. As a therapeutic strategy, gallium–selenium nanoparticles (GaSex) exert potent antibacterial activity, redirect neutrophils from NET formation toward phagocytosis, preserve osteoblast mitochondrial homeostasis, attenuate excessive mitophagy, and ultimately promote the repair of infected bone defects in rats. Collectively, these findings support NET‐driven osteoblast mitochondrial injury as a critical repair‐limiting mechanism in osteomyelitis and establish GaSex as a redox‐regulating platform that modulates this mechanism while preserving neutrophil antibacterial defense.
ncc27b22267e7: Achieving environmentally sustainable synthesis of high‐quality metal halide perovskite single crystals (MHP‐SCs) is critical for advancing next‐generation optoelectronic devices. The constrained solvent choices within the green chemistry framework pose a significant challenge to the fine control of crystallization pathways required for the growth of perfect MHP‐SCs. Here, we introduce a new paradigm for crystallization control based on steric hindrance engineering using a quantitatively validated green solvent system with high GlaxoSmithKline green solvent scores. We demonstrate that the steric bulkiness of solvent molecules, rather than donor number alone, plays the dominant role in governing the coordination strength between Pb2+ and solvent, thereby regulating precursor complex stability and crystallization kinetics. Finely tuned steric environments promote the unprecedented fast growth of MAPbI3 SCs with a record‐low trap density (2.56 × 108 cm−3) and narrowest x‐ray diffraction linewidth of 0.00802° (28.9″). These defect‐suppressed MAPbI3 SCs enable photodetectors with an ultrahigh specific detectivity of 6.8 × 1013 Jones and x‐ray detectors with a low detection limit of 3.6 nGyair s−1. The steric hindrance engineering strategy proves universal across perovskite compositions. This work establishes a sustainable, scalable platform for the growth of high‐quality MHP‐SCs using quantitatively green solvents.
n526c625dacb4: Plant stress during growth, caused by extreme environments and biotic attacks, threatens global biodiversity and crop production, necessitating urgent elucidation of plant adaptation mechanisms. Endogenous hormones of plant growth serve as master regulators and earliest indicators of stress adaptation, making it crucial to monitor their dynamics continuously. However, existing methods, including chromatography and electrochemical probes, fail because of their mismatch with the irreversible and plastic nature of plant growth. Here, we unexpectedly find a growing fiber sensor based on an electrode consisting of a dynamic polymer network infiltrated with liquid metal, termed metalgel. The sensor undergoes irreversible elongation ∼up to 10 times its original length under just 3.2 kPa tensile stress, at least 2 orders of magnitude lower than existing electronic conductive systems, thus achieving synchronous deformation with plant growth without inducing mechanical damage or hormonal disturbances. Hormone dynamics and relevant signaling pathways during plant growth in response to pathogen infection, salt stress, and even extreme ultraviolet radiation are thus revealed by the sensor. This work provides quantitative insights into plant stress resilience mechanisms and offers a feasible route to alleviate the food and ecological crises.
n8ba0aae01e29: Transitioning to halogen‐free solvent processing is essential for the scalable manufacturing of organic solar cells (OSCs), yet it remains challenging due to severe molecular aggregation and unfavorable phase separation.
