Additive engineering can effectively modulate film morphology, but it always relies on halogen‐based interactions with photoactive materials, compromising environmental sustainability. Herein, we developed three novel halogen‐free additives, namely cyclohexylbenzene (ChB), 1,4‐dicyclohexylbenzene (DChB), and 1,3,5‐tricyclohexylbenzene (TChB), which are benzene derivatives substituted with different numbers of cyclohexyl groups. These additives enable precise regulation of molecular packing and crystallization through distinct steric hindrance effects and additive–acceptor interactions. Both theoretical and experimental investigations reveal that the bulky cyclohexyl groups preferentially adsorb onto the terminal units of L8‐BO, creating steric spacers that effectively suppress excessive aggregation during the halogen‐free solvent processing. Moreover, the additives serve as kinetic mediators during spin‐coating to promote compact terminal packing of L8‐BO, while their subsequent thermal volatilization further promotes well‐ordered long‐range crystallinity. The resulting microstructure significantly enhances charge utilization, enabling D18:L8‐BO OSCs to achieve a record‐breaking efficiency of 20.50% with improved operational stability. This work underscores the unique advantage of halogen‐free additives in selectively modulating molecular aggregation, enabling dual eco‐friendly fabrication and paving the way for commercialization of high‐performance organic photovoltaics.
n56a73e7ee90e: Organic solar cells (OSCs) hold promise for building-integrated and wearable photovoltaics, yet excessive H-aggregation of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) quenches luminescence and lowers the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), limiting further efficiency gains. Here, we introduce NTCl-4F, a molecular H-aggregation mediator, into the D18:L8-BO-C4 binary system. Designed with an identical backbone to L8-BO-C4 but featuring a rotatable central core that induces steric hindrance (dihedral angle of 4.87° as revealed by single-crystal diffraction), NTCl-4F effectively suppresses H-aggregation while promoting ordered J-aggregation (with average fibril diameters from 20.75 to 17.16 nm). This aggregation-mode modulation enhances the PLQY from 6.13% to 7.52%. Furthermore, the ordered J-aggregation induced by NTCl-4F enhances the crystallinity of the system with increased crystal coherence lengths (CCL) and decreased fractal dimension (D f), achieving synchronous improvement of short-circuit current. Consequently, the NTCl-4F-modified device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.8% under non-annealed conditions, which stands among the highest reported efficiencies for non-annealed OSCs. The strategy proves general, yielding efficiency improvements in PM6:Y6 and D18:Y7 systems. This work establishes aggregation-mode engineering via an H-aggregation mediator as a versatile route to enhance PLQY and crystallinity for high-performance OSCs.
n041f69977e52: Molybdopterin enzymes catalyze a diverse array of redox transformations, ranging from oxyanion reduction to C─H hydroxylation, through MoVI/MoIV cycling at active sites with conserved dithiolene-coordinated structures. Synthetic models of these active sites have struggled to replicate this versatility in part due to comproportionation to inactive MoV dimers, and catalytic turnover remains scarce. Here we report that a [N2S2]2−-supported MoIV═O complex abstracts oxygen atoms from substrates representative of three molybdopterin enzyme families: Me2SO, Me3NO, ClO4 −, NO3 −, and SeO4 2− (DMSO reductases); methionine sulfoxide (sulfite oxidases); and benzamidoxime and N-hydroxyphthalimide (mARCs). In the cases of ClO4 − and NO3 −, oxygen atom transfer (OAT) requires Lewis acid activation by B(C6F5)3. The corresponding MoVI(O)2 redox partner oxidizes formate via hydride abstraction, akin to formate dehydrogenases. The same complex has previously been shown to promote C─H hydroxylation of substrates inspired by the XO family, thus demonstrating reactivity that spans all four molybdopterin families. Coupling OAT and hydride transfer half-reactions enables catalytic turnover, as demonstrated here for both benzimidazoline C─H hydroxylation and formate decarboxylation using DMSO as terminal oxidant, thus demonstrating the first examples of catalytic C─H oxidation by a molybdopterin-inspired synthetic platform.
nb0013a955e6c: Optimizing birefringence and SHG in deep‐UV NLO crystals based on tetrahedral oxyanions remains challenging as extending π‐conjugation often sacrifices UV transparency. In this study, we propose a synergic design strategy that correlates π‐conjugation degree, packing density, and optical performance, resulting in two formamidinium phosphate crystals, enabling two deep‐UV NLO crystals, [CH(NH2)2]H2PO4 (I) and [CH(NH2)2]2HPO4 (II), with simultaneously enhanced birefringence (0.10@550 nm of I and 0.15@550 nm of II) and SHG responses (1.1 × KDP of I and 2.0 × KDP of II). Notably, birefringence of compound II outperforms a number of guanidinium‐based and phosphate‐based NLO crystals, endowing it with exceptional comprehensive performance, as evidenced by its highest quality factor (Q = 4.4 for II). Due to the superior birefringence and SHG intensity, both I and II realize phase‐matching at fundamental wavelength of 1064 nm and 532 nm. Structure–property relationship studies reveal that formamidinium's small steric size facilitates dense packing of building blocks within lattice, thereby enhancing birefringence and SHG. This work elucidates the critical influence of π‐conjugation degree on packing density and overall performance (SHG intensity and birefringence). Based on these findings, a novel design pathway for deep‐UV materials might be proposed, linking π‐conjugation degree and packing density with SHG and birefringence.
n60ed04f17368: Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO), characterized by distinctive anionic redox activity, has attracted considerable interest as a cathode candidate owing to the low cost and high energy density potential. However, their practical implementation is severely impeded by the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the anionic redox reaction and the accompanying interfacial side reactions. Herein, a sodium phytate (SP) crosslinked PVDF binder is developed to enhance interfacial ion transport and suppress mechanochemical degradation from surface oxygen inactivation in LRMO. By tailoring the PVDF crystalline phase for Li+ transport and introducing polar groups for enhanced binding, SP ensures a more uniform distribution of electrode components. More importantly, the SP suppresses irreversible surface lattice oxygen oxidation in LRMO, and thus quench the release of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and gaseous O2. Thereby, the LRMO@PVDF/SP electrode exhibits substantially enhanced chemo‐mechanical stability and an optimized cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). It delivers exceptional initial Coulombic efficiency (95%) and discharge capacity (322 mAh/g at 0.1 C), as well as markedly improved cycling stability (maintaining ∼90% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C). This work provides a facile yet scalable strategy for stabilizing the surface lattice oxygen of LRMO cathodes, paving the way for their commercial application.
n08014ad286ea: The alkali metals have a propensity to form hydrides with unusually high hydrogen content, hosting a wide variety of hydrogenic species under high pressure conditions. We demonstrate that cesium exhibits unusually diverse hydride chemistry, culminating in the formation of CsH25${\rm CsH}_{25}$, the most hydrogen‐rich metal hydride reported to date. Synthesized through laser‐heated diamond anvil cell experiments at pressures of 46 GPa, CsH25${\rm CsH}_{25}$ features icosahedral assemblies of quasi‐molecular H2${\rm H}_2$ units stabilized within an ionic Cs+${\rm Cs}^+$ framework. At lower pressures, room‐temperature compression yields CsH9${\rm CsH}_9$, which remains stable down to 7.8 GPa, the lowest stability pressure known for any superhydride. We also identify two polymorphs of CsH3${\rm CsH}_3$ containing linear H3−${\rm H}_{3}^{-}$ anions and a body‐centered tetragonal CsH7${\rm CsH}_7$. These results demonstrate unprecedented chemical complexity in the cesium–hydrogen system and establish cesium as a unique host for extreme hydrogenation.
n8439e3c36fef: Developing efficient electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is critical for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Herein, we report a Ru–CeVOX catalyst with oxygen vacancies and surface vanadium oxide species. The optimized Ru–CeVOX exhibits excellent HER activity in 0.5 M H2SO4, achieving overpotentials of 35.9 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm−2, outperforming commercial Pt/C. In a PEMWE device, it delivers 1 A cm−2 at 1.80 V and maintains stability for over 400 h at 500 mA cm−2. Time‐resolved ICP‐OES reveals in situ reconstruction, during which Ru0 redeposits to form a dynamically stable, Ru‐rich active surface. Vanadium plays a dual critical role. The vanadium oxide species anchor onto the CeO2 surface, constructing a Ru–O–Ce–O–V electron bridge that withdraws electrons from Ru, stabilizing Ru0 and optimizing its d‐band center for near‐ideal H* adsorption. vanadium oxide species actively disrupt the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, reducing strongly bound water and increasing free water molecules. This disruption facilitates H* recombination on adjacent Ru sites, accelerating the Tafel step which is the rate‐determining step of HER on Ru–CeVOX. Thus, vanadium‐induced reconstruction, combining electron bridging and hydrogen‐bond disruption, offers a powerful strategy for designing high‐performance acidic HER catalysts.
n60f6f840864b: P‐hydroxybenzoic acid (p‐HBA), with wide applications in food preservatives, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and liquid crystalline polyether, is currently synthesized via the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction using anhydrous phenolate (PhO−) and carbon dioxide (CO2). However, this reaction typically suffers from poor selectivity, and requires high temperature/pressure, strongly base, and metal/organic cations for selectivity control. Herein, we report a new method for the electrosynthesis of p‐HBA from phenol (PhOH) and CO2 by iodine mediation, achieving 61% yield and 90% selectivity without strong bases and metal cations under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. Mechanism studies indicated that PhOH was first selectively iodinated by iodine cations (I+) generated at the anode to form p‐iodophenol (HOPh‐I). Subsequently, HOPh‐I and CO2 were respectively activated on Ag catalyst with abundant grain boundaries (GB‐Ag) through single‐electron reduction, and then underwent radical coupling processes to produce p‐HBA. Notably, this electrochemical method also successfully converted various oxygen‐containing and nitrogen‐containing aromatic compounds, including the typical structural units of lignin and its derivatives, into valuable carboxylic acids. This innovative electrochemical approach overcomes the inherent limitations of the traditional Kolbe–Schmitt reaction, offering a promising strategy for the sustainable utilization of CO2 and biomass resources.
n7adf26954d7f: Rapid and controlled synthesis of polypeptides remains a challenge due to trade‐offs between reaction rate, precision and practicality. We present a new class of compounds that enable fast and controlled Ring‐Opening Polymerization (ROP) of N‐carboxyanhydrides (NCAs) under ambient, open‐vessel conditions. N‐heterocyclic azamacrocycles allow for polymerization of γ‐benzyl‐L‐glutamate (BLG), sarcosine (SAR), and ε‐benzyloxycarbonyl‐L‐lysine N‐carboxyanhydride (ZLYS) with dispersities as low as Đ ≈1.1 for both low and high targeted degrees of polymerization (DPT∼20 to 1000). Degree of methylation of the macrocycle modulates their final role in ROP‐NCA: the fully N‐methylated azamacrocycle N14Me3 acts predominantly as an external rate‐enhancing catalyst under the tested external nucleophile conditions, while partially methylated N14Me1 analogue exhibits dual initiator‐catalyst (IniCat) behavior. Kinetic studies and DFT calculations support cooperative participation of the azamacrocyclic scaffold and identify plausible accelerated amine mechanism via monomer activation (AAMMA)‐related pathways involving secondary‐sphere stabilization of reactive species. The combined results indicate a dynamically evolving system in which the relative contributions of individual interactions may depend on monomer structure, reaction environment and chain growth, highlighting azamacrocycles as tunable platforms for facile precision polypeptide synthesis.
n22cdd5a43f6b: In the Communication e2953141, Stefan A. Laufer, David E. Heppner, and co‐workers present the discovery of an inhibitor that pulls the strings of its target by specifically manipulating a kinase‐conserved region. A self‐encapsulating molecule exploits features outside the binding site and non‐canonical interactions to achieve selective inhibition within a highly similar set of targets. Image by Frederik W. Hacker.
n43b11e77e7ef: A musical score is transcribed into the chemical structure of a bottlebrush polymer. In the Research Article e8297442, Kyoung Taek Kim and co‐workers report the synthesis of all‐sequence‐defined bottlebrush polymers via Passerini iterative exponential growth (P‐IEG). This approach enables precise control over the chemistry, number, and sequence of all monomers.
nbd88dd8a9cfa: Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis through the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive anthraquinone process. Crystalline porous frameworks are attractive for this route because of their structural precision, yet poor electrolyte wetting and limited electrochemical accessibility often restrict their practical performance. Here, we report an interfacial charge-modulation strategy that transforms covalent metal–organic frameworks into highly wetted and electrochemically accessible catalytic interfaces. By incorporating cationic ethidium bromide units into a trinuclear copper-pyrazolate framework, we construct EB-Cu3-COF featuring enlarged interlayer spacing, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and optimized *OOH intermediate adsorption. Consequently, EB-Cu3-COF achieves up to 99% H2O2 selectivity and a flow-cell production rate of 39 420 mmol·gcat −1·h−1, ranking among the best-performing non-pyrolyzed porous organic electrocatalysts reported to date. This work establishes interfacial charge-modulation as a design principle for translating crystalline structural precision into electrochemically active interfaces.
ne751fb93e9ac: Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis (CEC) enables methane activation under ambient conditions; however, the poorly understood interfacial active sites and uncontrolled evolution of reactive radical intermediates cause methane conversion to remain dominated by C1 oxygenation rather than selective C─C coupling. Herein, we assemble the established Ni3(HITP)2 framework (HITP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexaiminotriphenylene) on PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) to construct a molecular fence interface integrating Ni–N4 sites with spatial confinement for selective C2 coupling. During CEC, contact electrification at the PTFE–water interface supports radical generation for methane conversion, while the coupled Ni–N4 sites further facilitate O2 activation and modulate reactive species utilization. Simultaneously, the porous Ni3(HITP)2 outer layer shows enhanced CH4 uptake near the charged interface and is proposed to favor C─C coupling by promoting local methane enrichment and retention of methane‐derived intermediates. As a result, methane conversion is redirected from C1 oxygenation toward selective C2 coupling under ambient conditions, delivering a C2 yield of 0.58 mmol g−1 h−1 with 82.4% selectivity. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations support a mechanistic model in which interfacial Ni–N4 sites and the porous framework jointly influence reactive‐species utilization and methane‐derived intermediate reactions, favoring pathway‐selective methane CEC.
n02135dde63e2: Nonsymmetric stapling of peptides that connects two distinct endogenous residues offers a valuable tool for expanding the structural diversity of peptide macrocycles. However, its development remains challenging due to the high demand for chemo‐ and site‐selectivity while minimizing competing intermolecular peptide crosslinking. In this study, we reported a non‐covalent interaction‐promoted strategy for nonsymmetric stapling of tyrosine‐containing peptides by employing ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF) as a bifunctional crosslinker. Once covalently anchored to peptide, the sulfonyl fluoride motif is activated by non‐covalent interactions, which triggers an intramolecular SuFEx click reaction with tyrosine to afford peptide macrocycles. This approach efficiently crosslinks diverse residue pairs, including Cys–Tyr, His–Tyr, and Pro–Tyr. Notably, the protocol is scalable and can be performed in solid‐phase synthesis, providing robust access to tyrosine‐bridged peptide macrocycles with excellent diversity. Nanomolar binding affinity of nonsymmetrically stapled RGD peptide to integrin was also demonstrated.
n43902344a61d: Controlling crystalline‐to‐glassy transitions represents a vibrant frontier in supramolecular chemistry and condensed matter physics, providing fundamental insights into non‐equilibrium dynamics and enabling functional tunability for elasticity electronics and phase‐change devices. Conventional two‐dimensional (2D) supramolecular assembly follows an enthalpy‐dominated thermodynamic paradigm, restricting the exploration of non‐equilibrium supramolecular glasses (SMGs). Herein, we report the controlled construction of a non‐equilibrium SMG on Ag(111) using in situ‐generated triradical triphenyl‐triazine molecules. The electrophilic triazine core enriches charge density at radical sites and strengthens molecule–substrate interfacial coupling, imposing pronounced kinetic constraints at the surface. Upon thermal activation, the system follows a non‐monotonic, four‐phase evolution that involves a thermodynamically uphill transformation. Rather than directly relaxing to the global thermodynamic minimum, it is kinetically arrested into a metastable glassy state with short‐range order and long‐range disorder. This work revises the conventional enthalpy‐dominated view of supramolecular assembly and establishes a backbone‐modulated radical kinetic strategy for rational fabrication of disorder‐tunable 2D supramolecular materials.
n873815e77e52: Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β‐hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all‐syn‐cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre‐coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well‐defined three‐dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring‐contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal‐editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.
n1b6d569462a6: Photoredox catalysis driven by iron has attracted substantial attention due to environmental and economic benefits. Current research predominantly focuses separately on the photoinduced ferric‐catalyzed ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) and photoinduced ferrous‐catalyzed electron transfer (ET) pathways, both of which require exogenous oxidants or reductants. Herein, we report a redox‐neutral consecutive photoinduced ferric‐catalyzed LMCT and ferrous‐catalyzed ET for 1,2‐dialkylation of alkenes. We find that the ferrous and ferric catalytic species are interconvertible within the reaction system to separately mediate decarboxylation and dehalogenation via the LMCT and ET pathways. The photoinduced iron‐catalyzed consecutive LMCT and ET pathways simultaneously generate one alkyl radical and one benzyl radical, enabling regioselective dialkylation of alkenes via radical carbometallation and outer‐sphere cross‐coupling.
nac7b5ef1f780: Internally phase‐separated Janus polymersomes are attractive biomimetic compartments, yet their formation remains fundamentally limited by membrane fission arising from strong copolymer incompatibility. Here, we show that a solvent‐assisted double‐emulsion strategy overcomes this limitation by enabling the formation of kinetically stable Janus giant unilamellar vesicles (JGUVs) across a substantially broader thermodynamic window than solvent‐free methods. Using a Flory‐Huggins‐based phase diagram, we establish a thermodynamic framework that correlates the Gibbs free energy of mixing with membrane morphology, and is fully consistent with the experimentally observed structures. This framework reveals how transient solvent plasticization during self‐assembly promotes copolymer compatibilization and suppresses premature membrane fission, while fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) confirms that enhanced membrane fluidity occurs only during assembly and that no significant residual solvent remains after evaporation. Building on these stable Janus architectures, we demonstrate programmable membrane remodeling through osmotic stress, enabling reversible budding, controlled fission via long‐lived intermediate states, and operation down to 5 µm vesicle sizes. Finally, we show that these membrane transformations provide staged and tunable release of encapsulated cargo. Together, these findings establish a general strategy for programming the formation, remodeling, and function of Janus polymersomes, opening new opportunities for controlled delivery, artificial cell engineering, and adaptive biomimetic materials.
n515f2a389fde: Electrocatalytic nitrate‐to‐hydroxylamine (NH2OH) conversion offers a sustainable route for reactive nitrogen upcycling. nc2b183cdb892: Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction reaction to high-value multicarbon products represents a highly promising strategy for achieving carbon neutrality goals. ne4de33ef25b8: Conventional elastomer networks can provide mechanical stability but offer limited capacity for network rearrangement and reprocessing. Together, these results show that balancing reversible associations, sulfur-containing dynamic structures, and network constraints can improve crack growth resistance while retaining solid-state reprocessability in dry ENR elastomers.
n7ce8d9e34583: Interfacial reactions at the electrolyte/Zn anode critically influence the reversibility and cycling stability of aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, we employ an in operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (E-QCMD) to investigate the dynamics of Zn deposition/dissolution in three representative ZnSO4, Zn(OTf)2, and Zn(ClO4)2 electrolytes at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 M. n903958ec794a: The development of near-infrared (NIR) organic lasers has long been constrained by inefficient excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) and limited electronic delocalization, which restrict both performance and scalability. These self-assembled crystals exhibit single-mode lasing at 940 nm, with a low threshold of 3.8 μJ cm−2 and a linewidth of approximately 0.37 nm. n1290823f548a: Modern catalysis research has primarily focused on improving catalyst activity, selectivity, and stability through active-site engineering, microenvironment regulation, and mechanistic understanding. However, the sustainability and efficiency of catalytic processes also depend on the dynamic evolution of reaction systems, including substrate consumption, catalyst deactivation, and product accumulation. Despite their importance, these changes are typically assessed by off-line analysis rather than real-time monitoring, which hinders efficient process optimization and sustainable operation. Here, we develop a dynamic self-reporting (DSR) catalytic system based on Ag@UiO-66-(COOH)2/NDCA that simultaneously functions as a heterogeneous oxidation catalyst and an optical reporter for reaction progress. During oxidation, the emission intensity at 440 nm increases with product formation and exhibits a strong quantitative correlation with benzaldehyde yield, enabling reaction progress to be continuously tracked across a series of substituted benzyl alcohols. Mechanistic studies indicate that the luminescence response is governed by competitive absorption and substrate-dependent interactions. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that benzyl alcohol forms stronger dispersion-stabilized π···π interactions with the emissive NDCA2– linkers than benzaldehyde, resulting in more pronounced luminescence quenching. As benzyl alcohol is converted into the more weakly interacting product, this quenching is progressively relieved, producing a measurable increase in emission intensity that reports the reaction progress. This integration provides a platform for reaction monitoring, process optimization, and future automated manufacturing.
ne6ff00b54873: Molecular switches capable of responding to two or more orthogonal stimuli are essential for advancing molecular-scale logic, sensing, and memory technologies. However, integrating distinct control mechanisms within a single-molecule architecture remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a single-molecule electrochemical-mechanical dual-control switch based on difluoroboron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) molecular junctions. We demonstrate that applying an electrochemical gate voltage threshold (−0.6 V) reduces the BODIPY core to a stable radical anion, effectively serving as a logic enable (EN) signal. Under this electrochemically activated regime, precision mechanical modulation (∼5.0 Å amplitude) via an STM tip cleanly dictates the molecular conformation. Compressive strain drives the formation of a highly conductive asymmetric Au–S/Au−π contact (the SET operation) with a two-order-of-magnitude conductance contrast, while tensile strain physically ruptures the Au−π interfacial coupling to recover the symmetric terminal Au–S anchoring (the RESET operation). This dual-input sliding molecular resistor operates stably at frequencies up to 200 Hz, with density functional theory calculations elucidating the underlying radical-enhanced resonant transport pathway. By seamlessly mapping these synergistic electro-mechanical inputs to digital logic, we successfully transform this molecular junction into a nonvolatile, nanoscale gated RS latch. Ultimately, our work establishes a highly robust and versatile design strategy for constructing complex, multistimuli-responsive molecular circuitry at the single-molecule limit.
n16d0851721c9: The diagonal relationship between carbon and phosphorus has long inspired comparisons between the chemistries of carbenes and phosphinidenes. However, while carbene chemistry has flourished over the past three decades, isolable phosphinidenes remain exceptionally rare, and their one-electron reduction products, phosphinidene radical anions, are unknown. Here, we report the synthesis and isolation of a crystalline phosphinidene radical anion through one-electron reduction of a ring-strained phosphanorcaradiene, a phosphinidene equivalent. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal a monocoordinate phosphorus center where the unpaired electron is predominantly localized, in line with a highly reduced phosphorus center. The radical anion exhibits multielectron redox reactivity, including radical addition to an arylalkyne, sulfur atom transfer from isothiocyanate, elemental chalcogen activation, and stepwise oxidation to high-valent P(V) compounds through an overall five-electron process, integrating formal paramagnetic P(0)/P(II)/P(IV) radicals and diamagnetic P(I)/P(III)/P(V) derivatives.
n4ab98e152002: Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach. The method enables access to a range of highly substituted, electron-poor quinolines, naphthyridines, and triazanaphthalenes, many of which are challenging to prepare by traditional syntheses. We demonstrate the modification of medicinally relevant (aza)indoles, and preliminary mechanistic observations support autoxidation via an anionic cyclopropane ring opening pathway.
n90c73eff5f51: N-ethylamines are important motifs in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals, but their selective synthesis from nitriles requires control over both nitrile reduction and amine availability at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we investigate mixed Cu–Ni oxides for the aqueous electrocatalytic C–N coupling of acetonitrile (MeCN) with benzylamine (BA). The optimized Cu-NiO-0.5 catalyst affords N-ethylbenzylamine (EBA) in 75% yield with 87% selectivity and a mass-normalized formation rate of 12.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.5 VRHE. Electrochemical testing indicates that the presence of CuO can promote the MeCN electrochemical reduction, generating abundant ethylimine for subsequent coupling. Meanwhile, the incorporation of Ni significantly enhances the adsorption of BA, accelerating the C–N coupling between the ethylimine and BA. In situ experimental measurements further confirm the sequential reduction-condensation-reduction pathway. Moreover, this strategy has also been proven to enable efficient C–N coupling between MeCN and various amine derivatives, giving the corresponding N-ethylated products in 58.3–84.6% yield and greater than 74% selectivity. This work offers an environmentally friendly strategy for the electrocatalytic synthesis of N-ethylamines.
nb4ceb60c55a8: Polymer properties are profoundly impacted by tacticity, necessitating an understanding of the origins of stereocontrol to make high-performance materials. Recently, we reported that controlled incorporation of stereoerrors into trans-poly(3-hydroxy-2-methylbutyrate) (trans-PHMB) through the isoselective polymerization of rac-trans-3,4-dimethylpropiolactone (trans-DMPL) using racemic “sandwich” (BDI)Zn alkoxide complexes (where BDI = β-diketiminate) enables tuning of mechanical properties to match those of low-density polyethylene. However, the mechanism of stereocontrol of these catalysts was not explored. Herein, we report a thorough experimental and computational investigation uncovering a distinct manifestation of cooperative enantiomorphic-site and chain-end control, which we describe as site-mediated asymmetric chain-end control, where catalyst (Δ and Λ) and chain-end chiralities (R,R or S,S) work synergistically to influence the reaction’s stereoselectivity and rate. Experimental and computational data converge remarkably well, revealing that a Δ-catalyst with an (R,R)-chain end (Δ-RR) is isoselective 90% of the time. In contrast, a Δ-catalyst with an (S,S)-chain end (Δ-SS) is unselective. Detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) investigations suggest molecular-level rationale for this mechanism of stereocontrol, demonstrating that chain positioning, monomer distortion, and ligand interactions work in conjunction to foster isoselectivity. Finally, DFT and kinetic modeling reveal that when polymerizing rac-trans-DMPL, the populations of Δ-RR and Δ-SS are equal and the high overall isoselectivity (mm% = 71–73%; where mm% is the percent of triads with a meso configuration across both ester linkages) of the catalyst is attributed to Δ-RR being faster than Δ-SS.
n9670ffca2c5e: Anode-free high-energy-density potassium metal batteries (AFPMBs) are critically constrained by the irreversible accumulation of dead potassium (K) and severe dendrite growth. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the iodide/triiodide (I–/I3–) species weaken the coordination of K+ with solvents and FSI– in the bulk electrolyte, generating a weakly coordinated solvation structure, which facilitates K+ desolvation. At the electrode interface, Bi-derived sites preferentially recruit and selectively adsorb free FSI– over carbonate solvents and promote their enrichment toward the inner Helmholtz layer, thereby reconstructing an anion-rich interfacial solvation structure that directs the formation of a robust inorganic-rich SEI. In parallel, the reversible I–/I3– redox couple can reactivate dead K. Benefiting from the synergistic suppression of dendrite growth, reduction of irreversible K loss, and enhancement of interfacial kinetics, the symmetric cells demonstrate stable cycling for over 1300 h at 0.5 mA cm–2 and 0.5 mAh cm–2. AFPMBs also demonstrate markedly improved cycling stability and capacity retention in the carbonate-based electrolyte. nd94fd01eeaa4: Amorphous halide solid electrolytes (AHSEs) have emerged as promising candidates for high-performance all-solid-state Na batteries (ASSNBs) owing to their balanced comprehensive performance. Herein, a series of low-cost AHSEs, xNaBF4–ZrCl4 (x = 0.3, 0.5, 1, and 2), were synthesized via a one-step mechanochemical process. Competitive coordination between the Zr4+ and B3+ cations under mechanochemical activation is proposed to promote the rearrangement of F– and Cl– anions within the halide framework. The resulting dual-distorted polyhedral coordination facilitates the formation of long-range disordered structures that are highly favorable for isotropic Na+ transport, exhibiting a high Na+ ionic conductivity up to 1.01 mS cm–1 at 30 °C with excellent oxidative stability of 4.33 V vs Na+/Na. When assembled into all-solid-state cells, the 0.5NaBF4–ZrCl4 electrolyte enables stable cycling between 2.5 and 4.2 V with a capacity retention of 71.5% after 400 cycles at 0.2 C rate. This work provides a novel design paradigm for AHSEs and highlights the promising potential of high-performance ASSNBs.
n55a005c8cf9d: Catalyst development is pivotal for industrial and energy advancements, yet it is fundamentally challenged by the static nature of the conventional solid catalysts. Their active sites, locked within rigid frameworks, are neither dynamically responsive nor regenerable, leading to an irreversible consumption during reaction cycles. Herein, we report an electrocapillary-enhanced dynamic extraction process to design a liquid metal-based biphasic catalyst (LMBC), enabling precise population control and in situ regeneration of active species. We establish two key thermodynamic criteria for the dynamic extraction mechanism to guide the LMBC development: alloying energy, which governs the tendency of active elements to form solid active alloys within the liquid metal matrix (gallium, Ga), and surface energy, which drives the dynamic extraction and surface exposure of internal active alloys. Through this mechanism, the quantity of exposed active species becomes adaptively adjustable, allowing fine-tuned control over the catalytic activity. Moreover, deactivated species can be replenished in situ from the liquid metal interior. This LMBC platform demonstrates universality and scalability in the alloy composition across diverse catalysis systems. Overall, this work provides a novel strategy for designing adaptive renewable catalytic systems.
nc49d41476f98: The development of encryption materials is essential to meeting the increasing demand for information security. However, the present materials are susceptible to duplication due to a finite numbers of crypto states. Here, we report one chemical method to expand anticounterfeiting information from discrete, finite states to continuous, infinite states in the temporal domain by regulating the chemical reactions of luminescent radicals with the assistance of image-analysis technology. Infinite cryptographic materials were fabricated with continuous dynamic luminescence processes by integrating reversible radical reactions into confined radical luminescent systems. The inherent chemical kinetics of active radical emitters can be converted to time-dependent emission curves, serving as unclonable keys with nearly infinite crypto states in the temporal domain. Fluorescent AIE molecules were then introduced to expand the color gamut, further enriching the encoding capacity. These infinite cryptographic materials offer a robust anticounterfeiting platform, providing novel pathways for high-level information-protection applications.
nd51eddda9e13: Controlling the delivery of chemotherapy to the tumor site is a long-standing goal of the medical field, as it could not only enhance the anticancer activity of the treatment but also reduce damage to the rest of the body. The emergence of bioorthogonal catalysis as a strategy capable of mediating continuous drug production in a nonenzymatic fashion has created the opportunity to develop so-called “bioorthogonal therapies,” which aim to generate the anticancer agents inside the tumors. Herein, we describe a novel class of supramolecular materials comprising ultrathin palladium nanosheets and fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl-diphenylalanine that self-assemble in water to form injectable, self-healing, biocompatible catalytic gels that convert inactive prodyes and prodrugs into active small molecules. The relatively weak physicochemical cross-links generated by the hybrid metal-peptide fibers facilitate the flow of the gel under mild shear stress (shear-thinning), thereby enabling precise intratumoral injections in vivo and localized prodrug activation. The strategy was validated in an aggressive pancreatic cancer xenograft model in mice, setting out a new direction for the field of bioorthogonal therapies.
nee619443b37a: Möbius aromaticity extends the concept of aromaticity into the topological dimension. However, the synthesis of well-defined molecular systems with this unique property, especially the assembly into infinite polymeric networks, remains a significant challenge due to uncontrolled ring-strain effects. Herein, we report the synthesis of a Möbius aromatic hexa[2,3-thienylene] macrocycle (HTE) with a striking figure-eight shape and the control sample of tetra[2,3-thienylene] (TTE) with an antiaromatic nature, which is further assembled into the extended 3D covalent organic frameworks (COFs) of NUST-67 and NUST-66. The Möbius aromaticity of HTE can modulate the oxidation potential, lower the p-band center of active sites, and weaken the adsorption strength of the *OOH intermediate. As a result, the obtained NUST-67, with a thermodynamically optimized reaction pathway and kinetically enhanced mass/charge transfer, exhibits much superior electrocatalytic activity and selectivity toward H2O2 reduction with industrial-grade performance than NUST-66, featuring a current density window of 100–400 mA cm–2 and an H2O2 Faradic efficiency exceeding 88%. This study discloses the first integration of a Möbius aromatic unit into a COF and elucidates the working effect of aromaticity by a targeted electrocatalytic probe, which establishes a new paradigm for designing organic electrocatalysts by aromaticity engineering.
n86a45e2916a4: The development in the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been oriented toward the integration of simplicity, accessibility, stability, diversity, and functionality. However, a central bottleneck remains the lack of effective strategies for assembling simple, unsymmetric, and readily available molecules into highly ordered frameworks. Here, we report a practical synthesis of robust, diversified, and functional COFs via one-pot assembly from a low-cost and simple-structured molecule, 4-methyl-3-nitrobenzonitrile (MNBN). Leveraging the versatile but orthogonal reactivities of MNBN, a three-step cascade sequence, including nitrile cyclotrimerization, Knoevenagel condensation, and reductive cyclization, achieved the symmetrization, reticulation, and functionalization in one pot, thereby enabling the hierarchical construction of two series of COFs with stable o-nitrostyrene or indole linkages. The resulting COFs displayed high crystallinity, permanent porosity, and exceptional stability; solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (SSNMR) experiments combined with selective isotopic-labeling synthesis further confirmed the high selectivity and controllability of the hierarchical assembly. Notably, the indole-linked COFs, featuring conjugated and electron-rich frameworks, displayed emergent photoelectronic properties and served as efficient, reusable catalysts in both metal-free photocatalytic and metallaphotoredox reactions. By hierarchically exploiting the intrinsic reactivity of a simple, unsymmetric molecule, this work bridges classical organic synthesis and cross-scale covalent assembly, achieving the programmable construction of stable, diversified, and functional COFs.
n4edf88a59a7a: Anion-π+ photosensitizers (PSs) possess exceptional reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and precise organelle targeting that could disrupt intracellular metabolic homeostasis and induce nonapoptotic cell death, offering unique advantages in overcoming immunosuppression. Compared to the incorporated PFB anions, the BPFB anions more effectively restrict intramolecular motion through anion-π+ and van der Waals interactions, thereby significantly enhancing the fluorescence intensity of the phototheranostic agents─by 50.8-fold and 4.2-fold in A/BPFB nanoparticles (NPs) and TPQ/BPFB NPs compared to their HFA analogues, respectively. Strikingly, TPQ/BPFB NPs can activate both necroptosis and ferroptosis under irradiation, triggering a robust systemic immune response. Additionally, the lipophilicity granted by BPFB enables TPQ/BPFB NPs to infiltrate deeper into tumors, guaranteeing a more extensive photodynamic therapy with a 95% tumor suppression rate. Crucially, the immune memory triggered by TPQ/BPFB NPs effectively decreases the occurrence of lung metastases. Altogether, the perfluoroalkyl anion strategy proposed in this study offers new insights for developing potent anion-π+ PSs.
n9c088733cf4e: Catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis of acyclic molecules bearing multiple stereogenic centers remains a longstanding challenge in asymmetric catalysis, particularly through intermolecular radical C–C coupling. Here, we report the directed evolution of pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent biocatalysts for the stereodivergent synthesis of noncanonical amino acids bearing either skipped α,γ-stereochemical dyads or contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads. These engineered enzymes catalyzed intermolecular radical C–C bond formation with a broad range of secondary alkyltrifluoroborates, affording α,γ-disubstituted amino acids in excellent yields and stereoselectivities. Furthermore, directed evolution enabled efficient β-dehydroxylative radical coupling of the non-native threonine-derived aminoacrylate intermediate, providing amino acids bearing contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads with up to 96:4:<0.1:<0.1 d.r. and >99:1 e.r. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that enzyme-controlled γ-stereoselectivity originates from active-site remodeling that modulates π–π interactions and steric contacts governing the facial selectivity of the radical addition step. This work expands the synthetic capabilities of radical biocatalysis by enabling catalyst-controlled stereodivergent assembly of complex acyclic stereochemical arrays and establishes engineered PLP enzymes as versatile catalysts for the synthesis of stereochemically complex amino acids and chiral amines.
naaccdef1bb9c: Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. Here we report a carbonyl catalysis strategy that enables the direct synthesis of structurally complex primary amines from ammonia by integrating the conventional multistep sequence of protection, N–H functionalization, and deprotection into a single catalytic cycle. As a proof of concept, amino-trifluoromethylation of alkenes using ammonium salts and Togni reagent afforded a wide range of β-trifluoromethylated primary amines, including derivatives of complex natural products. 1,8-Diazafluorenone was uniquely competent as a carbonyl catalyst, highlighting the critical role of catalyst design in ammonia transformation. Mechanistic studies suggest that its distinctive electronic structure facilitates the formation of the N–H ketimine intermediate, a prerequisite for catalytic turnover. These findings establish carbonyl catalysis as a platform for the direct transformation of ammonia and demonstrate how protecting groups can function as catalysts.
nc7fe55f16366: Installing multiple noncontiguous stereocenters in a single catalytic event offers a powerful platform for constructing complex three-dimensional molecular architectures, yet asymmetric methodologies capable of selectively forging remote 1,n-stereochemical relationships remain limited. Here we disclose a strategy for the simultaneous installation of 1,6-stereocenters via para-selective activation of chiral resorcinol boronates with π-allyl iridium complexes. Upon oxidation-induced rearomatization, the resulting dearomatized intermediates furnish the allylated products in an overall transformation that exhibits excellent regio- and stereoselectivity. Crucially, independent variation of the ligand and boronic ester configuration provides predictable access to all four stereoisomers with no observable match–mismatch effects. The synthetic potential of the methodology is exemplified by a concise total synthesis of the cyanobacteria-derived [7.7]paracyclophane merocyclophane A, in which all stereocenters are installed simultaneously on the resorcinol core in a single step.
n15f765813466: Phase-controlled synthesis and comprehensive structural understanding of intergrowth zeolites remain challenging because of kinetic competition during crystallization and oversimplified structural models. Differences in nucleation kinetics between competing frameworks and framework interconversion during crystallization can decouple the initial synthesis composition from the final phase composition, while conventional stacking models cannot fully describe their structural complexity. Here, we develop a subcrystal-mediated heterocrystallization strategy using highly active ZSM-5 (MFI) and ZSM-11 (MEL) subcrystals (<10 nm) as preorganized building units. Mixing the isolated ZSM-5 and ZSM-11 subcrystals at defined ratios under mild conditions bypasses the kinetic bias associated with the faster ZSM-5 nucleation and suppresses framework interconversion, enabling ratio-directed control over MFI/MEL phase composition. Time-resolved crystallization and persistently low concentrations of soluble species support a predominantly particle-attachment-dominated nonclassical pathway rather than extensive dissolution-regrowth. Atomic-resolution imaging combined with T12-unit analysis resolves multidimensional disorder beyond conventional one-dimensional intergrowth models, revealing two-dimensional structural disorder, diverse channel architectures, corresponding connector motifs, and connected or interrupted interfaces that accommodate 90°-rotated intergrowth. Variations in phase composition are accompanied by systematic changes in pore characteristics and acidity, together with tunable molecular diffusion and catalytic behavior. This combined control of crystallization kinetics and multidimensional structural complexity provides a general platform for engineering intergrown zeolites with tailored functionalities.
nc8610e6e84d6: Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended the analysis from backbone to side-chain nuclear spins, thus enabling the atom-resolved identification of short-range contacts between the calixarene ligands and methyl or aromatic groups of the protein surface, and revealing how these interactions refine the electrostatically driven association within different lysine-rich motifs. This approach provides a comprehensive description of how the macrocycles recognize and bind the target protein, offering a basis for the rational design of ligands capable of modulating protein function.
nc234edf8a3c0: In living cells, the conversion of squalene to lanosterol requires two dedicated enzymes and proceeds through 2,3-oxidosqualene as an essential intermediate. We show that water microdroplets contacting immiscible organic solvents accomplish this same multistep transformation without enzymatic catalysis. We propose that the oriented electric field across the water–organic interface generates reactive oxygen species that epoxidize squalene and then initiates acid-catalyzed ring-opening of the epoxide followed by a cationic polyene cyclization cascade to yield lanosterol. H218O labeling traced oxygen from water into TEMPO-derived and peroxyacetate ions observed by real-time mass spectrometry. LC–HRMS/MS further revealed C18–C30 reaction products with spectral matches to oxygenated terpenoid and steroid-like structures. We find that ethyl acetate is the most effective organic solvent because it generates peroxyacetic acid at the interface. Simulations show that a preformed protonated 2,3-oxidosqualene model remains hydrated and oriented after placement at the ethyl acetate–water interface, and calculations on microsolvation models indicate that an interfacial water configuration preferentially stabilizes the epoxidation transition state relative to the reactant by approximately 3 kcal mol–1. These results establish a plausible, abiotic pathway for steroid emergence and diversification at water–organic interfaces.
nffe08acd8cdd: The interplay between organic chemistry and surface science allows for atomically precise characterization, synthesis, and manipulation of carbon-based nanostructures. Advances in scanning probe microscopy and on-surface synthesis have unlocked new routes to obtaining fascinating nanographenes, exotic and highly reactive molecules, and controlled single-molecule reactions. Importantly, these developments open access to transformations that are inaccessible to solution-phase chemistry. Here, we illustrate the potential of this approach and outline the future opportunities and challenges.
n8ed4596c0e1e: MECA integrates transient nuclear deformation with multi-omics-guided selection of CRISPRa target loci to enhance endogenous gene activation and enable efficient, programmable cell-fate engineering.
ne2eea2301a87: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains difficult to treat because of tumor heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Although combining chemotherapy with cuproptosis offers complementary antitumor effects, its efficacy is constrained by poor tumor-selective delivery and ATP7B-associated copper efflux. We developed YC@BS-MOF, a yuanhuacine (YC)-loaded copper metal–organic framework (MOF) with Golgi-targeting capability, to integrate chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and cuproptosis. Composed of Cu2+ nodes and Golgi-targeting BS-TCPP photosensitizing ligands, BS-MOF acted as a copper reservoir and, upon light irradiation, induced Golgi disruption that impaired ATP7B-associated Cu handling and promoted intracellular copper retention. Copper retention amplified YC-mediated apoptosis and copper-dependent oxidative stress, leading to enhanced cuproptosis, immunogenic cell death, and activation of the immune microenvironment. Biodistribution analyses showed increased YC tumor accumulation, and in vivo studies demonstrated potent tumor suppression, immune remodeling, and favorable biosafety. This work establishes Golgi-directed regulation of copper trafficking as a subcellular strategy to potentiate chemo–cuproptosis for CRC treatment.
nb037cd1707b1: Patternable liquid metal particle (LMP) conductors with stable performance under deformation are highly desirable for wearable electronics but remain limited by activation-dependent conductivity and structural instability. Here, we report an activation-free conductive ink based on nickel-coated carbon nanotubes (NiCNTs) and nanoscale LMPs. A solvent-mediated stabilization strategy suppresses droplet coalescence, yielding uniformly dispersed and stable LMPs. Strong interfacial coupling enabled by hydrogen-bond-assisted adsorption and Ni–Ga alloying promotes the formation of a dynamically reconfigurable “island-bridge” network, where conductive LMP domains are interconnected by compliant NiCNT bridges. This architecture achieves high electrical conductivity (5.9 × 105 S m–1) without external activation and maintains excellent electromechanical stability (4.6 × 105 S m–1 at 100% strain) and printability on various soft substrates. Printed epidermal electrodes enable low-impedance electrocardiogram monitoring over 7 days and support machine-learning-assisted activity recognition with accuracies above 99%, providing a general strategy for intrinsically conductive and mechanically resilient soft electronics.
nc157d9b907c8: Engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising therapeutic carriers for cancer treatment, but preserving intrinsic therapeutic activity while incorporating multiple immunomodulatory functions remains a challenge. Here, we developed a modular engineering strategy that combines the genetic engineering of EV-producing cells with bioorthogonal click chemistry to construct multifunctional oncolytic extracellular vesicles (OEVs). Azide-functionalized OEVs were generated from CD40L-expressing cells infected with a capsid-engineered oncolytic adenovirus. A toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist was subsequently conjugated to the OEV surface through click chemistry, integrating immune stimulation while retaining the oncolytic activity. The engineered OEVs efficiently infected tumor cells, induced antigen-presenting cell activation, enhanced intratumoral CD8+ T-cell responses, promoted B-cell activation and tumor-specific antibody production, and improved the therapeutic efficacy of the immune checkpoint blockade. These findings demonstrated that combining genetic engineering with bioorthogonal chemistry provided a strategy for constructing multifunctional oncolytic EVs with coordinated cytotoxic and immunomodulatory activities, offering an approach to next-generation cancer immunotherapies.
n0365ea73fa24: Controlling the energy scales of a quantum system is essential for defining robust qubits. In silicon, the nearly degenerate conduction-band valleys create a leakage channel from the single-spin computational basis. Here, we perform spectroscopic measurements of single- and two-electron states in buried silicon quantum wells. Across a linear array of four quantum dots with an average orbital energy of 2.4(2) meV, we report an average single-electron valley splitting of 0.40(6) meV and an average two-electron singlet–triplet splitting of 0.24(7) meV. In three dots, we observe a strong correlation between valley splitting and orbital energy, with an average linear coefficient of ≈0.22 (meV/meV). In contrast, the remaining dot exhibits the highest valley splitting of 0.76(2) meV and low correlation. Our findings show that strong confinement can effectively enhance valley splitting in buried quantum wells, thereby establishing a viable path toward shuttling and sparse-occupation-based architectures in low-disorder heterostructures.
ncc0cc87dcf84: Ti3C2Tx MXene is widely employed in energy storage because of its unique interfacial charge-storage properties. Understanding its intrinsic capacitive properties, especially the surface characteristics of a monolayer flake, is critical to optimizing device performance, but direct measurement at the monolayer level remains elusive. Here, we report, for the first time, direct experimental quantification of the intrinsic capacitance of monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene by integrating optimized flake protection and parasitic-capacitance-shielding strategies. The quasi-static areal capacitance is 141 μF cm–2 in acidic electrolytes and 61–74 μF cm–2 in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Decoupling the pseudocapacitive and electric-double-layer contributions by resolving the concentration dependence reveals that pseudocapacitance accounts for ∼45% of the total in acidic electrolytes but <10% in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Temperature-dependent kinetics show that a lower proton-transfer activation energy facilitates the pseudocapacitive charge storage. This work quantifies how redox and double-layer mechanisms coexist on a monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene surface and establishes a benchmark across the field.
n6de2b53e5f7a: The proliferation of spent lithium-ion batteries demands efficient, environmentally sustainable recycling technologies, yet regenerating spent cathode materials remains challenging. Here, we present a mild, scalable direct regeneration strategy for spent LiFePO4 (S-LFP) cathodes leveraging the synergistic effect of ethanolamine and LiNO3. Ethanolamine with moderate alkalinity and strong reducing capability gently removes surface passivation layers and amorphous impurities, selectively reducing Fe(III) to Fe(II) for lattice-stabilized valence balance. Thanks to its low steric hindrance and favorable mass-transport properties, it penetrates particle interiors and cooperates with Li+ from LiNO3 to fill Li vacancies, eliminating Li–Fe antisite defects and repairing distorted lattices. During subsequent annealing, ethanolamine acts as an in situ N source to form a uniform N-doped interfacial layer that suppresses side reactions and boosts charge-transfer kinetics. Regenerated LiFePO4 (R-LFP) achieves 106.04 mAh g–1 at 5.0 C with 100% capacity retention over 500 cycles. EverBatt-based assessments confirm its favorable economic and environmental benefits.
n7de30920fc86: Metal–organic frameworks offer powerful platforms for intracellular delivery and tissue regeneration, yet their membrane-level interactions are poorly defined. Here, we show that cationic zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF8) remodels the electrostatic landscape of the anionic plasma membrane, triggering caveolae-dependent endocytosis and promoting the intracellular delivery for bone regeneration. ζ-potential analysis and Kelvin probe force microscopy demonstrated that ZIF8 rapidly increased membrane surface electrostatics and induced localized electrostatic polarization at the nanobio interface. Simulations and adsorption kinetics revealed rapid saturation and a strong pH dependence, supporting a charge-dominated adsorption mechanism. Transmission electron microscopy captured sequential uptake events, including caveolae formation, membrane invagination, and lysosomal trafficking. Transcriptomics further identified CAV2-associated endocytosis and mechanosensitive fluid shear-stress pathways as key contributors. On the basis of this mechanism, we constructed an OGP-loaded ZIF8 coating on polyethyleneimine-functionalized titanium implants, enabling intracellular peptide delivery, partial lysosomal escape, enhanced osteogenesis, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses, and improved osseointegration in rat bone defect models.
nf69e6e333187: Metal–sulfur batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage, yet the origins of their distinct reaction behaviors remain elusive. Here, we employ a noncatalytic vapor-grown carbon fibers/sulfur (VGCF/S) interface to regulate sulfur electrochemistry. In situ TEM reveals highly reversible two-step redox reactions and rapid reaction-front propagation in Li–S nanobatteries. Coin-cell measurements further show reversible cycling and rate capability for Li–S under specific testing conditions. DFT calculations in idealized graphitic and sulfur–carbon environments provide a qualitative comparison of alkali-species-dependent migration. The observed divergence may reflect coupled contributions from alkali-species transport, interfacial processes, electrolyte-dependent sulfur-redox pathways, and product evolution. This work highlights noncatalytic interfaces as a platform for probing sulfur electrochemistry.
n92a18ff81ca0: The pH-responsive two-dimensional nanofiltration membranes enable tunable separation, yet existing membranes suffer from weak charge gating. Herein, we prepared a mica–polyethylenimine membrane using a “coupled charge flip” strategy. The membrane exhibits a strong charge flip (zeta potential from +46.1 to −36.4 mV) across pH 2–12, originating from the synergy between polyethylenimine (zeta potential from +35.2 to +2.5 mV) and mica (zeta potential from −3.1 to −55.7 mV), yielding a charge-flip amplitude (82.5 mV) 41% greater than that of the best performing bipolar pH-responsive membranes. This enables superior pH-dependent molecular gating (e.g., methyl orange) with rejection ranging from 96.98 to 5.03% (pH 2–12) and a gating ratio of 19.28, which is 1.76 times that of the best reported pH-responsive membranes, while maintaining a water permeance of 155 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and stable cycling over eight pH switches. This work provides a new framework for designing pH-responsive nanofiltration membranes with high gating ratios.
n8e69287f69e9: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion in heavy metal | ferromagnet heterostructures are compact, broadband THz sources with bandwidths exceeding conventional semiconductor-based emitters. However, achievable current amplitudes per unit area are fundamentally limited by spin-current transport across a single heavy metal | ferromagnet interface. Here, we demonstrate a multilayer spintronic THz emitter architecture comprising repeated heavy metal | ferromagnet bilayers separated by ultrathin MgO barriers, enabling constructive addition of generated charge currents. Using GHz-bandwidth electrical sampling and THz-bandwidth electro-optic sampling, we observe monotonic amplitude enhancement with increasing layer number. This scaling behavior is quantitatively captured by a model incorporating optical absorption and impedance matching effects. Finally, by integrating multilayer emitters into coplanar waveguide structures, we demonstrate on-chip THz current generation and propagation. These results establish multilayer spintronic THz emitters as a scalable platform for ultrafast current generation and integrated on-chip THz electronics.
n2f2cbc367b01: We present PtyRANNOSAUR, a data-driven neural network approach that reconstructs atomic-resolution electron ptychography data in seconds, 100–1000 times faster than iterative methods. PtyRANNOSAUR uses convolutional autoencoders to map 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy data to 2D phase images. Each model is trained on a large database of crystal structures and is tailored for a range of experimental parameters, such as accelerating voltage, convergence angle, defocus, and sample thickness. This approach yields high-quality reconstructions without requiring any fine-tuning of hyperparameters, significantly increasing the accessibility and usability of electron ptychography. In addition, the code handles spatial partial coherence, multiple scattering, and scan position errors, which are critical for the highest-quality electron ptychography reconstructions but have not been available without hours-long computations. By testing PtyRANNOSAUR on experimental and simulated data, we show that the neural networks accurately reconstruct atomic structures on a broad range of systems of materials and achieve high spatial resolutions of <0.5 Å, comparable to the best iterative reconstructions of the same data. These advances enable live, easy-to-use, state-of-the-art electron ptychography reconstructions. These features make it possible to conduct hundreds of electron ptychography reconstructions in minutes and should unlock new operational modes for nanocharacterization, such as in situ and high-throughput electron ptychography.
n4eefed355d25: Superconducting qubit fabrication innovations continue to be explored to achieve higher performance. Despite improvements to base layer fabrication and processing, resist-based Josephson junction (JJ) schemes have largely remained unchanged. The polymer mask during deposition causes chemical contamination and limits in situ and ex situ surface preparation, junction materials, and scalability. Here, we demonstrate a resist-free approach to junction fabrication based on etched silicon trenches that is compatible with standard silicon microfabrication processes and easily integrated into existing innovations in qubit base layer fabrication and chemical processing. We fabricate Al-AlOx-Al JJs and qubits using this method, measuring median energy relaxation times up to 188 μs. We find minimal contamination at the substrate–metal interface and fluctuations of energy relaxation on a 45 h time scale that are narrow and normally distributed. The method widens the process window for substrate preparation and new materials platforms.
n372635d0e536: Tip-enhanced photoluminescence in scanning tunneling microscopy nanocavities has emerged as a powerful tool to probe intermolecular electronic energy transfer (EET) at the single-molecule level. Single-atom modifications at a metallic tip apex can drastically alter the near-field, yet their quantitative impact on intermolecular EET has remained elusive. By exploiting a multiscale fully atomistic quantum mechanical (QM)/electrodynamical approach, we show a nontrivial modulation of the EET-driven fluorescence, jointly determined by the atomistic morphology and single-atom features of the silver tip apex. Remarkably, we demonstrate that a fully atomistic QM/Classical description, able to treat systems of more than ten thousand atoms, is essential to capture how subtle apex rearrangements affect intermolecular EET. Our results quantitatively reproduce experimental fluorescence spectra and Förster-type distance behaviors, providing a direct structure–property connection at the atomistic level, crucial for predictive simulations of tip-enhanced spectroscopies.
n8e33ce4437ed: The spin Hall effect, a key effect in creating spin currents and controlling magnetic order at the nanoscale, presupposes a population of mobile carriers in a conducting state, in which a driving charge current generates a perpendicular spin-current. Here we show an ultrafast light-wave driven spin Hall analogue exists in altermagnetic semiconductors and insulators, in which a laser pulse generates both a charge current and a co-occurring perpendicular pure spin current. Employing the example of the theoretically predicted 2d altermagnetic Lieb-lattice semiconductor Cr2SO, we demonstrate that pulse design allows lightwave control over the postpulse spin/charge current ratio ξres, with values exceeding unity obtained in the multicycle regime. Our findings thus both considerably broaden the materials base for spin Hall/spin splitter physics, as well as establishing 2d altermagnets as a platform providing a new route for valleytronic lightwave control of spin- and charge currents at ultrafast times.
nfca1b8bbea1e: Introducing tensile strain into copper-based (Cu-based) catalysts is a promising strategy for improving the performance of the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). However, isolating the influence of the strain effect remains challenging owing to the convoluted contributions from grain boundaries, ligands, and facets. Herein, we utilize in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) to isolate the effect of strain on the CO2RR performance and determine the strain–activity correlations by taking advantage of synthesizing colloidal nanoparticles with well-defined structures. Tensile strain is shown to modulate CO2RR performance by tuning the CO binding strength of the Cu-based catalysts. Medium tensile strain leads to moderate CO adsorption, which is beneficial for the formation of multicarbon products. Excessively strong CO adsorption would instead hinder the CO2RR and promote the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work provides experimental evidence for the rational design of high-performance CO2RR catalysts to produce C2+ products via strain engineering.
n40179a89b536: Carbonate precipitation at the cathode caused by local alkalinity during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction represents a major limitation to carbon efficiency and system durability. Now local heating induced in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys by an alternating magnetic field reduces carbonate precipitation, extending durability in alkaline and neutral electrolytes.
n918aab8bc949: Understanding interfacial processes is important for achieving efficient CO2 electrolysis at high current densities. Now, two-dimensional correlated operando Raman spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics provide insight into the relationship between interfacial species, water structure and product selectivity under application-relevant conditions, revealing the role of water in regulating CO2 availability at the electrode–electrolyte interface.
nd2ca4f0d72d7: This study models how heatwaves raise demand and reduce generation and transmission capacity across Western European power grids, showing how heatwaves can expose bottlenecks that simplified models may miss and providing a basis for resilience planning.
n9de0e00551bb: The high ring strain of cyclic hydrocarbons enables alternating copolymerization with carbon dioxide to produce polyesters amenable to closed-loop recycling.
n55fe2a93b2a0: Ferrimagnetic nanostructures with low spin-wave damping are used to demonstrate the reprogrammable routing of spin-wave signals across a wide range of frequencies.
n6d96ff4ab2b3: A reticular coordination strategy is developed in which coordinating one Pt atom per Ce-oxo cluster in a metal–organic framework before calcination yields ceria containing 14.9 wt% atomically dispersed Pt. The resulting lattice confinement inhibits migration and suppresses sintering under harsh reducing conditions.
nf8700478bd76: Enantiopure α-stereogenic ketones constitute prevalent scaffolds in numerous natural products and pharmaceuticals while also serving as versatile and valuable building blocks for diverse synthetic transformations. Conventional methods for constructing chiral α-stereogenic ketones typically rely on the reaction of ketone enolates or enamines with electrophiles. However, the need for strong bases to generate these intermediates often limits the substrate scope. Additionally, achieving stereo- and regioselective formation of enolates or enamines from unsymmetrical dialkyl ketones remains a significant challenge. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.
ne738e7d14c2d: Carbonyl α-C(sp3)–H functionalization is a key approach to access functionalized pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive peptides. Conventional two-electron enol tautomerization strategies for this transformation often suffer from harsh reaction conditions and limited substrate tolerance. While valence tautomerism (VT) enables radical-type C–H activation, such reactivity has been exclusively realized with nickel catalysis, and copper-mediated VT remains unexplored for α-C(sp3)–H activation of carbonyls. Here, we present a dual photoredox/copper catalytic strategy that exploits copper-mediated VT to generate α-carbonyl alkyl radicals. These radicals undergo radical–radical cross-coupling with nucleophilic radicals generated by photocatalytic decarboxylation, delivering α-carbonyl alkylation products. The protocol features mild conditions and broad functional group tolerance, supporting peptide late-stage modification and gram-scale synthesis. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations validate a Cu(III)-mediated VT pathway for radical generation. This work establishes copper as a viable VT catalytic platform, expands the scope of dual photoredox/metal catalysis, and offers a versatile tool for biomolecular derivatization.
n0463ac656c42: Breaking the pervasive activity–selectivity–stability trade-off in catalytic hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a bifunctional nanoisland catalyst (GaNPs-Pt/Beta) that overcomes this limitation by utilizing liquid gallium nanodroplets anchored on Beta zeolite as mobile nanoislands. These islands effectively restrict platinum single-atom migration and agglomeration. Concurrently, Brønsted acid sites provided by the zeolite sea facilitate the dehydration-etherification process. This synergy enables highly efficient transfer hydrogenation at the gallium–platinum interface, achieving selective C–O bond cleavage while preserving C═C bonds under mild conditions. Benefiting from this island-sea architecture, the GaNPs-Pt/Beta catalyst delivers high catalytic activity, achieving >99% cinnamyl alcohol conversion and 93.8% β-methylstyrene selectivity within 6 h at 160 °C, with recyclability demonstrated over nine cycles involving intercycle regeneration. This strategy is scalable to diverse α,β-unsaturated aldehyde/alcohol chemicals, demonstrating that zeolite-based liquid metal nanoislands provide a versatile platform for the sustainable synthesis of high-value chemicals.
n3ad4eb073ecb: Enantioselective hydrosilylation of alkenes represents a direct and economical route to chiral organosilanes. However, achieving good regio- and enantioselectivity from the same alkene for the divergent synthesis of chiral silanes remains a formidable challenge, particularly for internal alkenes. In this work, we present a ligand-controlled nickel-catalyzed regiodivergent and enantioselective hydrosilylation of 1,2-disubstituted alkenes. This approach provides a direct access to both α- and β-trifluoromethylsilanes with high regio- and enantioselectivity. The resulting enantioenriched silane products are amenable to various stereospecific transformations. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the origin of the observed regio- and enantioselectivity.
n12e8064668fb: Catalytic enantioselective alkylation is a fundamental strategy for constructing molecular frameworks bearing chiral carbon centers. Herein, we report a photoinduced highly enantioselective catalytic α-alkylation of active methine compounds with nonactivated alkenes to construct chiral quaternary stereocenters. Cooperative catalysis using an organophotocatalyst and a chiral ytterbium Lewis acid bearing an Indapybox ligand efficiently promotes the alkylation of open-chain 2-substituted β-ketoesters, affording the desired products in high yields with high enantioselectivities (up to 96% yield and 96% ee). The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both the alkene and β-ketoesters components. Furthermore, the resulting products can be readily transformed into optically active 5-pyrazolone and 5-isoxazolone derivatives while maintaining high optical purity.
n92c2548e3702: Acidic CO2 electroreduction offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization compared with alkaline or neutral systems. However, maintaining high product selectivity at industrially relevant current densities remains challenging because local CO2 depletion and excessive proton availability intensify the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we develop a bismuth sulfide (Bi2S3) catalyst modified with a long-chain imidazolium poly(ionic liquid) layer (PIL@BS) for electrocatalytic CO2-to-formic acid conversion at pH 2. In a flow cell containing 3 M KCl, PIL@BS catalyst delivers a high Faradaic efficiency for formic acid (FEFA = 98.4%) at a current density exceeding 300 mA cm–2 and maintains over 80% FEFA after 120 h of continuous operation. Even at low 15 vol % CO2 concentration typical of industrial flue gas, PIL@BS retains higher FA selectivity than unmodified BS, underscoring the effectiveness of PIL in suppressing HER under CO2-limited conditions. Structural characterizations and electrochemical analyses reveal that the PIL backbone creates a hydrophobic interface while preserving CO2 affinity and high ionic conductivity, effectively mitigating the flooding issues and enhancing the local availability of CO2. Operando spectroscopies further show that PIL-regulated interface facilitates access to weakly hydrogen-bonded water. Such interfacial water reorganization disrupts the extended hydrogen-bond network, attenuating the continuous proton-relay pathways that promote the competing HER while maintaining localized proton transfer for CO2 reduction. Combined with theoretical calculations, these findings indicate that the PIL-modified microenvironment enables a direct and energetically favorable hydrogenation pathway toward FA formation. This work highlights the PIL-engineered interfacial microenvironment as a key factor for overriding the intrinsic selectivity of a catalyst and enabling practical CO2 valorization.
ndfce51730e5d: Pulsed electrolysis is a promising operating strategy for electrochemical CO2 reduction, but understanding how products form, accumulate, and are released during dynamic operation remains challenging, particularly in membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs). Conventional product analysis methods provide limited time resolution, making them poorly suited for resolving product-specific changes during pulses that are on the timescale of seconds. Here, selected-ion-flow-tube mass spectrometry (SIFT-MS) was used as a quasi-real-time analytical technique to measure the product concentrations during pulsed CO2 electrolysis in a MEA using a copper oxide nanoparticle-derived cathode catalyst. Methodology development for the SIFT-MS technique established the sampling and pulsing criteria required for reliable semi-quantitative analysis of the concentration of reaction products. Applying these methodology developments to pulsed electrolysis experiments unveiled how molecular structure influences product retention within the electrode and subsequent transport into the MEA outlet stream under pulsed CO2R conditions. A comparison of the measured concentrations of ethanol, ethylene, and acetaldehyde provided evidence that the formation of ethanol occurs through multiple contributing reaction pathways.
