na37558c52271: By creating permanent cavities of well-defined size and shape within a fluid, porous liquids bring the precise control over gases afforded by microporous solids to the realm of liquids. Here, we reflect on how the porous liquid concept, beyond simply imparting fluidity to a porous solid, provides a promising platform for overcoming long-standing challenges with manipulating dissolved gases.
n465e258842c4: Silver-catalyzed ethylene epoxidation is a cornerstone of the chemical industry, yet the operando surface structure of Ag nanoparticles and the identity of selectivity-governing active sites remain elusive. Here, we integrate machine learning potentials, stochastic surface walking global optimization, molecular dynamics simulation, and statistical analysis to resolve the surface landscape of Ag nanoparticles approaching experimentally relevant sizes under reaction conditions. Oxygen-induced reconstruction transforms pristine Ag facets into a globally amorphous oxide layer composed of three types of locally ordered ring motifs interspersed with structural defects. A pentagonal motif (ring5), topologically required to accommodate nanoparticle curvature and absent in conventional slab models, dominates the surface across all investigated particle sizes. Its recessed central Ag atom acts as an electronic charge buffer that weakens the critical C–Ag bond in the oxametallacycle intermediate, conferring high intrinsic ethylene oxide selectivity. Microkinetic analyses confirm that the oxygen species of ring5 regulate ethylene oxide yield, peaking at a nanoparticle oxidation degree of O/Ag ≈ 0.3–0.4. This work establishes a statistical paradigm for decoding active phases on realistic catalyst surfaces through dynamic structural ensembles.
nc8456e98e64c: The complex structure of polyurethanes (PURs) presents a major barrier to their efficient recycling. Here, we report a chemoenzymatic cascade that enables the simultaneous recycling and upcycling of PUR through rapid alkaline pretreatment followed by urethanase-catalyzed depolymerization. Using in-house-synthesized model polyether- and polyester-based PUR elastomers, we establish that soft-segment chemistry dictates the composition, morphology, and accessibility of the pretreated residues, thereby governing the efficiency of the subsequent enzymatic hydrolysis. This insight enabled translation of the cascade to a commercial PUR elastomer, achieving >93% chemical conversion and recovery of up to 1 mM 4,4′-methylenedianiline (MDA) (97.2% purity), corresponding to a 40-fold increase over the nonenzymatic control, together with polyols obtained in 95% isolated yield that were directly reused for PUR synthesis. Mechanistic studies further show that alkaline pretreatment enhances substrate accessibility for the enzyme, and structural analysis of urethanase SP2 reveals a carbamate-specific hydrogen-bonding interaction that promotes urethane hydrolysis while minimizing esterase activity. The cascade was additionally applied to highly crosslinked commercial PUR foams and adhesives, demonstrating its versatility toward industrially relevant waste streams. Overall, this work establishes a mechanistically informed chemoenzymatic platform for PUR depolymerization and provides a strategy for converting chemically recalcitrant PUR waste into reusable molecular building blocks.
n1b554c55772f: Alkenes are among the most abundant and versatile feedstocks in synthetic chemistry, yet methods for their direct and regioselective conversion into nitrogen-containing frameworks remain scarce. In particular, the direct catalytic amidination of alkenes has remained underdeveloped. Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed anti-Markovnikov amidination of alkenes using a stable pyridinyl formimidamide synthon. This reaction enables the direct installation of amidine moieties onto a wide range of alkenes, including styrenes, aliphatic alkenes, and challenging internal alkenes that undergo efficient chain-walking with high regioselectivity and broad functional group tolerance, accommodating unprotected amines, phenols, and halides. The resulting pyridyl amidines can be readily transformed into amides, carboxylic acids and esters, establishing a practical platform for alkene diversification. Notably, late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules, including cyclosporine A, FK506, and quinine etc., provides access to previously inaccessible analogues. Mechanistic investigations, highlighted by the crystallographic capture of a key rhodium–aminopyridinyl formimidamide intermediate, provide compelling evidence for the proposed catalytic cycle. Collectively, this work not only fills a critical gap in alkene functionalization but also offers a concise and general route to high-value nitrogen-containing architectures.
n9cedba7009ee: The asymmetric construction of nonadjacent stereocenters in a single catalytic system remains a significant challenge due to the difficulty in controlling stereochemical relay between sequential transformations. Herein, we report a dual-enzyme relay catalytic system that integrates an artificial streptavidin-based copper metalloenzyme (Sav-Cu) with an engineered ketoreductase (KRED) for the one-pot synthesis of polycyclic alcohols bearing 1,3-non-adjacent stereocenters. In this relay process, the engineered SavDMase variant (S112A/K121D) catalyzes a non-natural decarboxylative Mannich reaction to establish the R-configured stereocenter in the enantioenriched ketone intermediate, which is then recognized by the engineered KREDAV mutant (S96A/Y190V) and reduced with high diastereo- and enantioselectivity to install the S-configured alcohol stereocenter, thereby furnishing the (R,S)-configured product as the dominant stereoisomer. The optimized system furnishes the products in up to 83% yield, 99% ee, and 96% de across a broad substrate scope, and is readily applicable to 2 mmol-scale synthesis. Structural analysis, docking, and molecular dynamics simulations support complementary roles of the two catalytic modules: SavDMase promotes productive organization of the Mannich step, while KREDAV stabilizes the reactive binding pose and constrains the hydride-transfer trajectory to enforce stereoselective reduction. This work demonstrates how artificial and natural enzymes can be integrated in relay catalysis to solve challenging stereochemical relay problems beyond the reach of individual biocatalysts.
nb3798da3a65c: In heterogeneous catalysis, the electronic structures of catalysts' active sites are modified to optimize intermediate binding and bond activation for achieving high reaction activity. However, studies on regulating the atomic structures of catalytic materials to enhance the configurational diversity of adsorbed intermediates remain scarce. Herein, we demonstrate that engineering under-coordinated active site motifs enables an entropy-enhanced catalytic mechanism that harnesses the configurational freedom of surface intermediates to improve reaction rates at reduced temperatures. Using CO2 methanation as a model reaction, we identified that under-coordinated Ru2+−oxygen vacancy (Ru2+−VO) sites promote delocalized catalyst−intermediate interactions and reduce the reaction energy barrier. Stable Ru2+−VO sites were created on Au nanoparticle-grafted (RuOx)a(CeOy)b solid-solution nanorods through plasmonic effects under reducing conditions. Eyring plot analysis revealed an activation entropy gain of TΔΔS‡ ≈ 12 kJ mol−1 for CO2 methanation at 300 °C, in situ spectroscopy revealed a *HCOO-mediated pathway, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations indicated a 0.22 eV free-energy barrier for *HCOO formation on Ru2+−VO motifs. A CH4 production rate of 550 mmol gcat−1 h−1 with >98% selectivity and >280 h stability at 300 °C was achieved at a high gas hourly space velocity of 40,000−100,000 mL gcat−1 h−1. The findings provide a conceptual framework beyond adsorption energy optimization in catalyst design, showing that configurational entropy is a tunable descriptor for enhancing catalytic kinetics.
n5cb9e09ff6c8: Efficient activation of interfacial water molecules and fast proton transfer are critical but challenging for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Herein, a Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid catalyst design strategy is proposed to achieve accelerated acidic OER by synergistically optimizing the configuration of interfacial water molecules and proton transfer kinetics on Mn-doped IrO2. In this catalyst, the Mn dopant serves as a Lewis acid site that readily captures hydroxyl groups, which perturbs the local hydrogen-bonding network and induces interfacial water molecules to form an H-down configuration toward surface active sites, thereby promoting the enrichment and dissociation of reactive interfacial water. On this basis, the formation of the Mn–Obri–Ir local structure enhances the Brønsted acidity of the bridge oxygen (Obri) site, accelerates the deprotonation of the Obri–H bond, promotes the formation of key OER intermediates and accelerates the reaction kinetics. Mn dopant also induces electron enrichment around Ir, suppresses excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ir species, and enhances catalyst stability performance. These synergistic effects enable Mn-IrO2 to achieve a 160 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm–2 and to operate stably for 1500 h at 10 mA cm–2 and 1200 h at 1.0 A cm–2 in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), demonstrating the promising potential of the Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid strategy in acidic OER catalyst design.
n5b2edc4d58d9: The selective conversion of methane to methanol remains a major challenge in catalysis, and no earth-abundant homogeneous catalyst has been demonstrated to carry out this transformation with high turnover. To explore previously synthesized complexes that might be amenable for this transformation, we start from macrocyclic ligands from experimental structures in the Cambridge Structural Database. After expanding this set of ligands with Hammett-tuning functionalization, we construct a design space of 21.9 million Mn and Fe catalysts. We employ active learning using neural network surrogate models with quantified uncertainty to efficiently identify catalysts with optimal methane-to-methanol turnover. We do this by jointly optimizing density functional theory (DFT)-computed hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and methyl radical rebound energetics. Square planar tetraaza-based macrocycles in combination with low-spin Fe(II) or Mn(II) emerge as a privileged class of transition metal complexes within the Pareto-optimal set, with Mn(II) catalysts exhibiting balanced energetic tradeoffs of the two steps. In contrast, porphyrin catalysts exhibit favorable HAT but unfavorable rebound, and seesaw catalysts, which are not widely employed, are indeed the least favorable in our set. Full reaction coordinate analysis of representative Pareto-optimal catalysts reveals that HAT and rebound thermodynamics no longer govern turnover, which is instead determined by the stability of the metal–oxo intermediate and the rebound kinetic barrier. Nonetheless, the resulting energetic spans for these catalysts remain competitive with known earth-abundant, methane-to-methanol catalysts, underscoring the effectiveness of active learning for discovering previously unexplored, synthetically accessible catalysts and unraveling catalyst design principles for methane-to-methanol reactivity.
n30646491aa66: Transition-metal-catalyzed cyclization of 1,n-enynes represents a versatile platform for the construction of structurally diverse chiral heterocycles. Despite substantial advances in this field, the enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,n-enynes remains a formidable synthetic challenge, primarily due to the inherent difficulty in simultaneous control of regio-, chemo-, and stereoselectivity. Herein, we disclose a highly enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,6-enynes employing two complementary alkylating reagents: diazo compounds and readily available alkyl iodides. This protocol proceeds under mild conditions and features broad substrate scope, delivering enantioenriched γ-lactams and pyrrolidine derivatives bearing quaternary stereogenic centers in good yields (up to 81%) and enantioselectivities (53 examples, up to 98% ee). Mechanistic studies corroborate that these two types of alkylating reagents follow entirely distinct catalytic pathways.
n6fd9c930f1c5: Selective one-step conversion of methane (CH4) to methanol (CH3OH) remains a grand challenge in catalysis, constrained by the trade-off between C─H bond activation and product overoxidation. Here, we integrate density functional theory (DFT) calculations with plasma-catalytic experiments to investigate direct CH4-to-CH3OH conversion using H2O as the sole oxidant on CuxOy clusters within MOR zeolite, compared to the CuO(111) surface. We show that C─H bond activation proceeds preferentially via homolytic H-abstraction on zeolite-confined CuxOy clusters, with Cu3O3/MOR exhibiting a low activation barrier of only 0.21 eV, more than three times lower than that on CuO(111). Vibrational mode-specificity analysis shows that the C─H stretching modes couple most effectively on higher-barrier surfaces. Importantly, we demonstrate that plasma-generated radical intermediates (CH3·, H·, OH·) reshape the reaction thermodynamics, with the Gibbs free energy shifting from endothermic (+1.13 eV) to exothermic (–3.21 eV and –8.25 eV), enabling pathways inaccessible under thermal conditions. Experimentally, Cu/MOR catalysts prepared by ion exchange, which favor well-dispersed zeolite-confined Cu-oxo sites, achieve the highest CH3OH production rate (0.26 mmol/h) at low plasma power (6.5 W), outperforming catalysts prepared by wetness impregnation. This work bridges Cu-oxo site topology, vibrational mode specificity, and radical-mediated thermodynamics, offering valuable insights for plasma-catalytic selective CH4-to-CH3OH conversion.
n96109b342764: The free C2-OH group of glycosyl donors is generally viewed as a liability in glycosylation because it can act as a competing nucleophile and compromise stereocontrol. Here, we show that this functionality can instead be harnessed as a programmable stereochemical element in a catalyst-controlled stereodivergent glycosylation. A single β-configured 2-hydroxy glycosyl 8-alkynyl-1-naphthoate donor was found to deliver either β- or α-glycosides simply by changing the gold(I) catalyst system. Triflate-based catalysts promoted highly β-selective glycosylation, whereas bistriflimide-based conditions enabled complementary α-selective glycosylation from the same donor. The method is applicable to a range of carbohydrate and noncarbohydrate acceptors and enables the programmable assembly of glucooligosaccharides bearing β-(1→6), α-(1→6), and alternating α/β-(1→6) linkages from a common donor platform. Mechanistic studies, including intermediate characterization, variable-temperature NMR experiments, computational analysis, and control glycosylations with the corresponding 2-O-Bn donor, reveal distinct roles of the donor 2-OH group in the two stereochemical manifolds.
n07dd93a63c45: Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds represents a promising route for selective conversion of organic molecules such as acetonitrile (CH3CN) into value-added products. However, as the most common reactive oxygen species, •OH radicals are nonselective and usually lead to overoxidation reactions, making it difficult to realize the target product with both high activity and selectivity in the photocatalytic system. Here, we demonstrate that, through oxygen vacancy (Vo) engineering, selective CH3CN conversion into HCOOH is enabled over a WO3 photocatalyst under mild conditions. Under simulated solar irradiation, the as-prepared Vo-rich WO3 nanosheets display notable photocatalytic CH3CN conversion performance, with a HCOOH yield rate of 8.8 mmol g–1 h–1 and a selectivity as high as 86.5%. In combination of various in situ spectroscopic techniques, it is revealed that the Vo constructs a coupling match between of •OH radicals and •CH2CN intermediates on the WO3 photocatalyst surface, which facilitates the selective conversion of CH3CN into HCOOH while preventing its overoxidation. This work extends the conversion pathway of CH3CN in a photocatalytic route and provides deeper insight into the selective conversion of inert molecules.
n7ba9123ac4bf: We investigate the interplay between carbon accumulation and redox-driven deactivation pathways in cerium-containing nickel (NiCe) and palladium (PdCe) bimetallic precursor materials upon eventual decomposition into a Ni- or Pd-ceria interfacial system during dry reforming of methane (DRM). By probing defined intermediate states, information from surface electronic structure, morphology, and bulk structure to track structural and chemical changes across several reaction, deactivation, and CO2 titration cycles is combined to identify how carbon accumulation, oxygen transfer, and dynamic metal–ceria interfacial interactions evolve under DRM reaction conditions. Despite their similar cerium-containing precursor architecture and surface composition, the two systems allow studying two detrimental deactivation processes. Bimetallic NiCe decomposes more readily into a Ni-ceria interface, where carbon formation is progressively suppressed. Loss of activity is a result of oxidation of Ni particles mediated by enhanced oxygen transfer from ceria. In contrast, bimetallic PdCe is much more decomposition-resistant, and the localized Pd-ceria interface exhibits high activity throughout multiple DRM cycles, even in the presence of substantial carbon deposition and filamentous carbon growth. The results demonstrate an intrinsic coupling between carbon accumulation and oxygen transfer to the metallic component, with carbon acting as a competing sink for reactive oxygen species. We emphasize the significance of dynamic interfacial structures and show that ceria-mediated oxygen transfer produces contrasting, metal-dependent catalytic outcomes. Whereas in NiCe, efficient oxygen delivery suppresses carbon accumulation, but progressively oxidizes Ni and diminishes methane activation, in PdCe, carbon generation outpaces oxygen-mediated removal, yielding a carbon-rich yet catalytically persistent surface.
n48f8def67571: A modified colloidal atomic layer deposition at room temperature grows a vacancy-ordered Cs2SnCl6 shell epitaxially on CsPbCl3 nanocrystals, avoiding the core degradation and parasitic shell nucleation that accompany high-temperature routes. The resulting core–shell nanocrystals achieve an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% and retain 65% of their emission after six months of ambient storage and 30% after 48 h of exposure to added water.
n874a803e9337: Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. Departing from the conventional host-centric view, we demonstrate that reversibility in Mg batteries can be governed by electrolyte-derived reaction chemistry. Here, we harness trace water to impart controlled electrolyte reactivity, enabling electrolyte-derived Mg/Cl-containing species to participate in cathode activation. In tunnel-type MnO2, the regulated electrolyte induces lattice expansion and improves electrochemical reversibility. In organic cathodes, improved rechargeability is consistent with a stabilizing role of Cl– in anion-coupled redox. Because polar-solvent chemistry can irreversibly passivate Mg metal, a Sn/MgCl2 artificial interface suppresses parasitic anode reactions while preserving cathode activation. This strategy enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, including α/γ-MnO2, methylphenothiazine, tetrathiafulvalene, and hybrid I2/O2 systems. These findings establish electrolyte-derived chemical activation as a guiding principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in magnesium batteries.
n7b18684a7f4e: Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Although a uniform Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is suggested to improve cycle stability, the synthesis–structure relationship governing domain formation remains underexplored. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Through a comparative investigation of the synthesis mechanism, we reveal the templating effect that more clustered transition-metal oxide precursors lead to more localized Li2MnO3-like ordering in the final cathodes, a tendency also observed with a different lithium source. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.
n8d648f4076f8: The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.
n03850d8c938a: Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. Although poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) possesses high intrinsic permittivity, stabilizing its polar structure remains thermodynamically challenging. Here, we report a scalable physical processing strategy to optimize PVDF-based films via a specialized shear-imposed coating methodology. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.
ned76db721745: Atomic precision in metal–sulfur assemblies offers a transformative pathway to programmable nanomaterials, with applications spanning energy-efficient optoelectronics to highly selective CO2 reduction catalysis. However, the inherent lability of the metal–sulfur bond remains a formidable barrier to the rational design of robust frameworks. While strong-field ligands such as cyclic (alkyl)(amino)carbenes (CAACs) are gold-standard scaffolds for stabilizing reactive monometallic centers, their impact on the structural fidelity of multinuclear clusters remains elusive. Herein, we report a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of a CAAC-supported Cu8(μ3-S)4 cluster─a high-impact prototype for metal-chalcogenide systems with relatively weak metal–sulfur bonds. Through electrochemical and protonation studies, we demonstrate that while the potent σ-donor ability of the CAAC ligand successfully enforces solution integrity and thermal resilience, the structural boundaries of the multinuclear scaffold under chemical stress are ultimately governed by the core topology and metal–sulfur bond lability rather than local metal–ligand bonding. In-depth density functional theory (DFT) analysis demonstrates that while the CAAC ligands actively strengthen the peripheral Cu–S bonds via a pronounced inverse trans influence, the trigonal pyramidal (μ3-S) motifs remain vulnerable to proton-induced bond labilization and oxidative S–S coupling. Our findings establish that the design rules for multinuclear assemblies diverge fundamentally from monometallic species: whereas CAACs successfully passivate peripheral coordination sites to thermal decomposition, they do not preclude internal, core-mediated degradation pathways. These clear boundaries reveal that achieving structural durability in functional base metal–sulfur assemblies requires pairing strong local donors with supramolecular and/or multidentate ligand strategies designed explicitly to buttress the metal–sulfur core.

n37b44689883c: The ammonia (NH3) decomposition reaction represents an attractive pathway for hydrogen production from carbon-free energy carriers, offering significant potential for long-term and large-scale renewable energy conversion. However, the high thermodynamic...
nb6b7edcdbed8: Efficient photothermal CO₂ reduction requires the coordinated regulation of catalyst morphology, surface defects, and light-to-heat conversion. Herein, hierarchical hollow In2O3 (h-In2O3) was prepared from an indium–terephthalate coordination precursor (In-BDC), followed...
n80fcdd851a13: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. Its unique surface coordination architecture governs substrate adsorption via steric effects; this structural feature, combined with the cluster’s remarkable stability, concurrently facilitates effective alkyne activation and ensures high hydrogenation selectivity. Notably, this work overcomes the conventional dependence on noble metals such as gold and palladium in hydrogenation catalysis, revealing the significant potential of ligand-protected copper nanoclusters for this transformation.
nb91102874037: While polyester waste represents a valuable carbon resource for chemical production, its upcycling typically involves multiple steps for polymer depolymerization, intermediate separation, and subsequent conversion. This work establishes a tandem catalytic method that integrates depolymerization and selective upcycling in a single process, which selectively converts diverse commercial polyesters and mixed waste streams into valuable dicarboxylic acids.
n9a1bfe755e63: This review summarizes the bioinspired design principles, core modules, assembly strategies, unique functions, advances, and bottlenecks of artificial photosynthetic cells, and outlines future opportunities for synthetic photobiological systems.
ne129cee4338d: This review summarizes molecular design strategies for shifting molecular motors from UV to visible and near-infrared operation, with emphasis on recent advances and emerging applications.
naffa31d5ae58: Branched quaternary ammonium chlorides were explored as low-chloride aqueous electrolytes for four-electron Zn–I 2 batteries. 3-Chloro-2-hydroxypropyl trimethylammonium chloride proved optimal for Ah-level pouch cells.
ndbb7453165ae: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (eCO 2 RR) has been widely regarded as a promising approach to address environmental issues associated with rising atmospheric CO 2 levels. Recently we have reported a bottom-up synthesis...
n7c477b3c2b75: Facing global freshwater scarcity and energy shortages, this work designs a flower-inspired 3D solar evaporator made from modified ramie yarns that simultaneously generates clean water and electricity. Its conical structure traps sunlight to drive rapid evaporation (1.77 kg m−2 h−1) and produce thermoelectric voltage (38 mV) while resisting salt crystallization even in high-salinity brine, offering a sustainable, off-grid solution for water-electricity cogeneration.
n056ae4039b79: High-entropy chalcogenides represent an emerging class of functional materials with immense potential in broad applications. To date, colloidal high-entropy nanocrystals (NCs) have predominantly been accessed via co-nucleation of precursors or simultaneous incorporation of multiple cations. While effective, these approaches lack a mechanistic understanding of NC synthesis. Here, we report the colloidal synthesis of high-entropy Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S NCs in the tetrahedrite phase, employing a sequential, low-temperature cation-exchange strategy, starting from a Cu–Zn–Sb–S tetrahedrite template. Subsequent sequential cation exchanges preserve the crystal phase while enabling precise control over morphology. This bottom-up approach circumvents the need for high-temperature synthesis, while allowing isolation and characterization of intermediate states, providing important mechanistic insight into the evolution of high-entropy NCs. The nanocrystals served as hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysts with less negative cathodic potentials. This work introduces the high-entropy tetrahedrite phase, paving the way for entropy-stabilized chalcogenides for energy conversion applications.
nb5b8266bf453: Transition metal dihalides are promising magnetic van der Waals materials because of their structural simplicity, chemical stability, and compatibility with nanofabrication. While magnetic order in these systems is typically associated with bulk-like monolayers, its relation to interfacial phases remains largely unexplored. Here we show that in CoBr2 grown on Au(111), long-range magnetic order already emerges in a structurally distinct interfacial precursor phase, prior to the formation of the bulk-like monolayer. During growth, this phase evolves into the monolayer, accompanied by a transition from molecular-like states to semiconducting behavior. Spin-resolved STM reveals an inhomogeneous in-plane magnetic response that is locally suppressed by point defects, whereas macroscopic XMCD demonstrates robust long-range order with pronounced in-plane anisotropy. These results establish that long-range magnetic order in CoBr2 does not require an ideal bulk-like monolayer but can emerge from interfacial phases with distinct electronic and structural properties, enabling magnetism beyond the monolayer limit.
nf891a8c7f84a: Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) defects are promising building blocks for quantum photonics and sensing, yet their nonlinear optical signatures remain poorly understood. We use first-principles calculations to determine the polarization-resolved linear, second-order, and third-order susceptibilities of multilayer h-BN containing vacancies and carbon-based defect complexes. Defects weakly affect the linear response but strongly enhance nonlinear susceptibilities through symmetry breaking and resonant defect transitions. Carbon complexes produce orders-of-magnitude increases in second-harmonic generation and distinct polarization-dependent spectra that differentiate defects with identical composition but different geometry. Third-harmonic generation is also enhanced, although it is less sensitive to local structure. Measurements on carbon-doped h-BN qualitatively support these trends. These results establish nonlinear spectroscopy as a powerful probe of defect identity and geometry in h-BN and provide a route to defect-engineered nonlinear quantum photonics.
n495d2a1713d2: Multifocal phase holography offers a route to parallel femtosecond laser micro- and nanofabrication, but conventional weighted Gerchberg–Saxton (GSW) phase retrieval requires target-specific iterations and does not jointly optimize the optical quantities governing exposure quality. Here we introduce PhyFlow, a physics-consistent invertible flow model that generates phase-only multifocal holograms from target multifocal patterns in a single inverse pass. A multiscale invertible backbone learns target-to-phase correspondence, while differentiable Fourier optics constraints optimize diffraction efficiency, focal uniformity, and target-shape preservation. Across focal numbers and array scales, PhyFlow matches or surpasses GSW in energy concentration, focal balance, and shape fidelity while reducing per-hologram generation time by 98.8%. Optical-field measurements and femtosecond laser writing further show improved dot-area consistency, narrower line width distributions, and fewer nontarget written features. PhyFlow therefore connects rapid learned hologram generation with physically optimized fields and more uniform parallel fabrication.
n958f5dd3d88f: Chiral nanostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their strong interactions with circularly polarized light (CPL) and their various applications. Although various fabrication methods have been reported, photoelectrochemical approaches using CPL as the chiral source are attractive because of their simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and scalability. However, previous CPL-based methods have required two or more steps, including the preparation of anisotropic precursors. Here, we demonstrate a single-step method for the selective growth of chiral PbO2 nanostructures with handedness dictated by CPL at a chiral yield of 87%, by simply irradiating a transparent electrode with CPL, without using precursor nanoparticles. The obtained structures exhibit well-defined spiral morphologies and high chiroptical activity with maximum dissymmetry factors (g-factors) ranging from 0.006 to 0.010. This conceptual framework, involving symmetry breaking through random nucleation and Mie-resonance-mediated spiral growth under CPL, may be applicable to the template-free fabrication of various chiral nanomaterials.
nac7cf40e3af8: Au nanoparticles (NPs) are inherently thermally unstable at elevated temperatures because their large surface-to-volume ratio promotes melting, migration, and coalescence. Here, we demonstrate that silica (SiO2) nanoconfinement thermodynamically elevates the melting point (Tm) of Au NPs through confinement-induced compressive pressure. Atomic-resolution in situ heating scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with local Fourier crystallinity mapping reveals that bare Au NPs lose crystallinity at 1,000 °C, whereas SiO2-encapsulated Au cores (Au@SiO2) remain crystalline. Accordingly, in situ heating TEM shows bare Au NPs progressively merge while Au@SiO2 remain structurally isolated. Temperature-dependent lattice-parameter measurements reveal significantly suppressed thermal expansion of confined Au cores, corresponding to an estimated compressive stress of 4–5 GPa. Finite-element simulations support this estimate, showing that SiO2 shell shrinkage generates several-GPa core pressure, with thicker shells producing higher pressure and greater Tm elevation. These findings establish nanoconfinement-induced pressure as a general thermomechanical strategy for stabilizing metallic NPs under extreme thermal environments.
n273ad8756d72: Magnesium, a promising alternative for sustainable nanophotonics, crystallizes in a hexagonal close-packed (HCP) system, unlike the face-centered cubic (FCC) structures of gold, silver, copper, and aluminum. We report the high-yield colloidal synthesis of an unexpected shape in an HCP system: cubes. Nanocubes with narrow size distributions were produced from colloidal reduction of a magnesium precursor in the presence of a sodium salt nucleating agent. Electron microscopy and diffraction reveal multiple twinning leading to the formation of six single-crystal units within the nanocubes. A self-limiting, sub-10 nm passivating oxide layer protects the metallic core against further oxidation in air and organic solvents. Strong, multimode plasmonic responses were observed using bulk extinction spectroscopy, single-particle scattering correlated with electron microscopy, and electron energy loss spectroscopy; experimental results were corroborated by numerical simulations. These findings expand the crystallographic boundaries of non-FCC plasmonics and establish magnesium nanocubes as versatile building blocks for nanophotonic applications.
nfc8cd9517c63: Altermagnets have recently gained attention for hosting symmetry-enforced spin-split bands despite zero net magnetization. Angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES) offers direct access to their electronic structure. However, the intrinsic surface sensitivity of this technique complicates the identification of the observed features: Surface states can be misinterpreted as the spin-split counterpart of bulk bands. This issue becomes particularly relevant for layered intercalated systems, where micrometer-sized domains with distinct terminations often coexist on a cleaved surface. We discuss this scenario for CoNb4Se8, one of the first established layered altermagnets. Supported by density functional theory calculations, we employ micro-ARPES to probe individual domains and reveal two contrasting surface terminations. We identify Co- and Se-terminated domains with characteristic surface states arising from bulk-surface connectivity of the material. Our work shows that termination-dependent surface contributions are essential for the reliable spectroscopic identification of altermagnetism and for assessing its presence across the family of layered materials.
n00630f7656ef: Charge-transfer doping provides a nondestructive route to tune two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), but selectively patterned n-type dopants effective across different TMD channels remain limited. Here, ultrathin bismuth oxide (BiOx) is used as an n-type charge-transfer doping and passivation layer for monolayer MoS2 and WSe2 transistors. In MoS2, 2 nm BiOx preserves the channel structure and yields a TLM-extracted effective contact resistance of 0.71 ± 0.06 kΩ·μm at n2D = 1.8 × 1013 cm–2. Thicker BiOx strengthens n-type modulation but reduces gate controllability. The modulation remains stable after ambient storage and air annealing. BiOx also enhances electron transport in WSe2 and enables homogeneous WSe2 inverters with MoOx-doped p-FETs, achieving a gain of ∼19 and a total normalized noise margin of 0.895 VDD at VDD = 2 V. These results establish BiOx as a cross-TMD n-type charge-transfer dopant for contact, threshold-voltage, and polarity engineering.
n79a1f2802c3b: A bioresorbable, metal-free molecular magnet for wireless deep-tissue sensing is reported that enables continuous cardiac monitoring and injectable organ tracking in vivo before the material safely degrades.
n8f0b777ffd55: Strong coupling between magnons and excitons in CrSBr enables microwave-to-optical transduction, offering a route towards efficient conversion between otherwise disparate frequency regimes.
n8662555b8320: Heteroleptic organosilanes with four different substituents are prepared by a selective and simple method based on the controlled monobromination of multihydrosilanes. This approach avoids the limitations of conventional methods, tolerates diverse functional groups and enables iterative access to highly substituted silanes in excellent yields.
n2f6e6b14dbd3: The stepwise installation of carbon substituents at silicon starting from tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes is burdened by chemoselectivity issues, typically affording product mixtures. Now, monoselective bromination of multihydrosilanes followed by nucleophilic displacement opens the door to the programmable and reliable synthesis of functionalized silicon building blocks.
n617dd9db8a0f: Advances in dynamic covalent chemistry have dramatically broadened its use in polymer research. Cyclic disulfide bonds are a widely used, versatile platform for engineering dynamic polymers. The resulting polymers leverage the dynamic character of exocyclic linkages associated with cyclic disulfide bonds, along with modular, tailorable chain-end functionalities to enable self-healing and chemical recycling. This review summarizes recent advances in dynamic polymer chemistry based on cyclic disulfide bonds that have enabled new design principles for the development and innovation in advanced polymers. We highlight living/controlled polymerization strategies for cyclic disulfide monomers, covering the principal polymerization strategies and mechanisms, and discuss the future challenges and prospective directions of the field in the context of emerging societal and technological demands.
nb67843be428e: Interlayer CO 3 2− polarizes the Ni–O–Fe motif in NiFe-LDH, inducing differentiated electronic responses at the Ni and Fe sites. This site-dependent electronics promote the early formation of Ni 3+ –O and *OOH, enabling ampere-level alkaline OER.
nc5a607337783: Rational molecular engineering of the perovskite/hole transport layer interface offers a promising route to simultaneously address inefficient charge extraction, defect-mediated recombination, and lead leakage in CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite solar cells. Herein, we introduce 2,2′-dinitro-9,9′-spirobifluorene (DN-SBF) as an interfacial molecular bridge to tackle these challenges. DN-SBF optimizes energy level alignment, establishes π–π interactions, and forms exciplexes with Spiro-OMeTAD, thereby facilitating interfacial charge transport. Meanwhile, DN-SBF passivates undercoordinated Pb2+ through multiple coordination modes, including robust bidentate chelation formed by adjacent nitro groups, effectively passivating defects and suppressing non-radiative recombination. Importantly, multipoint coordination immobilizes leachable Pb2+, substantially mitigating lead leakage and improving film biocompatibility. As a result, DN-SBF-engineered CsPbI3–xBrx devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 22.40% along with significantly enhanced operational and environmental stability. This work highlights the potential of versatile molecular bridges to concurrently enhance performance, stability, and eco-friendliness, which may contribute to the development of more sustainable perovskite photovoltaics.

ned9501745b95: Transition metal fluorides (TMFs) are promising conversion-type cathode materials for high-energy lithium–metal batteries owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, making them attractive for demanding applications such as electric aviation. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish conversion kinetics, pronounced voltage hysteresis, and poor electrochemical reversibility. Understanding the structural and chemical evolution of TMFs and the electrode–electrolyte interphase formed during cycling is essential for improving their performance. Monodisperse nanocrystalline TMFs are ideal model systems for high-resolution transmission electron microscopy because their uniform size, morphology, and electron transparency enable representative nanoscale characterization. Here, we investigate a reproducible colloidal synthesis of monodisperse, single-crystalline CoF2 nanorods and elucidate the mechanisms governing their formation to achieve precise control over particle size and aspect ratio. By independently varying reaction time, temperature, precursor composition, and ligand chemistry, we identify the key factors controlling precursor decomposition, burst nucleation, phase selection, and anisotropic crystal growth. These insights provide a transferable framework for the controlled synthesis of a broad range of transition metal fluoride nanocrystals.
n8e5d09d9c91c: Activating the exceptionally strong N≡N bond remains a fundamental challenge due to the chemical inertness of molecular nitrogen (N2). Plasmonic nanoclusters offer a promising approach by generating localized electromagnetic fields and energetic hot carriers that can drive bond activation under ambient conditions. Here, we combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory with Ehrenfest molecular dynamics to reveal how plasmonic coupling between tetrahedral Ag20 nanoclusters governs N2 activation and dissociation. Systematic variation of the intercluster separation shows that a 6 Å nanogap maximizes near-field enhancement and hot-electron transfer to the adsorbed N2, accompanied by N–N activation. Consequently, N2 dissociation is achieved at incident field strengths as low as 0.5 V Å–1, whereas larger-gap dimers exhibit substantially lower activity. Similarly, isolated N2 remains intact under comparable conditions. These findings establish nanogap engineering as an effective strategy for optimizing plasmon-driven N2 activation and provide design principles for developing efficient plasmonic catalysts.
n80308568dfd5: Solution-processable quantum dot (QD) lasers are essential for next-generation integrated photonic circuits, ranging, and optical sensing. However, their practical deployment remains hampered by high lasing thresholds. Here, we report AgAuSe QD lasing with a record-low threshold of 0.01 μJ cm–2 at 900 nm, representing a reduction of more than 4 orders of magnitude compared to those of previous near-infrared (NIR) QD lasing reports. This achievement is enabled by a well-designed twisted-lattice photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity delivering extreme light confinement with an ultrahigh quality (Q) factor. The extended photon lifetime reduces the required gain volume, enabling lasing from a single-layer self-assembled QD superlattice (SL), which minimizes scattering losses. Crucially, the robust system allows us to push the operational regime to quasi-continuous-wave (q-CW) lasing at room temperature. These results establish a new benchmark for solution-processed NIR QD sources and provide a technologically viable pathway for sustained CW operation.
n9d636f098eaa: Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a single regioisomer in moderate to good diastereoselectivity (up to 11:1 dr) and in most cases with high enantioselectivity (up to >99.5:0.5 er). The densely functionalized γ-allylic allenones can be elaborated into useful building blocks, including a highly substituted chiral 2-allyl furan derivative. Through this work, α-alkynyl enol silanes are introduced as alkynylogous nucleophiles in transition metal catalysis.
n2765627ad6ec: The narrow amine donor scope of imine reductases (IREDs) limits their application in the synthesis of opine compounds. Herein, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided protein engineering strategy to address this limitation. An IRED from an unclassified Ensifer, IRED5, was identified through deep-learning-based screening for its strict enantioselectivity toward methyl glycinate. Subsequent engineering using a few-shot learning for protein fitness prediction approach yielded the M178T/A208L/P241V/A36E/S67Q/Q187N (M6) variant with six mutations across the active site and protein surface. Kinetic analysis showed 156-fold toward methyl pyruvate and 72-fold improvements toward methyl glycinate in catalytic efficiency, respectively, over the wild-type (WT) enzyme. M6 accepted diverse keto esters and amino acid esters, enabling stereoselective formation of opine derivatives bearing two stereocenters. Structural and computational analyses revealed the molecular basis for activity enhancement. In preparative synthesis, M6 achieved complete conversion at a 3 M substrate loading, corresponding to a space time yield of 366 g·L–1·d–1. At a 4 M substrate loading, conversion remained high at 95.4% with a space time yield of 525 g·L–1·d–1, affording 10.5 g of enantiopure methyl N-(2-methoxy-2-oxoethyl)-d-alaninate (1a) in 75.0% isolated yield with > 99.9% ee. This work establishes an efficient biocatalytic route to opine compounds and demonstrates the utility of ML-guided enzyme engineering in expanding IRED synthetic capability.
n1b2f50547d9f: The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine- and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt3Cu/SiO2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting the adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro-cis-aminoindanol.
n37a94272487d: Water oxidation in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) uses IrO2 nanoparticles supported on corrosion-resistant TiO2. However, the low conductivity of TiO2 imposes electronic transport limitations that necessitate high Ir loadings for effective catalysis. Here, we present a catalyst design strategy that couples a heavily V-doped TiO2 support with high-density Ir single atoms, enabling water oxidation at minimal Ir loading. In this design, Ti-site-substituted V provides n-type doping, and selective V leaching creates cation vacancies that anchor Ir as isolated atoms. TEM with convolutional neural network (CNN)-based analysis shows Ir single-atom density increases with V content, accompanied by lower charge-transfer resistance and higher Ir-specific activity. The density functional theory indicates that cation-site Ir introduces a midgap state below V 3d levels and shifts neighboring V 3d orbitals toward the Fermi level. Ir1/V-TiO2 achieves 1480 A gIr–1 at 1.55 V vs RHE (1.3 wt % Ir) and demonstrates device-level PEMWE operation at an Ir loading as low as 0.027 mgIr cm–2.
nc350d618c723: The reductive dispersion of metal oxides into isolated cationic species in zeolites is an important strategy for generating well-defined catalytic sites, yet its kinetics and molecular mechanism remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the H2-induced redispersion of In2O3 physically mixed with H-CHA using in situ/operando UV–vis spectroscopy, In K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), SEM-EDS mapping, modulation-excitation spectroscopy, H2-TPR, XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Time-resolved UV–vis spectroscopy quantitatively tracks the consumption of bulk-like In2O3 under H2 and reveals that the redispersion rate depends on temperature, H2 concentration, In2O3 precursor properties, and zeolite framework. Higher temperatures and H2 concentrations accelerate the process, with the highest reliable initial rate observed at 600 °C under 10% H2. In K-edge XANES indicates selective formation of reduced In species assigned to framework-stabilized In+ rather than metallic In0, demonstrating a partial-reduction pathway in CHA. H2-TPR provides quantitative redox evidence consistent with reductive solid-state ion exchange and reversible reduction of isolated oxygen-containing In species. SEM–EDS mapping shows the disappearance of surface In-rich domains after H2 treatment, consistent with indium redistribution, while XANES provides bulk-sensitive evidence for formation of reduced In species. Operando redox-cycling experiments reveal reversible interconversion between In(I) and oxygen-containing In(III) species under H2/O2 switching. DFT calculations using representative 1Al and 2Al CHA models suggest that local Al environments can influence the relative stability of framework-bound reduced In(I) and oxygen/hydroxyl-containing In(III)-type species. Together, these results support a two-step mechanism in which bulk In2O3 is first reduced to mobile In+ species and then anchored at acid sites within the zeolite framework. This work provides mechanistic insight into reductive redispersion and offers design principles for regenerable indium-based zeolite catalysts.
neb2ff219589e: The selective hydrodeoxygenation of lignin as a substitute for fossil resources into aviation fuel-range cycloalkanes faces significant challenges due to its complex structure and diverse reaction pathways. Herein, we introduced MoOx species onto Ni nanoparticles-loaded Beta zeolite (Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta), which catalyzed the complete hydrodeoxygenation of lignin dimers and lignin-derived phenols into the corresponding cycloalkanes under mild conditions (200 °C, 2 MPa H2). Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta also enabled the hydrodeoxygenation of real lignin, achieving a cycloalkanes selectivity of over 83%. Mechanistic studies indicated that the synergistic effect between Ni nanoparticles and MoOx species was key to enhancing the hydrodeoxygenation performance. Ni nanoparticles enabled the adsorption and dissociation of H2, and horizontally adsorbed benzene ring in the oxygen-containing substrate, while adjacent MoOx species with abundant oxygen vacancies facilitated the vertical adsorption of oxygen-containing groups in the ring-saturated intermediates and the activation of C–O bonds. Simultaneously, the strong hydrogen spillover on Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta ensured the benzene ring hydrogenation and the cleavage of C–O bonds. This work provides an approach for designing non-noble metal catalysts for lignin hydrodeoxygenation, holding significant value for advancing the application of lignin-based aviation fuels.
n4598f3ccb9e9: In anode-free Li metal batteries, a bare current collector must be converted into a reversible Li metal anode during the first charge, making Li nucleation decisive for reversibility. However, how current collector microstructure governs Li nucleation and growth remains poorly understood, since prior studies focused on single-crystal surfaces to identify favorable crystallographic orientations, leaving grain boundaries unexplored. Here, we identify grain boundary density and character in copper current collectors as key regulators of Li deposition uniformity. Systematic annealing decouples grain size from surface chemistry, revealing that deposition uniformity improves with copper grain coarsening but saturates as disordered boundaries are eliminated during grain growth, leaving predominantly low-energy configurations. Atomistic simulations show disordered boundaries impose high barriers to Li adatom migration, whereas ordered boundaries and adjacent low-index terraces provide low-barrier pathways for redistribution. Copper foils engineered beyond this threshold sustain uniform Li plating across diverse electrolytes and improve cyclability in anode-free cells.
n9f4039694a62: Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) based on colloidal InAs quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as promising light sources for the short-wave infrared (SWIR) range. However, their development is limited by relatively low photoluminescence quantum yield as well as intrinsic device design challenges. Here, we report LEDs with electroluminescence (EL) in the SWIR based on InAs/ZnSe core/shell colloidal QDs, synthesized via a seedless one-pot approach that enables the rapid growth of relatively large InAs cores. Zirconium-doped indium oxide (InZrO) was used as the bottom transparent electrode owing to its significantly higher infrared transparency compared to the commonly employed tin-doped indium oxide (ITO). These two key innovations pushed the EL beyond 1500 nm, with external quantum efficiencies of 3.0, 1.2, and 0.6% at 1093, 1198, and 1547 nm, respectively.
n677d8e82fc56: Conventional carbonization of semi-coke induces excessive ordering of aromatic skeletons, producing dense graphitic structures that hinder Na+ intercalation and suppress low-potential plateau capacity. Here, we develop a rapid thermomechanical coupling sintering strategy using moderate pressure to drive π–π interactions and topological reconfiguration of aromatic units. This process suppresses excessive graphitization while constructing interconnected, twisted pseudo-graphitic domains with abundant closed nanopores. At 1000 mA g–1, PTR-HC reaches 80% SOC in ≈14.4 min and retains 90.1% of its plateau capacity, enabled by abundant Na+ storage sites and rapid diffusion pathways. Kinetic analyses reveal accelerated Na+ transport and a thin, NaF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase with fewer organic components. In situ XRD and Raman attribute slope capacity to surface/defect adsorption and intercalation and the plateau capacity to quasi-metallic Na clusters in closed pores. This work establishes pressure-driven topological engineering as a promising strategy for upgrading semi-coke into fast-charging hard carbon with high plateau-capacity retention.
nadb66549bf6c: Interfacial losses at the perovskite/C60 and C60/metal contacts limit inverted perovskite solar cell performance. Here, we introduce a vacuum-evaporated molecule with giant spontaneous orientation polarization, 6F-2PI, for simultaneously tailoring both interfaces. Incorporating 6F-2PI increases the work function of perovskite, reducing the conduction band offset at the perovskite/C60 interface, which facilitates electron extraction. Concurrently, its phthalimide moieties passivate defect states, suppressing nonradiative recombination, as evidenced by a 0.03 eV recovery in quasi-Fermi level splitting. At the C60/metal interface, 6F-2PI also delivers efficient charge extraction, improved interfacial contact, and thermal resilience. Moreover, its hydrophobic fluorinated units prevent moisture ingress. Consequently, this dual-interface modulation boosts PCE from 18.5% to 22.5% with exceptional device stability, retaining over 90% of its initial efficiency after 2000 h under ambient conditions. Furthermore, this framework exhibits universal compatibility across both vacuum-deposited and solution-processed devices and simplifies processing for mass production.

n37d5bb016408: The bacterial surface represents the primary interface between pathogens and hosts, yet its chemical and architectural complexity challenges conventional classification. This Review examines structural organization, molecular composition, and biogenesis of bacterial surface components across the Gracilicutes and Terrabacteria clades, linking mechanistic detail to pathogenic function. We describe lipid diversity, integral membrane protein biogenesis, and lipoprotein processing at the inner membrane and how these components support surface remodeling, secretion, and virulence. We then examine the peptidoglycan layer and its role in immune recognition and surface protein display, teichoic acids and their contributions to antimicrobial resistance and immune evasion, and S layers, whose crystalline arrays mediate adhesion and immune modulation. The outer membrane section covers lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, outer membrane protein biogenesis and folding, lipoprotein trafficking, and contributions to pathogenicity, while the mycobacterial section addresses the mycolyl-arabinogalactan-peptidoglycan complex and virulence factors. We discuss bacterial capsule diversity, biosynthesis, and use as vaccine antigens, along with adhesive surface structures such as fimbriae, pili, and curli fibers and their roles in colonization and biofilm formation, before covering secretion systems types I through XI and their contributions to virulence. This Review provides a framework for understanding how bacterial surface diversity shapes infection and identifies chemical vulnerabilities for therapeutics.
n3f072c4ef5be: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer exceptional structural resolution for investigating how local environments govern catalytic behavior and, ultimately, for controlling these effects through catalyst design. Yet, atomic dispersion does not imply a single or fully defined catalytic environment. The behavior of atomically dispersed active centers is shaped by a hierarchical local environment comprising persistent and transient contributions, while also being influenced by an extended reaction environment that intersects with the local environment in controlling reactivity and can become integrated into it. Establishing these boundaries and understanding how these contributions evolve and interact are central challenges in the interpretation and design of SACs. Here, we critically examine how local environments are generated and controlled, experimentally and theoretically resolved across spatial and temporal scales, transformed from synthesis through operation and deactivation, and linked to catalytic performance through structural, energetic, and electronic descriptors. By integrating aspects that are often considered separately and highlighting those that remain insufficiently addressed, we provide a roadmap toward the predictive, environment-driven design of SACs and a deeper understanding of catalytic phenomena.
n98cc28f955b7: Regenerated cellulose (RC), derived from natural cellulose through dissolution and regeneration processes, has emerged as a sustainable, versatile, and cost-effective material for advanced electronic devices. With unique hierarchical structures, abundant hydroxy groups, and excellent mechanical and thermal properties, RC allows extensive customization of its characteristics, offering biocompatibility, flexibility, processability, and environmental friendliness. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in RC-based electronics, focusing on its multiscale molecular configuration, dissolution and regeneration mechanisms, and functionalization and engineering strategies. It first provides a detailed molecular-level analysis of RC structures and formation mechanisms. The principles and strategies of cellulose dissolution and regeneration are then discussed, with emphasis on solvent systems and structure-regulating mechanisms essential for processing control. Functionalization strategies are categorized into direct modification and hybridization with functional materials. Notably, the hybridization approach involves the development of conductive, semiconductive, and insulating RC composites, evaluated from the perspectives of material selection, interfacial design, and processing techniques. Subsequently, engineering approaches to enhance mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and optical transparency are explored. Applications of RC in sensors, actuators, circuits, energy harvesting and storage devices, and electromagnetic shielding devices are highlighted, demonstrating its potential to drive sustainable innovation in electronics. Finally, future directions are proposed to address remaining challenges, paving the way for RC to contribute to eco-friendly, high-performance electronic devices.

ne25eeb3fee85: This review summarizes the classification, physical and chemical synthesis, and structure–property relationships of layered superlattices, with emphasis on emerging applications, structural control, dynamic characterization, and device integration.
nca9f0c2237c8: This review proposes a mechanism-based unified framework for liquid hydrocarbon separation membranes and discusses the fabrication- and application-oriented regulation strategies in microenvironment engineering.
n8f2204474093: Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier due to its clean and versatile nature, offering opportunities for decarbonizing diverse sectors. Hydrogen utilization in many applications relies on identifying and understanding materials with exceptional hydrogen storage and transport properties. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of hydrogenation reactions in ternary ABO3 perovskites using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML) screening. We performed DFT simulations for a diverse range of perovskites featuring a variety of A-site cations (Ca, Sr, Ba) and B-site cations (Co, Fe, Mn, Ce, Ti, Zr) across various phases (cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, and hexagonal). By computing all data at the same theoretical level, we establish a consistent framework to compare how crystal phase, lattice-site chemistry, and host electronic structure govern hydrogen incorporation and diffusion. Therefore, we identify hexagonal SrMnO3, cubic SrFeO3, and hexagonal BaFeO3 as particularly promising candidates, combining favorable hydrogenation thermodynamics (ΔG < 1 eV) with low rotation and hopping barriers (<0.2 eV), while orthorhombic phases, although thermodynamically preferred, suffer from proton trapping, highlighting the importance of phase engineering toward cubic/hexagonal frameworks. Ab initio molecular dynamics further support this phase-dependent kinetic picture by showing relatively facile H diffusion in cubic SrFeO3 but much slower proton motion in orthorhombic BaCeO3 under the same conditions. By incorporating spatial and electronic descriptors with the DFT data into our ML models, we further develop a mechanistically motivated ML model based on structural and electronic descriptors to screen hydrogenation thermodynamics across 111 ternary ABO3 compositions. This model led to the identification of two additional promising candidates, hexagonal BaPdO3 and cubic BaSnO3, which were subsequently validated by DFT calculations. These findings provide a foundation for the rational design of ABO3 perovskites and demonstrate the potential of ML-driven frameworks with chemical insights to accelerate materials discovery in energetic and catalytic applications.
n84be227f2011: The propagation of both catalyst diffusion and reaction fronts in a polymeric chemically amplified resist (CAR) is evaluated by time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) depth profiling, and is compared with the propagation of catalyst diffusion fronts in inert resist analogues. We report that catalysts display accelerated and highly non-Fickian dynamics in the reactive CAR, even when located well behind the propagation front, while simple Fickian diffusion is observed for the same conditions in inert resist analogues. The complex catalyst dynamics of reactive systems is attributed to two key factors: (1) Transient free volume following deprotection events, which is a long-hypothesized acceleration mechanism acting on the diffusion front; and (2) a newly identified plasticization process induced by inert, nonvolatile byproducts of catalyst photoactivation. We propose a physics-informed model of enhanced catalyst diffusion due to the independent contributions of these two processes, and demonstrate that this model coupled to a first-order reaction provides a reasonable prediction of both the diffusion and reaction fronts. Our study presents a critical evaluation of mechanisms that control the spatial extent of reaction in CARs, and suggests that quantitative models of the patterning process should account for the impact of nonvolatile catalyst activation byproducts.

n91d94e745e84: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? This perspective reveals they actually deliver markedly enhanced thermal safety over carbonates in sodium architectures alongside uniquely higher thermal resilience toward metallic sodium than lithium equivalents. However, this protective margin is fundamentally negated by oxygen-driven chemical autoxidation rather than mere electrochemical degradation. These insights establish the anode-free ether configuration as the definitive trajectory for future sodium batteries, perfectly balancing energy density with robust safety.
ne37abb50eb58: Next-generation two-dimensional electronics require robust insulating layers that effectively control current without compromising device performance. Here, we report fluorinated diamane, a diamond-like van der Waals material, as a high-performance gate dielectric. By combining a high dielectric constant, exceptional breakdown strength, and efficient heat dissipation, fluorinated diamane integrates seamlessly with diverse two-dimensional semiconductors and memory devices. This material platform addresses long-standing dielectric bottlenecks in ultra-scaled two-dimensional electronics.
n038f2d444bb3: Conventional antiferroelectric states generally suppress the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) and enable skyrmion erasure by restoring inversion symmetry. However, noncentrosymmetric antiferroelectric states preserve broken inversion symmetry, offering an additional dimension for manipulating DMI and topological magnetic phases. Here, combining first-principles calculations with atomistic simulations, we demonstrate polarization-driven reconstruction of the DMI vector field and topological magnetic phases in monolayer CuCrP2Se6. FEu-AFE-FEd polarization switching enables the evolution of a uniform DMI into an anisotropic DMI vector field by reconstructing the lattice symmetry, thereby achieving reversible control between topologically nontrivial skyrmions and topologically trivial magnetic bubbles. These findings establish DMI vector-field reconstruction in noncentrosymmetric AFE states as a mechanism for engineering magnetic topology beyond conventional DMI reversal (D → −D) or suppression (D → 0).
n6628b158e57e: Silicon nanomembranes provide mechanically compliant devices for strain engineering. Here, we investigate third-harmonic generation in flat and crumpled silicon nanomembranes of 15 and 35 nm using polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation microscopy with ab initio calculations. In flat silicon nanomembranes, the measured polarization dependence is reproduced by the calculated third-order susceptibility, identifying the intrinsic nonlinear response of silicon. In crumpled silicon nanomembranes, local strain variations between valleys and apexes generate distinct polarization-dependent responses. Uniaxial strain along the [110] direction breaks electronic structure symmetry and induces anisotropy between X- and Y-polarized components, while the real and imaginary parts of the third-order susceptibility exhibit quadratic strain dependence. Morphology-induced redistribution of the local optical field further modifies the response in crumpled geometry, and a finite-difference time-domain-based local-field correction substantially improves agreement with the experiment. Therefore, the third-harmonic response of crumpled silicon nanomembranes is controlled by both strain-induced electronic structure modification and morphology-induced local optical-field redistribution.
n13a8e447775c: Translating local stereochemical information into higher-order helical architectures is a central challenge in materials design. Now it has been shown that stereochemically preorganized Au4 nanoclusters assemble into homochiral triple helices through directional aurophilic interactions, providing a design strategy for chiral nanocluster materials with amplified chiroptical responses.
n1c5fe76634c2: Molecular motors typically rotate by cycling through excitation and relaxation to ground states. Now it has been shown that a molecular motor can be driven by angular-momentum transfer. Circulating positive and negative currents flowing through orbitals of opposite helicity along a carbon–carbon triple bond enable unidirectional rotation.
nc4af52b33230: When defect-mediated losses are mitigated, lithium niobate phononic crystal nanomechanical resonators can have intrinsic phonon lifetimes of up to 21 ms at gigahertz frequencies.
n78efa0d612ee: Confining water within a polymeric hydrogen-bond network creates a controlled aqueous reaction environment that stabilizes precursors and directs the growth of dense, crack-free perovskite thick films. The resulting X-ray detectors achieve an ultralow detection limit of 19.8 nGyair s−1.
n28e992a16ec2: Diffusion-limited conversion of pre-formed covalent organic framework membranes creates a continuous chemical gradient across their thickness, with linkage conversion increasing from one face to the other while preserving aligned crystalline nanochannels. This asymmetry directs selective ion transport and increases salinity-gradient energy conversion, while the formation of robust linkages improves acid stability.
n38cc2abfab13: Reversible zinc oxidation, enhanced by lactate coordination, enables a self-sustained, circuit-free pathway for high-density hydrogen storage and delivery. By overcoming solubility limits under ambient conditions, this system delivers higher volumetric capacity and safety than existing carriers, providing a robust alternative to high-pressure infrastructure for decentralized, on-demand green hydrogen delivery.
n0d952b2b1d7b: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are a class of crystalline, porous networks constructed by polymerization of organic building blocks. However, most COF syntheses developed so far rely on acid- or base-catalysed reactions that are sensitive to monomer structure, require extensive condition screening, proceed under harsh conditions over several days and often yield low-quality products. Here we report a general hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy enabled by benzimidazole and its derivatives, acting as both hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors, to produce high-quality COFs. Distinct from conventional catalysis, these catalysts interact with monomers, intermediates and transition states, thereby reducing energy barriers at each step and promoting reversibility. This approach enables control through catalyst-to-monomer ratios and allows the rapid synthesis, within hours, of imide-, imine-, hydrazone- and sp2-carbon-linked COFs with high crystallinity and porosity. The method further supports catalyst reuse and 1,000-fold scale-up, producing COFs with benchmark proton conductivity, establishing hydrogen-bonding catalysis as a versatile route for scalable COF synthesis and applications. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are typically synthesized under harsh acid- or base-catalysed conditions. Here a hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy based on reusable benzimidazole enables the rapid and scalable production of COFs with high crystallinity and porosity, offering a general route to imide, imine, hydrazone and sp2-carbon-linked COF synthesis.
nf0562d26e0df: Porosity has long been considered a property exclusive to solids, yet a new class of materials now combines permanent, well defined pores with the ability to flow. nb499b9db648a: A diffusion-limited topotactic exchange strategy transforms vertically aligned imine-linked covalent organic framework membranes into gradient-encoded frameworks across multiple linkage chemistries while preserving crystallinity and channel orientation. n6032b82d1751: Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of tryptamines has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing chiral pyrroloindoline frameworks, which are ubiquitous in bioactive natural products. This catalytic system demonstrates a transformation of alkoxyallenes and offers a metal-free approach to access enantioenriched allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, with significant potential for the synthesis of structurally diverse alkaloids.
n819e845d5be8: The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. nca948f974a8a: A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. Growth rates exceeding 1 µm/min are obtained for crystalline, highly oriented perovskite films with good optical and electronic properties. The perovskite film is integrated into a fully vacuum-deposited p-i-n photovoltaic device, yielding a promising power conversion efficiency of 9.6%.

n42eecee7a9e0: A ferroelectric junction field-effect transistor memory is realized by coupling ferroelectric polarization with a van der Waals p-n heterojunction. na4e19c33972d: Understanding the dynamic interplay between all components in complex electrocatalytic systems is crucial to advancing their performance. ndb93c9e28c4f: The crystal structure of tetralayer graphene can be switched between rhombohedral and Bernal stacking through interlayer sliding controlled by gate voltages. n414658b01773: The widespread use of the term ‘battery’ has caused misunderstandings about what truly defines a battery. na1cf152b01fc: The electrochemical carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) is an attractive anodic alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction, offering a route to lower the energy demand of electrosynthesis while utilizing abundant industrial waste gas. Here, we establish a COOR∥two-electron oxygen reduction reaction paired electrolysis platform for H2O2 and CO32– coproduction using simulated CO-rich steelmaking flue gas. The system sustains bias-free operation for >140 h. Pulsed electrolysis was introduced to alleviate such carbonate buildup and stabilized operation at 100 mA cm–2. Techno-economic analysis estimated an H2O2 minimum selling price of $0.71 kg–1. Together, these results establish COOR as a practical strategy for energy-efficient electrosynthesis using industrial waste gas.
na2ef69e2788a: Integrating dry carbon electrodes (CEs) into inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offers a solvent-free, scalable route to low-cost photovoltaics. Consequently, our devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.12% and maintain their initial efficiency after 1000 h of dark N2 storage, establishing metal-polymer interfacial coordination as a viable pathway for robust inverted C-PSCs.
nc8d8f7d0533e: Two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) mixed tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, but uncontrolled crystallization produces excessive low-n phases that impede charge extraction due to a quantum confinement effect. Consequently, inverted tin perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.94% and an open-circuit voltage of 0.91 V, together with improved operational and storage stability. nae349e85fe17: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures.
